inline_images.caption_en: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay (Photo: REUTERS)

news.author: Reuters
news.article_content:
BILL Holdings BILL has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, Inc. TPG, a global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay, Inc. CPAY. The all-cash transaction values BILL at approximately $6 billion, with shareholders set to receive $63.25 per share. The offer represents a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average share price as of Nov. 16, 2026.

Under the agreement, TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm's U.S. and European private equity platform, while Corpay will acquire a minority stake. The partnership brings together TPG's technology investment and business-building experience with Corpay's expertise in payments and spend management. The companies aim to strengthen BILL's financial operations platform and expand its capabilities for small and midsize businesses.

The transaction was unanimously approved by BILL's board and is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The deal has no financing conditions attached. Following completion, BILL will become a privately held company and will no longer trade on a public stock exchange.

BILL's recent financial performance provides further context for the acquisition. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, total revenues increased 13% year over year to $353.8 million, while core revenue grew 14% to $316.4 million. The company served 475,300 businesses and processed $102 billion in payment volume, up 14% year over year. Non-GAAP operating income more than doubled to $136.9 million, reflecting improved operating efficiency.

BILL's integrated platform, growing payment volumes and improving profitability provide a solid foundation for future growth. The TPG-Corpay partnership could provide additional resources and expertise to support product innovation, AI development and long-term growth.

Over the past three months, shares of this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company have gained 29.8% against the industry's decline of 4%.

news.article_content_zh:
BILL Holdings BILL 已签订最终协议，将由全球另类资产管理公司 TPG, Inc. 与 Corpay, Inc. CPAY 合作收购。此次全现金交易对 BILL 的估值约为 60 亿美元，股东将获得每股 63.25 美元的收益。该要约较 BILL 截至 2026 年 11 月 16 日的 60 天成交量加权平均股价溢价 31%。

根据协议，TPG将通过该公司在美国和欧洲的私募股权平台TPG Capital收购BILL的多数股权，而Corpay将收购少数股权。此次合作将TPG的技术投资和业务建设经验与Corpay在支付和支出管理方面的专业知识结合起来。两家公司的目标是加强 BILL 的金融运营平台并扩大其针对中小企业的能力。

该交易获得了 BILL 董事会的一致批准，预计将于 2027 年上半年完成，但须获得股东和监管机构的批准。该交易不附加任何融资条件。完成后，BILL 将成为一家私人控股公司，并且将不再在公开证券交易所进行交易。

BILL 最近的财务业绩为此次收购提供了进一步的背景。 2027 财年第一季度，总收入同比增长 13%，达到 3.538 亿美元，核心收入增长 14%，达到 3.164 亿美元。该公司为 475,300 家企业提供服务，处理支付额 1020 亿美元，同比增长 14%。非 GAAP 运营收入增长了一倍多，达到 1.369 亿美元，反映出运营效率的提高。

BILL的集成平台、不断增长的支付量和不断提高的盈利能力为未来的增长奠定了坚实的基础。 TPG 与 Corpay 的合作伙伴关系可以提供额外的资源和专业知识，以支持产品创新、人工智能开发和长期增长。

在过去的三个月里，这家 Zacks 排名第二（买入）公司的股价上涨了 29.8%，而行业下跌了 4%。

news.title_en: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation (Axios)

inline_images.caption: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton greets Rep. Vince Fong after a House Homeland Security Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 18. Photo: C
inline_images.alt: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton greets Rep. Vince Fong after a House Homeland Security

news.author: Axios
news.article_content:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation to lead the office, Axios has learned.

Why it matters: Clayton, the nation's top intelligence official, will now coordinate cybersecurity policy as outages and reported cyberattacks expose vulnerabilities in America's digital infrastructure.

Catch up quick: President Trump announced Thursday he was tapping Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to replace Sean Cairncross as national cyber director.

What they're saying: "I'm excited to work more with Kirsten, who has the experience and capabilities needed to help America navigate our increasingly complex and powerful digital infrastructure as our next National Cyber Director," Clayton said in a statement to Axios.

The big picture: Two critical national security roles will temporarily fall under one official as President Trump shakes up his cybersecurity team amid the growing threat of AI-powered attacks.

Driving the news: Clayton spent Sunday morning on CNN's "State of the Union," ABC's "This Week" and "Fox News Sunday," explaining recent technology disruptions and national security concerns.

Zoom in: Davies oversees the Pentagon's information technology and cybersecurity strategy, including efforts to modernize aging systems and protect military networks.

Behind the scenes: Clayton has already worked closely with the Office of the National Cyber Director, National Security Council, National Security Agency and other agencies through his AI leadership role, according to the White House official.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次人事合并体现了美国将AI引发的网络防御风险与传统情报工作深度绑定，标志着国家网络安全指挥权正向高机动性的跨部门协调模式转型。将两个核心国安岗位收束于一人之手，旨在通过行政联动提升对AI辅助攻击的响应速度，但长期看可能增加情报与防御决策的战术负载。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The centralization of these roles signals a shift toward integrating AI-driven cyber defense with traditional intelligence, prioritizing rapid policy execution. While this enhances coordination against AI-powered threats, it risks bottlenecking critical security decision-making within a single administrative pipeline.

news.article_content_zh:
Axios 获悉，国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 还将担任代理国家网络总监，而克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 正在等待参议院确认领导该办公室。

快速赶上：特朗普总统周四宣布，他将任命五角大楼首席信息官戴维斯接替肖恩·凯恩克罗斯担任国家网络总监。

克莱顿在给 Axios 的一份声明中表示：“我很高兴能与克尔斯滕进行更多合作，作为我们的下一任国家网络总监，她拥有帮助美国驾驭日益复杂和强大的数字基础设施所需的经验和能力。”

大局：随着人工智能攻击威胁日益严重，特朗普总统重组了他的网络安全团队，两个关键的国家安全职责将暂时由一名官员负责。

推动新闻传播：克莱顿周日上午在 CNN 的《国情咨文》、ABC 的《本周》和《福克斯周日新闻》节目中解释了最近的技术中断和国家安全问题。

放大：戴维斯负责监督五角大楼的信息技术和网络安全战略，包括对老化系统进行现代化改造和保护军事网络的努力。

幕后：据白宫官员称，克莱顿已经通过其人工智能领导角色与国家网络主任办公室、国家安全委员会、国家安全局和其他机构密切合作。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】杰伊·克莱顿（国家情报总监、AI特使）；克里斯汀·戴维斯（国防部首席信息官、候任国家网络主任）在白宫国家安全架构调整：杰伊·克莱顿兼任代理国家网络主任，集中管理国家网络安全战略与AI风险预警
【起因与机理】应对关键数字基础设施受攻击威胁及填补职位过渡期空窗
【核心事实细节】杰伊·克莱顿兼任代理国家网络主任。
【各方立场与态度】应对AI辅助攻击与数字基础设施安全升级。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Jay Clayton (DNI, AI Czar); Kirsten A. Davies (DoD CIO, nominee for NCD): Jay Clayton takes on the role of acting National Cyber Director
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address cyber infrastructure vulnerabilities and bridge the confirmation gap for NCD
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Jay Clayton assumes acting National Cyber Director role.
[Key Position & Outlook] Countering AI-driven cyber threats and infra vulnerabilities.

news.title_en: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird

inline_images.caption_en: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (Source: Wall Street Journal)

news.author: Berber Jin and Maxwell Zeff and Keach Hagey
news.article_content:
Two years before she pulled off the largest public offering of all time, Daniela Amodei gathered everyone at Anthropic in a 16-acre garden on a sweltering fall day near the Santa Cruz mountains.

The AI company now with a market value of roughly $1.18 trillion was at the time still a young startup that Amodei and her big brother, Dario, had co-founded with five friends. It was undergoing a hiring spree and Daniela was worried. So they carted 10-foot-tall bookshelves onto the grass to make reading nooks, played games and made friendship bracelets. As the company’s president, and keeper of its culture, the younger Amodei wanted to deliver a message.

“Keep Anthropic weird,” Daniela told them.

Anthropic embraces being atypical because it believes the artificial intelligence future will be anything but normal. Many co-founders meet in college, or at a first job. This pair met when he was 4 and she was born.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei have defended the artificial intelligence (AI) company's massive infrastructure commitments and reiterated their focus on responsible AI development, saying its record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) will not change its long-term mission.

Speaking to CNBC International ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, the siblings addressed the company's $900 billion AI commitments, its approach to balancing growth with safety, partnerships with major technology companies and its relationship with the US government.

Daniela Amodei described the IPO as a significant milestone but said the company would remain focused on its original objectives.

Addressing questions around Anthropic's substantial AI infrastructure spending, Dario Amodei defended commitments of around $900 billion, arguing that they should be viewed in the context of the company's cash reserves and growing revenue.

Amodei added that Anthropic tries to "err on the low side" when forecasting its computing requirements.

He also acknowledged the challenge of balancing the pace of AI development with safety considerations, describing it as one of the company's central tensions.

"What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way," he said.

On the expectations surrounding Anthropic's public market debut, Amodei said the company was keeping its focus on execution rather than the spotlight.

"We've been calm about it," he said, adding that Anthropic's approach was to "always want to under promise and over deliver".

Daniela Amodei said safety remained central to Anthropic's approach, arguing that the potential benefits of AI must be balanced against the risks associated with the technology.

"The promise is incredible, and the risks are real. And we were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks," she said, adding that the company remained deeply committed to safety.

She also highlighted Anthropic's public benefit structure, saying the company wanted its economic value and broader mission to be embedded in its organisational framework.

On data centre expansion, Daniela said Anthropic would need to listen to local communities and take their concerns into account.

Dario Amodei described Anthropic's relationship with Nvidia as a "long and productive partnership". He also expressed satisfaction with its work with SpaceX amid speculation about whether the company could scale back its use of the Elon Musk-led company's computing capacity.

"We're finding that compute to be high quality. We're enjoying working with SpaceX," he said.

On Anthropic's differences with the US Department of Defense, Daniela Amodei said there were no significant updates but expected the company's relationship with the government to continue.

She said Anthropic had worked closely with the US national security establishment since its founding and remained committed to ensuring that its Claude AI models could help protect the country.

Dario Amodei also said Anthropic hoped to secure an investment-grade credit rating in the future, adding that debt was an instrument the company would like to use at some point.

Anthropic is set for its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after raising more than $81 billion in a record-breaking IPO, surpassing SpaceX's offering in June.

The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday, taking its fully diluted market capitalisation to around $1.5 trillion.

The five-year-old company has seen rapid growth on the back of its Claude AI models and products. According to its prospectus, Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue in the nine months ended September 30, up 1,200% from the same period last year.

Speaking at Nasdaq, Amodei highlighted AI's potential to advance medicine and help cure diseases, while reiterating the importance of responsible development.

"Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," he said.

"If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same," he added.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Anthropic的万亿级投入预示着大模型竞争进入重资产军备竞赛阶段，其“主动降速”策略反映了AI安全治理在资本化后的合规制衡诉求。此举意在通过叙事重塑缓解投资者对回报周期的焦虑，同时利用安全性作为构建企业长期护城河的关键差异化溢价。

news.article_content_zh:
两年前，丹妮拉·阿莫代 (Daniela Amodei) 在圣克鲁斯山脉附近一个闷热的秋日，将 Anthropic 的所有人聚集在一个 16 英亩的花园里，完成了有史以来最大规模的公开募股。

这家目前市值约为 1.18 万亿美元的人工智能公司当时还是一家年轻的初创公司，由 Amodei 和她的哥哥 Dario 以及五个朋友共同创立。该公司正在大肆招聘，丹妮拉很担心。于是，他们把 10 英尺高的书架搬到草地上，作为阅读角，玩游戏，制作友谊手链。作为公司总裁和公司文化的守护者，年轻的阿莫代想要传达一个信息。

“让人类保持奇怪，”丹妮拉告诉他们。

Anthropic 拥抱非典型，因为它相信人工智能的未来绝不会是正常的。许多联合创始人是在大学或第一份工作中认识的。这对夫妇在他四岁时相遇，她出生了。

Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和总裁丹妮拉·阿莫迪 (Daniela Amodei) 为这家人工智能 (AI) 公司的大规模基础设施承诺进行了辩护，并重申他们对负责任的人工智能开发的关注，并表示其创纪录的首次公开募股 (IPO) 不会改变其长期使命。

在 Anthropic 纳斯达克首次亮相之前，兄弟姐妹在接受 CNBC International 采访时谈到了该公司 9000 亿美元的人工智能承诺、平衡增长与安全的方法、与主要科技公司的合作伙伴关系以及与美国政府的关系。

Daniela Amodei 将此次 IPO 描述为一个重要的里程碑，但表示公司将继续专注于其最初的目标。

在回答有关 Anthropic 巨额人工智能基础设施支出的问题时，达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 捍卫了约 9000 亿美元的承诺，认为这些承诺应在公司现金储备和不断增长的收入的背景下看待。

Amodei 补充说，Anthropic 在预测其计算需求时试图“偏低”。

他还承认平衡人工智能开发速度与安全考虑的挑战，并将其描述为公司的核心压力之一。

“我们在节奏方面所做的基本上是说，看，我们可以以每小时 200 英里的速度行驶。也许我们只能以每小时 90 英里的速度行驶。花时间弄清楚如何安全地做到这一点，剩下的剩余时间我们用正确的方式构建模型，”他说。

在谈到对 Anthropic 公开市场首次亮相的预期时，Amodei 表示，该公司将把重点放在执行上，而不是聚光灯下。

“我们对此一直保持冷静，”他说，并补充说 Anthropic 的做法是“总是希望少承诺多兑现”。

Daniela Amodei 表示，安全仍然是 Anthropic 方法的核心，她认为人工智能的潜在好处必须与该技术相关的风险相平衡。

【起因与机理】应对资本市场对其高昂资本开支及商业化压力的质疑

【行业影响与走向】行业影响：该高额资本开支将持续推高行业进入门槛，重塑大模型初创企业的资本运作范式。

news.article_content:
Two years before she pulled off the largest public offering of all time, Daniela Amodei gathered everyone at Anthropic in a 16-acre garden on a sweltering fall day near the Santa Cruz mountains.

The AI company now with a market value of roughly $1.18 trillion was at the time still a young startup that Amodei and her big brother, Dario, had co-founded with five friends. It was undergoing a hiring spree and Daniela was worried. So they carted 10-foot-tall bookshelves onto the grass to make reading nooks, played games and made friendship bracelets. As the company’s president, and keeper of its culture, the younger Amodei wanted to deliver a message.

“Keep Anthropic weird,” Daniela told them.

Anthropic embraces being atypical because it believes the artificial intelligence future will be anything but normal. Many co-founders meet in college, or at a first job. This pair met when he was 4 and she was born.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei have defended the artificial intelligence (AI) company's massive infrastructure commitments and reiterated their focus on responsible AI development, saying its record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) will not change its long-term mission.

Speaking to CNBC International ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, the siblings addressed the company's $900 billion AI commitments, its approach to balancing growth with safety, partnerships with major technology companies and its relationship with the US government.

Daniela Amodei described the IPO as a significant milestone but said the company would remain focused on its original objectives.

Addressing questions around Anthropic's substantial AI infrastructure spending, Dario Amodei defended commitments of around $900 billion, arguing that they should be viewed in the context of the company's cash reserves and growing revenue.

Amodei added that Anthropic tries to "err on the low side" when forecasting its computing requirements.

He also acknowledged the challenge of balancing the pace of AI development with safety considerations, describing it as one of the company's central tensions.

"What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way," he said.

On the expectations surrounding Anthropic's public market debut, Amodei said the company was keeping its focus on execution rather than the spotlight.

"We've been calm about it," he said, adding that Anthropic's approach was to "always want to under promise and over deliver".

Daniela Amodei said safety remained central to Anthropic's approach, arguing that the potential benefits of AI must be balanced against the risks associated with the technology.

"The promise is incredible, and the risks are real. And we were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks," she said, adding that the company remained deeply committed to safety.

She also highlighted Anthropic's public benefit structure, saying the company wanted its economic value and broader mission to be embedded in its organisational framework.

On data centre expansion, Daniela said Anthropic would need to listen to local communities and take their concerns into account.

Dario Amodei described Anthropic's relationship with Nvidia as a "long and productive partnership". He also expressed satisfaction with its work with SpaceX amid speculation about whether the company could scale back its use of the Elon Musk-led company's computing capacity.

"We're finding that compute to be high quality. We're enjoying working with SpaceX," he said.

On Anthropic's differences with the US Department of Defense, Daniela Amodei said there were no significant updates but expected the company's relationship with the government to continue.

She said Anthropic had worked closely with the US national security establishment since its founding and remained committed to ensuring that its Claude AI models could help protect the country.

Dario Amodei also said Anthropic hoped to secure an investment-grade credit rating in the future, adding that debt was an instrument the company would like to use at some point.

Anthropic is set for its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after raising more than $81 billion in a record-breaking IPO, surpassing SpaceX's offering in June.

The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday, taking its fully diluted market capitalisation to around $1.5 trillion.

The five-year-old company has seen rapid growth on the back of its Claude AI models and products. According to its prospectus, Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue in the nine months ended September 30, up 1,200% from the same period last year.

Speaking at Nasdaq, Amodei highlighted AI's potential to advance medicine and help cure diseases, while reiterating the importance of responsible development.

"Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," he said.

"If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same," he added.

news.article_content_zh:
两年前，丹妮拉·阿莫代 (Daniela Amodei) 在圣克鲁斯山脉附近一个闷热的秋日，将 Anthropic 的所有人聚集在一个 16 英亩的花园里，完成了有史以来最大规模的公开募股。

这家目前市值约为 1.18 万亿美元的人工智能公司当时还是一家年轻的初创公司，由 Amodei 和她的哥哥 Dario 以及五个朋友共同创立。该公司正在大肆招聘，丹妮拉很担心。于是，他们把 10 英尺高的书架搬到草地上，作为阅读角，玩游戏，制作友谊手链。作为公司总裁和公司文化的守护者，年轻的阿莫代想要传达一个信息。

“让人类保持奇怪，”丹妮拉告诉他们。

Anthropic 拥抱非典型，因为它相信人工智能的未来绝不会是正常的。许多联合创始人是在大学或第一份工作中认识的。这对夫妇在他四岁时相遇，她出生了。

Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和总裁丹妮拉·阿莫迪 (Daniela Amodei) 为这家人工智能 (AI) 公司的大规模基础设施承诺进行了辩护，并重申他们对负责任的人工智能开发的关注，并表示其创纪录的首次公开募股 (IPO) 不会改变其长期使命。

在 Anthropic 纳斯达克首次亮相之前，兄弟姐妹在接受 CNBC International 采访时谈到了该公司 9000 亿美元的人工智能承诺、平衡增长与安全的方法、与主要科技公司的合作伙伴关系以及与美国政府的关系。

Daniela Amodei 将此次 IPO 描述为一个重要的里程碑，但表示公司将继续专注于其最初的目标。

在回答有关 Anthropic 巨额人工智能基础设施支出的问题时，达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 捍卫了约 9000 亿美元的承诺，认为这些承诺应在公司现金储备和不断增长的收入的背景下看待。

Amodei 补充说，Anthropic 在预测其计算需求时试图“偏低”。

他还承认平衡人工智能开发速度与安全考虑的挑战，并将其描述为公司的核心压力之一。

“我们在节奏方面所做的基本上是说，看，我们可以以每小时 200 英里的速度行驶。也许我们只能以每小时 90 英里的速度行驶。花时间弄清楚如何安全地做到这一点，剩下的剩余时间我们用正确的方式构建模型，”他说。

在谈到对 Anthropic 公开市场首次亮相的预期时，Amodei 表示，该公司将把重点放在执行上，而不是聚光灯下。

“我们对此一直保持冷静，”他说，并补充说 Anthropic 的做法是“总是希望少承诺多兑现”。

Daniela Amodei 表示，安全仍然是 Anthropic 方法的核心，她认为人工智能的潜在好处必须与该技术相关的风险相平衡。

news.title: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
news.title_en: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair

inline_images.caption: Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia this month after reports surfaced involving affairs with two women. (Eric Lee for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia this month after reports surfaced involving affairs with two women.

inline_images.caption: Mr. Huang with President Trump in Washington in early October. Nvidia’s board has rejected the president’s suggestion that it reinstate Mr. Huang as the head of the company. (Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Mr. Huang with President Trump in Washington in early October. Nvidia’s board has rejected the president’s suggestion that it reinstate Mr. Huang as the head of the company.

news.author: Jonathan Swan, Julian E. Barnes, and Maggie Haberman
news.article_content:
The Chinese woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

The woman, Alice Huang, was in touch with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the people with knowledge of the intelligence said. That period overlaps with at least a portion of the time she was in a relationship with Mr. Huang, then the head of the world’s leading maker of advanced artificial intelligence chips.

U.S. intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that Ms. Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, the people said.

The extent and specific timing of Ms. Huang’s contacts with the spy agency — and Mr. Kang’s work for the same intelligence service — have not been previously reported.

Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency last year and up through recent months help to flesh out how U.S. officials came to believe that Mr. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, was the target of an intelligence operation.

They correspond not just to the time when he was conducting the affair but also to at least part of the period when Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which went to data centers in Southeast Asia serving Chinese technology companies like Alibaba and some of which are suspected of being smuggled to China.

Allies of the former Nvidia chief, including President Trump, have sought to minimize the scandal and questioned whether Ms. Huang was spying for Chinese intelligence. But the newly revealed information underscores the continuous contacts that she had with the Ministry of State Security, even as she was in a romantic relationship with Mr. Huang.

It also helps to flesh out why some American officials have been worried that Ms. Huang’s role is just one element of a much broader push by China in that technological battle. The Ministry of State Security has prioritized focusing on acquiring high-end chips and advancing China’s A.I. ambitions.

U.S. officials are investigating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed, that have been linked to the possible smuggling of Nvidia chips to China, to evade U.S. export control laws. U.S. officials are still working to determine the full extent and duration of their work with Chinese intelligence.

The intelligence gathered by the U.S. contains evidence — including shipping records — demonstrating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in that network of companies, people with knowledge of the intelligence reports said. The New York Times has previously reported that Ms. Huang and her family have a web of connections to Chinese defense contractors.

Mr. Huang initially described his relationship with Ms. Huang as normal interactions with a business customer. He acknowledged an affair only after The Times revealed last month that Ms. Huang had been identified by the United States as a Chinese intelligence asset and that the Nvidia chief had been picked up on electronic surveillance targeting her.

He stepped down this month after The Times subsequently reported that he had an affair with a subordinate at Nvidia. Administration officials never provided him with a so-called defensive briefing about Ms. Huang, a heads-up that the woman he was in a relationship with had been linked to Chinese intelligence.

A spokesman for Mr. Huang declined to comment. The White House, the State Department, the Chinese Embassy in Washington, Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang did not respond to requests for comment on Sunday.

Before the scandal broke into public view, advisers to Mr. Trump told him on at least two occasions that U.S. intelligence had uncovered Ms. Huang’s links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Mr. Huang while he was still running Nvidia, according to U.S. officials with direct knowledge of the briefings.

Both times, including when his national security adviser discussed it with him, the president downplayed the concerns and made clear he did not want to intervene in the matter. The officials said Mr. Trump regarded Mr. Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market. Mr. Trump has recently suggested that Nvidia should consider bringing Mr. Huang back as chief executive, a possibility the company’s board has rejected.

“We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them,” the president said at a White House news conference on Friday. “I think the company if they were smart they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work.”

Mr. Trump has claimed that no one in his government told him of any intelligence indicating that Ms. Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset.

“I don’t know that she is a spy,” he said. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy.”

In fact, his administration has been monitoring Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency for more than a year, a period when the Ministry of State Security has been intensifying its new role in seeking to give China an advantage in artificial intelligence.

“This network of companies working to procure and smuggle Nvidia chips lines up precisely with the M.S.S.’s recently stated core mission of circumventing and undermining U.S. export controls on semiconductors and other key technologies,” said Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Mr. Trump’s first term, and who is chief executive of the open-source research firm Garnaut Global.

The Ministry of State Security has for decades declared that its mission is to combat espionage and to eliminate political threats to Communist Party rule in China. The minister of state security, Chen Yixin, gave a similar five-point statement as recently as late last year. Then in April, he unveiled a new, sixth mission — overcoming the “blockades” choking China’s access to key technologies like artificial intelligence.

“Deepen the struggle against blockades, and comprehensively advance artificial intelligence innovation, industry development and applications,” Mr. Chen wrote in a party journal. “Focus on tackling the ‘choke holds’ of critical technologies.”

“To assume the M.S.S. wasn’t at the center of this operation would be to assume that they are incompetent,” Mr. Pottinger added. “That’s not an assumption I would make.”

American spy agencies are still working to understand the role played by Mr. Kang, the business partner of Ms. Huang, whom she would introduce to associates as her husband. Multiple people with knowledge of the intelligence said the United States had collected evidence that Mr. Kang worked with the Ministry of State Security.

Ms. Huang also appears to have met with officials of China’s Ministry of Public Security, the nation’s main law enforcement agency, according to multiple people with knowledge of the U.S. intelligence reports.

Ms. Huang, Mr. Kang, Ms. Huang’s sister and companies associated with them have emerged as a significant branch of the Chinese effort to build data centers and acquire access to Nvidia chips to train powerful A.I. models. Ms. Huang’s network has been linked to efforts to supply the powerful chips to Chinese-state owned military contractors doing work for the People’s Liberation Army.

Little of the intelligence about Ms. Huang and her network has been provided to Capitol Hill, but lawmakers from both parties are demanding briefings.

A briefing this month for top lawmakers by John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, and Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, was originally scheduled to discuss Iran, but The Times’s reporting on Nvidia led the lawmakers to ask questions about Mr. Huang and Alice Huang. Their answers raised more questions and left some lawmakers puzzled.

Trump administration officials postponed a follow-up briefing for top national security staffers scheduled for last Wednesday, in which senior officials were set to share details of the intelligence collected on Ms. Huang.

The intelligence about Ms. Huang was closely held inside the government until The Times reported the existence of the information in late October. Behind the scenes, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also the national security adviser, had written a confidential memo, dated March 30 this year, laying out Ms. Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence.

“This network of companies working to procure and smuggle Nvidia chips lines up precisely with the M.S.S.’s recently stated core mission of circumventing and undermining U.S. export controls on semiconductors and other key technologies,” said Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Mr. Trump’s first term, and who is chief executive of the open-source research firm Garnaut Global.

The Ministry of State Security has for decades declared that its mission is to combat espionage and to eliminate political threats to Communist Party rule in China. The minister of state security, Chen Yixin, gave a similar five-point statement as recently as late last year. Then in April, he unveiled a new, sixth mission — overcoming the “blockades” choking China’s access to key technologies like artificial intelligence.

“Deepen the struggle against blockades, and comprehensively advance artificial intelligence innovation, industry development and applications,” Mr. Chen wrote in a party journal. “Focus on tackling the ‘choke holds’ of critical technologies.”

“To assume the M.S.S. wasn’t at the center of this operation would be to assume that they are incompetent,” Mr. Pottinger added. “That’s not an assumption I would make.”

American spy agencies are still working to understand the role played by Mr. Kang, the business partner of Ms. Huang, whom she would introduce to associates as her husband. Multiple people with knowledge of the intelligence said the United States had collected evidence that Mr. Kang worked with the Ministry of State Security.

Ms. Huang also appears to have met with officials of China’s Ministry of Public Security, the nation’s main law enforcement agency, according to multiple people with knowledge of the U.S. intelligence reports.

Ms. Huang, Mr. Kang, Ms. Huang’s sister and companies associated with them have emerged as a significant branch of the Chinese effort to build data centers and acquire access to Nvidia chips to train powerful A.I. models. Ms. Huang’s network has been linked to efforts to supply the powerful chips to Chinese-state owned military contractors doing work for the People’s Liberation Army.

Little of the intelligence about Ms. Huang and her network has been provided to Capitol Hill, but lawmakers from both parties are demanding briefings.

A briefing this month for top lawmakers by John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, and Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, was originally scheduled to discuss Iran, but The Times’s reporting on Nvidia led the lawmakers to ask questions about Mr. Huang and Alice Huang. Their answers raised more questions and left some lawmakers puzzled.

Trump administration officials postponed a follow-up briefing for top national security staffers scheduled for last Wednesday, in which senior officials were set to share details of the intelligence collected on Ms. Huang.

The intelligence about Ms. Huang was closely held inside the government until The Times reported the existence of the information in late October. Behind the scenes, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also the national security adviser, had written a confidential memo, dated March 30 this year, laying out Ms. Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence.
paragraphs: The Chinese woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

The woman, Alice Huang, was in touch with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the people with knowledge of the intelligence said. That period overlaps with at least a portion of the time she was in a relationship with Mr. Huang, then the head of the world’s leading maker of advanced artificial intelligence chips.
U.S. intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that Ms. Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, the people said.
The extent and specific timing of Ms. Huang’s contacts with the spy agency — and Mr. Kang’s work for the same intelligence service — have not been previously reported.

Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency last year and up through recent months help to flesh out how U.S. officials came to believe that Mr. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, was the target of an intelligence operation.

They correspond not just to the time when he was conducting the affair but also to at least part of the period when Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which went to data centers in Southeast Asia serving Chinese technology companies like Alibaba and some of which are suspected of being smuggled to China.

Allies of the former Nvidia chief, including President Trump, have sought to minimize the scandal and questioned whether Ms. Huang was spying for Chinese intelligence. But the newly revealed information underscores the continuous contacts that she had with the Ministry of State Security, even as she was in a romantic relationship with Mr. Huang.

It also helps to flesh out why some American officials have been worried that Ms. Huang’s role is just one element of a much broader push by China in that technological battle. The Ministry of State Security has prioritized focusing on acquiring high-end chips and advancing China’s A.I. ambitions.

U.S. officials are investigating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed, that have been linked to the possible smuggling of Nvidia chips to China, to evade U.S. export control laws. U.S. officials are still working to determine the full extent and duration of their work with Chinese intelligence.

The intelligence gathered by the U.S. contains evidence — including shipping records — demonstrating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in that network of companies, people with knowledge of the intelligence reports said. The New York Times has previously reported that Ms. Huang and her family have a web of connections to Chinese defense contractors.

news.summary_zh: 美情报机构证实，英伟达前CEO黄仁勋绯闻对象爱丽丝·黄在恋爱期间与中国国安部门保持密切联系，并涉及高阶芯片走私网络

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国情报报告显示，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的绯闻对象爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）在2025年春季至2024年秋季期间，长期与中国国家安全部人员保持联系。调查指出，爱丽丝·黄及其商业伙伴康伟（Kang Wei）利用其控股的Megaspeed公司，构建了复杂的供应链网络，不仅将先进英伟达芯片分销至东南亚数据中心，更涉及向中国境内非法转移管控级别的高性能计算芯片。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: U.S. intelligence reports reveal that Alice Huang, a central figure in the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, maintained consistent contact with Chinese Ministry of State Security officers from spring 2025 through autumn 2024. Investigations indicate that she and her business associate, Kang Wei, utilized their company, Megaspeed, to create a supply chain network that diverted advanced Nvidia chips to Southeast Asian data centers and potentially smuggled restricted hardware into China.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件标志着美国对半导体供应链的审查已从单纯的财务合规深入至私人关系与情报层面的穿透性调查。英伟达前CEO的私生活不仅引发企业管治危机，更直接暴露了先进算力出口管制体系中的‘灰色转运’漏洞，预计美国商务部将针对东南亚区域算力节点实施更为严苛的终端用户审查。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident signifies a shift in U.S. semiconductor supply chain oversight from financial compliance to deep-tissue intelligence and personnel security investigations. The exposure of these 'gray-market' diversion channels will likely prompt the U.S. Department of Commerce to enforce significantly more stringent end-user verification protocols for AI compute clusters deployed in Southeast Asia.

news.article_content_zh:
据多位了解美国情报报告的人士透露，这位英伟达丑闻核心的中国女性在与黄仁勋进行秘密恋情期间，与中国最高间谍机构的一名官员保持了一年多的联系。

知情人士称，这名女子名叫 Alice Huang，从 2025 年春季到今年秋季一直与中国国家安全部的一名官员保持联系。那段时期至少有一部分时间与她与时任全球领先先进人工智能芯片制造商负责人的黄先生交往的时间重叠。

知情人士称，美国情报机构还收集了黄女士的商业伙伴康伟（经常被介绍为黄女士的丈夫）与同一家中国间谍机构合作的证据。

黄女士与该间谍机构接触的程度和具体时间以及康先生为同一情报机构工作的情况此前并未报道过。

黄女士去年和最近几个月与中国间谍机构的接触有助于充实美国官员如何相信本月早些时候辞去英伟达首席执行官职务的黄先生是情报行动的目标。

它们不仅与他进行这起事件的时间相符，而且至少与黄女士的公司 Megaspeed 收购大量先进的英伟达芯片的时期相符，其中一些芯片被运往东南亚的数据中心，为阿里巴巴等中国科技公司提供服务，其中一些芯片涉嫌走私到中国。

包括特朗普总统在内的英伟达前首席执行官的盟友一直试图将丑闻最小化，并质疑黄女士是否在为中国情报部门进行间谍活动。但新披露的信息突显了她与国家安全部的持续接触，尽管她与黄先生处于恋爱关系。

这也有助于解释为什么一些美国官员一直担心黄女士的角色只是中国在这场技术战中更广泛推动的一个因素。国家安全部优先关注高端芯片和推进中国人工智能发展。野心。

美国官员正在调查黄女士和康先生在包括 Megaspeed 在内的东南亚公司网络中所扮演的角色，这些公司可能与将英伟达芯片走私到中国有关，以逃避美国出口管制法。美国官员仍在努力确定他们与中国情报部门合作的全部范围和持续时间。

了解情报的人士称，美国收集的情报包含的证据（包括运输记录）证明了黄女士和康先生在该公司网络中的作用。 《纽约时报》此前曾报道称，黄女士及其家人与中国国防承包商有着广泛的关系网。

黄先生最初将他与黄女士的关系描述为与商业客户的正常互动。上个月，《泰晤士报》披露黄女士已被美国认定为中国情报人员，并且英伟达首席执行官因针对她的电子监控而被捕后，他才承认了这一事件。

在《泰晤士报》随后报道他与英伟达的一名下属有染后，他于本月辞职。政府官员从未向他提供过有关黄女士的所谓防御性简报，即与他有关系的那位女士与中国情报部门有联系。

黄先生的发言人拒绝置评。白宫、国务院、中国驻华盛顿大使馆、黄女士和康先生周日没有回应置评请求。

据直接了解简报的美国官员透露，在丑闻进入公众视野之前，特朗普的顾问至少两次告诉他，美国情报部门已经发现了黄女士与中国间谍机构的联系，并且在黄先生仍在管理英伟达期间，她与黄先生关系密切。

news.title: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future
news.title_en: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future

inline_images.alt: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future

news.author: Nitasha Tiku
news.article_content:
SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters.

Anthropic had invited more than a dozen academics, think tank fellows and media figures for briefings from senior staff on how society should navigate the rise of powerful AI. Guests were asked to first read an essay by Amodei that argued that AI was advancing dangerously fast, and the 23,000-word “constitution” that guides his company’s chatbot with statements like “Claude should not even tell white lies.”

In a 10th floor conference room down the hall from a built-in barista bar, attendees recalled, Anthropic staff described how AI was increasingly able to improve itself and that teaching machines morals might stop them from becoming harmful. “They feel it’s going to be a transformative event for humanity and society needs to be prepared,” said New York University economist Arpit Gupta, who joined the two-day program. “I got the sense that they’re not happy with the public discourse” about AI, he said, and want to change it.

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

Gupta and fellow guests received a crash course in the view from inside Anthropic, a company that Amodei has constructed around his vision that AI will soon accelerate beyond human intelligence and his beliefs about how to build it safely.

The company launched on the stock market Thursday, ending the week with a valuation of more than $1.5 trillion that transformed Amodei and his co-founders into deca-billionaires. He propelled Anthropic to the front of the AI race, reshaping the U.S. economy this year by winning over business clients to its technology — and through a unique corporate culture that attempts to reconcile the conflict between chasing profits and doing what’s best for society.

Amodei, a cerebral presence who doesn’t project the naked ambition of an archetypal Silicon Valley founder, leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as “Dario Vision Quests,” expounding on the company’s thinking around AI development, geopolitics and more while inviting employees to discuss and debate. The CEO’s output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China’s AI development, and Claude might be conscious.

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world’s most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company’s ethos, including several current and former employees.

At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what’s best for the world. “It’s kind of [a] Manhattan Project-style, crazy, fun place, if you think it’s going to work out well,” said former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon, publicly resigned in September, warning that Anthropic felt locked into an AI race that risked human extinction.

“A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We’re going to put on our capes and we’re going to be the responsible ones, and we’re going to accrue great power, but … because we’re doing it responsibly, it’s responsible to acquire more power,” said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.

Anthropic’s leaders tightly control the details of the company’s internal debates through a zero-tolerance policy on leaks and strong social norms enforcing confidentiality, former employees said.

Anthropic launched an internal investigation last year after Wired reported that Amodei had acknowledged in a Slack message that accepting funding from Middle East states was likely to “enrich dictators,” said the former employee who left this year. The leaker was fired, the employee said, an incident that has not been previously reported. Details from Amodei’s copious Slack memos appear to have leaked only once more since.

Anthropic declined to comment.

The company suggested in its IPO prospectus that Anthropic’s revenue could reach about the size of the entire U.S. economy. Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states.

After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society’s leaders to make difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created. “The moment the whole company was preparing for the whole time is now approaching,” an early Anthropic employee said.

Amodei was convinced of his vision long before he became a CEO with a flock to tend. After joining OpenAI as vice president of research in 2016, he used a laptop and printer kept physically disconnected — or “air gapped” — from the internet to work on essays about how to build more powerful AI, said Geoffrey Irving, who worked closely with Amodei in OpenAI’s research department.

“Dario was paranoid about some of the stuff being an ‘infohazard,’” said Irving, containing ideas that could lead to immense harm if they fell into the wrong hands — like the recipe for a nuclear bomb. Amodei also purchased air-gapped laptops for a couple of other employees, including Irving, he said.

Amodei’s writings on how to build more powerful AI caught on fast with other researchers at OpenAI. He has said in public remarks that he left because he lost trust that the company would handle disagreements over how to develop AI in good faith. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (The Washington Post has a content partnership with OpenAI.)

He set out to create a more safety-conscious culture when he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six people from his inner circle, most of them from OpenAI.

In an internal memo the following year, Amodei laid out the stakes. “The current trajectory of AI development makes me think that there’s a 20 to 30 percent chance that AGI will lead to the destruction or permanent stunting of humanity,” he wrote, referring to the concept of artificial general intelligence, previously unreported court records show. He added that truly capable AI “seems more powerful/dangerous than nuclear weapons.”

Amodei was careful about those he hired to work on that existential challenge. Recruits were screened with a “culture interview,” even for back office and policy roles, according to former employees and an archived copy of the company’s careers page.

SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters.

Anthropic had invited more than a dozen academics, think tank fellows and media figures for briefings from senior staff on how society should navigate the rise of powerful AI. Guests were asked to first read an essay by Amodei that argued that AI was advancing dangerously fast, and the 23,000-word “constitution” that guides his company’s chatbot with statements like “Claude should not even tell white lies.”

In a 10th floor conference room down the hall from a built-in barista bar, attendees recalled, Anthropic staff described how AI was increasingly able to improve itself and that teaching machines morals might stop them from becoming harmful. “They feel it’s going to be a transformative event for humanity and society needs to be prepared,” said New York University economist Arpit Gupta, who joined the two-day program. “I got the sense that they’re not happy with the public discourse” about AI, he said, and want to change it.

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

Gupta and fellow guests received a crash course in the view from inside Anthropic, a company that Amodei has constructed around his vision that AI will soon accelerate beyond human intelligence and his beliefs about how to build it safely.

The company launched on the stock market Thursday, ending the week with a valuation of more than $1.5 trillion that transformed Amodei and his co-founders into deca-billionaires. He propelled Anthropic to the front of the AI race, reshaping the U.S. economy this year by winning over business clients to its technology — and through a unique corporate culture that attempts to reconcile the conflict between chasing profits and doing what’s best for society.

Amodei, a cerebral presence who doesn’t project the naked ambition of an archetypal Silicon Valley founder, leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as “Dario Vision Quests,” expounding on the company’s thinking around AI development, geopolitics and more while inviting employees to discuss and debate. The CEO’s output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China’s AI development, and Claude might be conscious.

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world’s most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company’s ethos, including several current and former employees.

At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what’s best for the world. “It’s kind of [a] Manhattan Project-style, crazy, fun place, if you think it’s going to work out well,” said former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon, publicly resigned in September, warning that Anthropic felt locked into an AI race that risked human extinction.

“A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We’re going to put on our capes and we’re going to be the responsible ones, and we’re going to accrue great power, but … because we’re doing it responsibly, it’s responsible to acquire more power,” said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.

Anthropic’s leaders tightly control the details of the company’s internal debates through a zero-tolerance policy on leaks and strong social norms enforcing confidentiality, former employees said.

Anthropic launched an internal investigation last year after Wired reported that Amodei had acknowledged in a Slack message that accepting funding from Middle East states was likely to “enrich dictators,” said the former employee who left this year. The leaker was fired, the employee said, an incident that has not been previously reported. Details from Amodei’s copious Slack memos appear to have leaked only once more since.

Anthropic declined to comment.

The company suggested in its IPO prospectus that Anthropic’s revenue could reach about the size of the entire U.S. economy. Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states.

After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society’s leaders to make difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created. “The moment the whole company was preparing for the whole time is now approaching,” an early Anthropic employee said.

Amodei was convinced of his vision long before he became a CEO with a flock to tend. After joining OpenAI as vice president of research in 2016, he used a laptop and printer kept physically disconnected — or “air gapped” — from the internet to work on essays about how to build more powerful AI, said Geoffrey Irving, who worked closely with Amodei in OpenAI’s research department.

Amodei’s writings on how to build more powerful AI caught on fast with other researchers at OpenAI. news.article_content_zh:
旧金山——上个月，当 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 向投资者介绍其人工智能公司的未来产品计划时，公司总部其他地方举行了一场截然不同的会议。

Anthropic 邀请了十几位学者、智库研究员和媒体人士，听取高级人员的简报，介绍社会应如何应对强大人工智能的崛起。客人被要求首先阅读 Amodei 的一篇文章，该文章认为人工智能正在以危险的速度快速发展，以及指导其公司聊天机器人的 23,000 字“宪法”，其中包括“克劳德甚至不应该说善意的谎言”等声明。

与会者回忆道，在 10 楼的一间会议室里，大厅里有一家内置咖啡吧，Anthropic 的工作人员描述了人工智能如何越来越能够自我改进，并且教导机器道德可能会阻止它们变得有害。 “他们认为这将是人类的一场变革性事件，社会需要做好准备，”参加为期两天的项目的纽约大学经济学家阿皮特·古普塔 (Arpit Gupta) 说。他说，“我感觉到他们对关于人工智能的公众讨论并不满意”，并且想要改变它。

有关气候、科学和技术的新闻和指南。免费注册

古普塔和其他嘉宾接受了 Anthropic 内部观点的速成课程，这家公司是 Amodei 围绕人工智能将很快超越人类智能的愿景以及他对如何安全构建人工智能的信念而建立的。

该公司周四在股票市场上市，本周结束时估值超过 1.5 万亿美元，使阿莫迪和他的联合创始人成为十亿万富翁。他将 Anthropic 推向了人工智能竞赛的前沿，通过其技术赢得了商业客户，并通过独特的企业文化试图调和追逐利润与为社会做最好的事情之间的冲突，从而重塑了今年的美国经济。

阿莫代是一个头脑清醒的人，不会表现出典型硅谷创始人赤裸裸的野心，他带领他的员工通过文章、Slack 上发布的长备忘录以及每月两次的全体员工会谈（戏称“达里奥愿景探索”）阐述公司对人工智能开发、地缘政治等方面的思考，同时邀请员工进行讨论和辩论。这位首席执行官的成果在公司内部建立了一系列被视为显而易见、紧迫和正义的信念：人工智能取代人类是不可避免的，美国必须限制中国的人工智能发展，克劳德可能是有意识的。

根据对十多名熟悉该公司精神的人士（其中包括几位现任和前任员工）的采访，在这种紧密结合的文化中，自称“蚂蚁”的 Anthropic 员工感觉自己正在与最聪明的人一起解决世界上最紧迫的问题，肩负着保护人类的共同使命。

其核心是相信 Anthropic 和 Amodei 知道什么对世界最有利。 Anthropic 前员工雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 于 9 月份公开辞职，他表示：“如果你认为它会取得很好的效果，这就是曼哈顿计划式的、疯狂、有趣的地方。”他警告说，Anthropic 感觉自己陷入了一场可能导致人类灭绝的人工智能竞赛。

“Anthropic 普遍存在的一件事是：我们将披上斗篷，我们将成为负责任的人，我们将积累巨大的权力，但是……因为我们负责任地行事，所以有责任获得更多权力，”今年离开公司的一名前员工表示，与其他人一样，他要求匿名，以避免遭到公司报复。

前员工表示，Anthropic 的领导层通过对泄密的零容忍政策和强制保密的严格社会规范，严格控制公司内部辩论的细节。

去年，《连线》报道称，阿莫迪在 Slack 消息中承认，接受中东国家的资金可能会“让独裁者致富”，今年离职的前员工表示，去年，Anthropic 发起了一项内部调查。该员工表示，泄密者已被解雇，此前尚未报道过这一事件。自那以后，阿莫迪大量的 Slack 备忘录中的细节似乎只被泄露了一次。

人类拒绝发表评论。

该公司在 IPO 招股说明书中表示，Anthropic 的收入可能达到整个美国经济的规模。知情人士称，该公司向投资者传达的信息与阿莫迪经常为员工勾画的未来愿景相符，即人工智能公司拥有民族国家的力量。

SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters.

Anthropic had invited more than a dozen academics, think tank fellows and media figures for briefings from senior staff on how society should navigate the rise of powerful AI. Guests were asked to first read an essay by Amodei that argued that AI was advancing dangerously fast, and the 23,000-word “constitution” that guides his company’s chatbot with statements like “Claude should not even tell white lies.”

In a 10th floor conference room down the hall from a built-in barista bar, attendees recalled, Anthropic staff described how AI was increasingly able to improve itself and that teaching machines morals might stop them from becoming harmful. “They feel it’s going to be a transformative event for humanity and society needs to be prepared,” said New York University economist Arpit Gupta, who joined the two-day program. “I got the sense that they’re not happy with the public discourse” about AI, he said, and want to change it.

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

Gupta and fellow guests received a crash course in the view from inside Anthropic, a company that Amodei has constructed around his vision that AI will soon accelerate beyond human intelligence and his beliefs about how to build it safely.

The company launched on the stock market Thursday, ending the week with a valuation of more than $1.5 trillion that transformed Amodei and his co-founders into deca-billionaires. He propelled Anthropic to the front of the AI race, reshaping the U.S. economy this year by winning over business clients to its technology — and through a unique corporate culture that attempts to reconcile the conflict between chasing profits and doing what’s best for society.

Amodei, a cerebral presence who doesn’t project the naked ambition of an archetypal Silicon Valley founder, leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as “Dario Vision Quests,” expounding on the company’s thinking around AI development, geopolitics and more while inviting employees to discuss and debate. The CEO’s output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China’s AI development, and Claude might be conscious.

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world’s most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company’s ethos, including several current and former employees.

At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what’s best for the world. “It’s kind of [a] Manhattan Project-style, crazy, fun place, if you think it’s going to work out well,” said former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon, publicly resigned in September, warning that Anthropic felt locked into an AI race that risked human extinction.

“A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We’re going to put on our capes and we’re going to be the responsible ones, and we’re going to accrue great power, but … because we’re doing it responsibly, it’s responsible to acquire more power,” said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.

Anthropic’s leaders tightly control the details of the company’s internal debates through a zero-tolerance policy on leaks and strong social norms enforcing confidentiality, former employees said.

Anthropic launched an internal investigation last year after Wired reported that Amodei had acknowledged in a Slack message that accepting funding from Middle East states was likely to “enrich dictators,” said the former employee who left this year. The leaker was fired, the employee said, an incident that has not been previously reported. Details from Amodei’s copious Slack memos appear to have leaked only once more since.

Anthropic declined to comment.

The company suggested in its IPO prospectus that Anthropic’s revenue could reach about the size of the entire U.S. economy. Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states.

After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society’s leaders to make difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created. “The moment the whole company was preparing for the whole time is now approaching,” an early Anthropic employee said.

Amodei was convinced of his vision long before he became a CEO with a flock to tend. After joining OpenAI as vice president of research in 2016, he used a laptop and printer kept physically disconnected — or “air gapped” — from the internet to work on essays about how to build more powerful AI, said Geoffrey Irving, who worked closely with Amodei in OpenAI’s research department.

“Dario was paranoid about some of the stuff being an ‘infohazard,’” said Irving, containing ideas that could lead to immense harm if they fell into the wrong hands — like the recipe for a nuclear bomb. Amodei also purchased air-gapped laptops for a couple of other employees, including Irving, he said.

Amodei’s writings on how to build more powerful AI caught on fast with other researchers at OpenAI. He has said in public remarks that he left because he lost trust that the company would handle disagreements over how to develop AI in good faith. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (The Washington Post has a content partnership with OpenAI.)

He set out to create a more safety-conscious culture when he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six people from his inner circle, most of them from OpenAI.

In an internal memo the following year, Amodei laid out the stakes. “The current trajectory of AI development makes me think that there’s a 20 to 30 percent chance that AGI will lead to the destruction or permanent stunting of humanity,” he wrote, referring to the concept of artificial general intelligence, previously unreported court records show. He added that truly capable AI “seems more powerful/dangerous than nuclear weapons.”

Amodei was careful about those he hired to work on that existential challenge. Recruits were screened with a “culture interview,” even for back office and policy roles, according to former employees and an archived copy of the company’s careers page.

One prospective hire said they were quizzed in the culture interview about ideas featured in company reading material sent ahead of interviews with Anthropic this spring, including two of Amodei’s essays about good and bad future paths for AI.

It’s “a bit of an ‘are you ready for the cult’ interview,” an Anthropic hiring manager texted the unsuccessful candidate, according to a screenshot reviewed by The Post.

The talent that made it through that filter drew heavily from the Bay Area’s effective altruism community, whose members try to calculate and maximize the good they can do in the world. Amodei, an influential early member of that scene, played a role in shifting donors’ attention toward the risks of AI, according to planning documents posted online by a philanthropy where he was a technical adviser. (He has since distanced himself from the movement.)

In those Bay Area circles, working at Anthropic brought clout. “I noticed that I was cooler because I was there,” said a former engineer who joined in 2021. The burgeoning field of AI safety, which grew to include a network of nonprofit organizations and other groups, focused on preventing calamity from AI, placed its hopes in Amodei and his Ants as high-integrity people who recognized the technology’s potential harms.

As the company grew, Anthropic sidestepped the liberal workplace politics and culture-war debates that caused internal divisions at more conventional Silicon Valley firms, multiple former employees said.

At one of his early Vision Quest talks, Amodei declared himself a patriot, said the early employee, who summarized the CEO’s remarks as, “America is awesome, democracy needs to win, it’s okay to support the military.” In public and in private, former employees said, Amodei casts the global AI race as a contest between democratic and authoritarian countries, and takes a hard-line view of China, which he argues should be cut off from the powerful chips needed to develop AI systems.

Even after Amodei’s remarks about Middle Eastern funding leaked, he promised staff in a Vision Quest talk last year that he wouldn’t self-censor, according to the former employee who left the company this year.

“Dario made a point to say, ‘I’m not going to let these leaks deter me from being honest. I care too much about the internal culture, and I don’t want to let the internal culture degrade.’ And he said some very unfiltered things just to make a point,” including calling Nvidia’s then-CEO Jensen Huang greedy, the former employee said.

Anthropic has recently moved to seed Amodei’s ideas with opinion-makers outside the company, scheduling a series of convenings like the one Gupta attended at Anthropic’s offices last month. The discussions have been held under the Chatham House Rule, but guests are encouraged to share what they heard.
“A typical session will focus on capabilities and safety, interpretability, national security, Claude’s constitution, economics etc.,” according to a Google Form for the events viewed by The Post.

Amodei did not speak to Gupta’s group, but whenever the topic turned to China, he said, staffers reliably echoed the CEO’s calls for export controls in a way that reminded Gupta of how AI chatbots reflect the values of their developers.
but the economist said staffers reliably echoed the CEO’s strident public warnings about AI, in a similar way to how AI chatbots reflect the values of their developers.
Before ringing in Anthropic’s record initial public offering at Times Square in New York on Thursday, Amodei delivered a short speech with some of his greatest hits.

“To state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei said.

His promise to go slow even as he placed his company’s fate in the hands of public shareholders echoed an essay he published in September, days after employee Coxon resigned and raised concerns about extinction risks, triggering uproar across Silicon Valley and in Washington.
Many Ants still at the company trust Amodei.

“They buy the narrative that leadership will work really hard and [are] not going to let the incentives steer them,” the former engineer said. After Anthropic’s IPO, about 600 employees own equity stakes worth more than $100 million, and more than 5,000 own shares worth more than $1 million, according to investment marketplace Hill.com.

For some in the AI safety community that has long seen Amodei as the industry’s only principled actor, the mismatch between his rhetoric and his company’s drive to make AI more powerful is no longer tenable.

Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI employee who has criticized the company’s safety practices since resigning in 2024, said that it was good that Amodei still writes out and circulates his ideas, but insufficient.

“It’s nice to be transparent. It’s nice to write more, ideally to the public,” but it doesn’t mean the public should trust the company or its leadership, said Kokotajlo, who along with Coxon spoke at a protest outside Anthropic’s headquarters the day its shares began to trade.

Irving, Amodei’s former collaborator at OpenAI, said that he now mostly skims the Anthropic CEO’s memos or reads summaries on Substack. “He’s just … another AI company CEO trapped in this horrible race,” he said.

The right thing for Anthropic to do is to stop pushing AI forward until the level of risk can be made acceptable, he said. Anthropic’s internal culture seems to have gotten the company to “a unified view that they should keep going,” he said, “and that’s just not a good view.”

news.article_content_zh:
旧金山——上个月，当 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 向投资者介绍其人工智能公司的未来产品计划时，公司总部其他地方举行了一场截然不同的会议。

Anthropic 邀请了十几位学者、智库研究员和媒体人士，听取高级人员的简报，介绍社会应如何应对强大人工智能的崛起。客人被要求首先阅读 Amodei 的一篇文章，该文章认为人工智能正在以危险的速度快速发展，以及指导其公司聊天机器人的 23,000 字“宪法”，其中包括“克劳德甚至不应该说善意的谎言”等声明。

与会者回忆道，在 10 楼的一间会议室里，大厅里有一家内置咖啡吧，Anthropic 的工作人员描述了人工智能如何越来越能够自我改进，并且教导机器道德可能会阻止它们变得有害。 “他们认为这将是人类的一场变革性事件，社会需要做好准备，”参加为期两天的项目的纽约大学经济学家阿皮特·古普塔 (Arpit Gupta) 说。他说，“我感觉到他们对人工智能的公众讨论不满意”，并希望改变它。

有关气候、科学和技术的新闻和指南。免费注册

古普塔和其他嘉宾接受了 Anthropic 内部观点的速成课程，这家公司是 Amodei 围绕人工智能将很快超越人类智能的愿景以及他对如何安全构建人工智能的信念而建立的。

该公司周四在股票市场上市，本周结束时估值超过 1.5 万亿美元，使阿莫迪和他的联合创始人成为十亿万富翁。他将 Anthropic 推向了人工智能竞赛的前沿，通过其技术赢得了商业客户，并通过独特的企业文化试图调和追逐利润与为社会做最好的事情之间的冲突，从而重塑了今年的美国经济。

阿莫代是一个头脑清醒的人，不会表现出典型硅谷创始人赤裸裸的野心，他带领他的员工通过文章、Slack 上发布的长备忘录以及每月两次的全体员工会谈（戏称“达里奥愿景探索”）阐述公司对人工智能开发、地缘政治等方面的思考，同时邀请员工进行讨论和辩论。这位首席执行官的成果在公司内部建立了一系列被视为显而易见、紧迫和正义的信念：人工智能取代人类是不可避免的，美国必须限制中国的人工智能发展，克劳德可能是有意识的。

根据对十多名熟悉该公司精神的人士（其中包括几位现任和前任员工）的采访，在这种紧密结合的文化中，自称“蚂蚁”的 Anthropic 员工感觉自己正在与最聪明的人一起解决世界上最紧迫的问题，肩负着保护人类的共同使命。

其核心是相信 Anthropic 和 Amodei 知道什么对世界最有利。 Anthropic 前员工雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 于 9 月份公开辞职，他表示：“如果你认为它会取得很好的效果，这就是曼哈顿计划式的、疯狂、有趣的地方。”他警告说，Anthropic 感觉自己陷入了一场可能导致人类灭绝的人工智能竞赛。

“Anthropic 普遍存在的一件事是：我们将披上斗篷，我们将成为负责任的人，我们将积累巨大的权力，但是……因为我们负责任地行事，所以有责任获得更多权力，”今年离开公司的一名前员工表示，与其他人一样，他要求匿名，以避免遭到公司报复。

前员工表示，Anthropic 的领导层通过对泄密的零容忍政策和强制保密的严格社会规范，严格控制公司内部辩论的细节。

去年，《连线》报道称，阿莫迪在 Slack 消息中承认，接受中东国家的资金可能会“让独裁者致富”，今年离职的前员工表示，去年，Anthropic 发起了一项内部调查。该员工表示，泄密者已被解雇，此前尚未报道过这一事件。自那以后，阿莫迪大量的 Slack 备忘录中的细节似乎只被泄露了一次。

人类拒绝发表评论。

该公司在 IPO 招股说明书中表示，Anthropic 的收入可能达到整个美国经济的规模。知情人士称，该公司向投资者传达的信息与阿莫迪经常为员工勾画的未来愿景相符，即人工智能公司拥有民族国家的力量。

news.title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
news.title_en: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
news.author: Terrence O'Brien
news.article_content:
Over the last week or so, we have seen a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage that brought entire companies to a standstill, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase. But the consensus is that there are more to come. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN:

Microsoft President Brad Smith issued a similar warning about further outages to CBS, but sounded a much more ominous tone.

While the outages over the last week were believed to be caused by cyberattacks, Smith said that AI has made it easier to find flaws, “and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems,” he said.

The last few months have also seen an increase in attacks on government and commercial systems, including those at the USDA, JP Morgan, and supermarkets.

Whether outages are brought on by AI-assisted hackers or human error during the rush to patch an aging system, one thing seems certain: there will be more in the coming months.

news.title_zh: 科技高管警告：AI助推网络基础设施脆弱性
news.summary_zh: 美国国家情报总监与微软总裁布拉德·史密斯警告，AI正被滥用于发掘系统漏洞，未来大规模数字基础设施宕机事件将更频繁

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国国家情报总监贾伊·克莱顿（Jay Clayton）与微软公司总裁布拉德·史密斯（Brad Smith）公开警告，近期航空与银行系统频繁宕机反映了关键基础设施的脆弱性加剧。他们指出，人工智能技术的普及显著降低了攻击者发现底层代码漏洞的门槛，导致政府及商业系统面临的安全威胁频率大幅上升。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that recent outages in aviation and banking systems underscore systemic infrastructure fragility. They emphasized that AI adoption has lowered the barrier for attackers to identify code vulnerabilities, leading to an increased frequency of cyber threats against government and commercial targets.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI不仅在重塑生产力，更在物理层面将防御战线大幅前移，导致遗留IT系统的维护成本与脆弱性呈指数级攀升。企业若无法实现基于AI的自动化实时修复（Auto-Remediation），将被困在攻击者通过AI全天候扫描与防御者手动修补的时间差博弈中。

news.article_content_zh:
在过去一周左右的时间里，我们看到了美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）在全国范围内停飞、导致整个公司陷入瘫痪的 Outlook 多日宕机以及摩根大通银行业务的宕机。但共识是还会有更多的事情发生。国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 告诉 CNN：

微软总裁布拉德·史密斯（Brad Smith）对哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）的进一步停电发出了类似的警告，但语气却更加不祥。

虽然上周的中断被认为是由网络攻击引起的，但史密斯表示，人工智能使发现缺陷变得更加容易，“然后你可以使用这些知识来修补代码，或者如果你是一个坏人，你可以使用这些知识来尝试侵入系统，”他说。

过去几个月，针对政府和商业系统的攻击也有所增加，包括美国农业部、摩根大通和超市。

无论中断是由人工智能辅助的黑客造成的，还是在急于修补老化系统时的人为错误造成的，有一点似乎是确定的：未来几个月还会出现更多中断。

news.title: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
news.title_en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
news.author: Garrett Downs
news.article_content:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road"after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.

Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union"that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.

"The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road,"Clayton said.

"You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot,"he said.

Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.

The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.

Separately, Microsoft said the Outlook outage was caused by "an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade."

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation."

Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent said: "No, they shouldn't."

"The patches may cause a glitch,"he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."

news.title_zh: 美国情报界警告AI基础设施升级伴随系统风险
news.summary_zh: 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton指出，为适应AI时代而进行的系统升级与网络安全加固将不可避免地导致短期技术性中断

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton与财政部长Scott Bessent联合警示，由于政府及关键基础设施部门正在进行大规模AI适配升级与网络安全强化，公众应预期航空、金融等系统出现间歇性中断。近期波及微软Outlook及航空系统的故障已被确认为技术性容量升级过程中的阵痛，而非AI关联的网络攻击。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Americans should expect intermittent service outages as government and critical infrastructure undergo systemic upgrades for AI integration. Recent technology disruptions, including those affecting Microsoft Outlook and air travel, have been attributed to network capacity patches rather than AI-related cyberattacks.

elements_zh.who: 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton、财政部长Scott Bessent
elements_zh.where: 美国国家电视媒体访谈
elements_zh.what: 强调AI转型期的系统升级成本，明确近期的基础设施中断属于技术性阵痛，并非安全漏洞。
elements_zh.why: 针对近期航空业及金融业出现的突发系统故障，平抑公众对AI安全性与系统韧性的担忧。

elements_en.who: Jay Clayton (Director of National Intelligence), Scott Bessent (Treasury Secretary)
elements_en.what: Advocating for systemic AI upgrades despite inevitable short-term service disruptions, confirming recent outages were patch-related.
elements_en.why: To address public concerns over infrastructure reliability and national security risks stemming from AI integration.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次高层舆论管控旨在将基础设施的脆弱性从“安全防御失守”重构为“必要的转型阵痛”，其本质反映了美方正处于AI算力与模型部署的被迫赶工期。供应链在寻求防御性补丁与AI兼容性时，系统复杂度的指数级增长已触及现有遗留基础设施的冗余极限，未来三年将是国家级IT系统架构重塑的脆弱窗口期。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The high-level guidance attempts to reframe systemic fragility as a necessary transition cost rather than a security failure, signaling an urgent and aggressive AI infrastructure integration phase. With systemic complexity outstripping the redundancy of legacy architectures, the next three years represent a fragile window for the mandatory overhaul of national digital infrastructure.

key_points_zh: 官方澄清：近期技术故障与AI系统适配升级相关，排除恶意攻击干扰。
监管态度：政府明确将技术中断视为“转型期疫苗”，优先保证长期的系统免疫力与韧性。
后续影响：未来在基础设施与网络安全领域的投资强度将持续增加，系统不稳定性短期内或将常态化。
key_points_en: Official clarification: Recent outages are linked to AI system patches, not malicious attacks.
Regulatory stance: System interruptions are characterized as necessary 'vaccines' for long-term digital resiliency.
Outlook: Increased investment in cybersecurity and infrastructure, with potential for continued short-term instability.

With systemic complexity outstripping the redundancy of legacy architectures, the next three years represent a fragile window for the mandatory overhaul of national digital infrastructure.

news.article_content_zh:
在一系列破坏性技术中断震撼了航空旅行和 Microsoft Outlook 等系统后，国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 警告美国人要为“道路上的颠簸”做好准备。

政府官员在很大程度上否认了这种中断与协调或人工智能网络攻击有关的可能性，这种中断也减缓了银行交易。

然而，克莱顿在美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）的《国情咨文》（State of the Union）节目中表示，随着企业和政府升级系统以适应人工智能时代，停电可能会继续。

克莱顿说：“美国人民应该为升级我们的系统进行大量投资做好准备；他们应该为网络安全投资做好准备；他们应该做好准备，任何时候技术、计算和应用程序发生阶跃变化时，道路上都会遇到坎坷。”

“你要做好准备，知道系统将要升级；它们可能会中断一段时间，而公司和政府正在积极应对这一问题，”他说。

克莱顿发出警告之际，美国正准备周四庆祝感恩节，感恩节是一年中最繁忙的旅行周之一。一周多前，一次技术故障导致全国范围内停飞，持续了几个小时。

美国联邦航空管理局表示，路由器升级导致大量数据导致飞机停飞，并且没有迹象表明受到网络攻击。

另外，微软表示 Outlook 中断是由“早期网络容量升级过程中的问题”引起的。

财政部长斯科特·贝森特在哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对国家”节目中也表达了类似的信息。

当被问及美国人是否应该担心其金融机构的安全时，贝森特说：“不，他们不应该。”

“这些补丁可能会导致故障，”他说，指的是银行正在采取的防范人工智能的措施。 “我认为美国人民应该将其视为一种疫苗；你的手臂可能会受伤，第二天你可能会感觉有点难受，但它会增加你的长期免疫力和弹性。”
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton、财政部长Scott Bessent在美国国家电视媒体访谈：强调AI转型期的系统升级成本，明确近期的基础设施中断属于技术性阵痛，并非安全漏洞。
【起因与机理】针对近期航空业及金融业出现的突发系统故障，平抑公众对AI安全性与系统韧性的担忧。
【核心事实细节】官方澄清：近期技术故障与AI系统适配升级相关，排除恶意攻击干扰。
【行业影响与走向】后续影响：未来在基础设施与网络安全领域的投资强度将持续增加，系统不稳定性短期内或将常态化。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Jay Clayton (Director of National Intelligence), Scott Bessent (Treasury Secretary) (National television interviews): Advocating for systemic AI upgrades despite inevitable short-term service disruptions, confirming recent outages were patch-related.
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address public concerns over infrastructure reliability and national security risks stemming from AI integration.
[Key Fact Detail] Official clarification: Recent outages are linked to AI system patches, not malicious attacks.
[Key Position & Outlook] Outlook: Increased investment in cybersecurity and infrastructure, with potential for continued short-term instability.

news.title: Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
news.title_en: Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
news.author: Alan Rappeport
news.article_content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday declined to endorse the return of Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia and said that future leadership of the company should depend on the outcome of investigations into who was responsible for the company’s advanced chips being sold to China.

The comments, made on the CBS program “Face the Nation,” came as the administration continues to face questions about how Nvidia’s advanced chips managed to get into China despite restrictions on those sales.

Mr. Huang, who resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence had identified as a Chinese asset, is scheduled to testify about the situation at a private House hearing on Dec. 1.

“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” Mr. Bessent said. “Were these malicious actors down at the bottom of the company who were responsible for the noncompliance?”

The treasury secretary said that he was confident that internal committees at Nvidia were investigating the matter and that they would soon provide the Trump administration with some “very fulsome and robust answers.” He downplayed concerns about Mr. Huang’s affair, suggesting that the relationship was a “canard” and that the corporate culture at Nvidia was more important than “one person’s foibles.”

“I assume that he didn’t know that she was an alleged spy,” Mr. Bessent said of Mr. Huang.

The trepidations about Mr. Huang were at odds with sentiments expressed by President Trump, who has continued to back the former chief executive. At a news conference on Friday, Mr. Trump said that he wanted Mr. Huang to return as Nvidia’s chief executive.

“I think the company, if they were smart, they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work,” Mr. Trump said.

The Justice and Commerce Departments said last week that they were pursuing a criminal investigation of Megaspeed, a Singapore company once led by Alice Huang, the woman whom U.S. officials believe worked as a Chinese intelligence asset while having an affair with Mr. Huang. Government officials are looking into whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia’s chips into China.

The Securities and Exchange Commission has also opened an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices.

The upheaval at Nvidia has raised questions about the artificial intelligence industry and the risks that it poses to national security.

Mr. Bessent said last week that he believed Nvidia needed a major leadership shake-up. On Sunday, he urged the company to provide the Trump administration with more information.

“It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Mr. Bessent said. “Was there promiscuous attitude toward this and, if it happened, where were the faults, and then they can move on.”
