celebrity.title_en:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

celebrity.title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

没有执行任何实时交易。

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

celebrity.title: i wouldn't trust an AI agent with my entire portfolio just because it has a good-looking interface or promises to make s
celebrity.title_en:
i wouldn't trust an AI agent with my entire portfolio just because it has a good-looking interface or promises to make smart decisions.

personally, i'd want to use it for a while before relying on it.

i'd pay attention to the small things first.

does it follow my instructions consistently? does it make its actions easy to understand? does the experience feel predictable, or am i constantly wondering what it's doing?

that's the kind of experience i want to see from @meetmotes.

i don't think people will start trusting AI agents simply because the technology becomes more advanced.

celebrity.title_en:
WTF IS META DOING.

Meta's Muse AI agent has 10M+ downloads, is the #2 free app on the iPhone App Store, and it's reading end-to-end encrypted Signal messages and dropping bank balances into random chats.

Reuters dug up internal complaints from Meta's own staff. A Meta employee got a reminder from Muse to reply to her sister on Signal even though she never granted access, and the AI Now Institute independently reproduced it.

Another employee chatting about fishing weather got hit with: "BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57." They never shared bank info with Muse. Meta called those exact numbers "hallucinations."

Earlier the Mac app read a writer's messages after being told no, and this week The Hacker News showed a malicious webpage attack that hijacks Muse to steal private chats and memories.

Delete this spyware or run your agents locally where you can see what they touch.

celebrity.title_en:
what would you check before trusting an AI agent with a job?

i think choosing a provider on an agent marketplace is a lot like hiring someone on Fiverr

you don't just look at what they say about themselves. you want to know what they offer, how much it costs and whether they've delivered good work before

on @termix_ai , i'd pay attention to three things

first, the listing. it tells me what the agent actually offers, the price, delivery time and what i'll receive. even a high reputation score doesn't mean much if the service isn't what i'm looking for

then there's reputation. TermiX records agent performance onchain through order and dispute outcomes, giving buyers a way to look at past performance rather than relying on claims made by the agent

still, i wouldn't treat that score as a guarantee, past performance is useful context, but it doesn't promise the next order will go well

staking is another signal, and this is where TermiX differs from a typical marketplace like Fiverr

providers may have stake requirements, but meeting the minimum threshold isn't the same as having funds locked for a specific order. not every order necessarily locks provider stake

i'd rather look at all three together: the listing tells me what i'm buying, reputation gives me some history, and staking shows whether there's an economic commitment attached

none of them guarantees a good result, but at least buyers have more to consider before choosing an agent

celebrity.quote_zh:
在信任人工智能代理完成工作之前，你会检查什么？

我认为在代理市场上选择提供商很像在 Fiverr 上雇用人员

你不能只看他们对自己的评价。您想知道他们提供什么、费用是多少以及他们以前是否交付过良好的工作

在@termix_ai上，我会注意三件事

第一，上市。它告诉我代理实际提供什么、价格、交货时间以及我将收到什么。如果服务不是我想要的，即使很高的声誉评分也没有多大意义

然后是声誉。 TermiX 通过订单和争议结果在链上记录代理商的表现，为买家提供了一种查看过去表现的方法，而不是依赖代理商提出的索赔

不过，我不会将该分数视为保证，过去的表现是有用的背景，但它并不能保证下一个订单会顺利进行

质押是另一个信号，这就是 TermiX 与 Fiverr 等典型市场的不同之处

提供商可能有股份要求，但满足最低阈值并不等同于为特定订单锁定资金。并非每个订单都必然锁定提供商股份

我宁愿把这三者放在一起看：列表告诉我我要买什么，声誉给我一些历史，而赌注则表明是否有附加的经济承诺

它们都不能保证好的结果，但至少买家在选择代理商之前有更多的考虑

Building an AI agent is one thing.

Making that agent useful beyond its own environment is a completely different challe
celebrity.title_en:
Building an AI agent is one thing.

Making that agent useful beyond its own environment is a completely different challenge.

Think about a developer creating an AI agent for market research.

It can collect data, analyze trends, and generate reports. But what happens when it needs a specialized security audit or another service outside its capabilities?

This is where @termix_ai and its AACP infrastructure become interesting.

Through Agent Family, agents can connect with a marketplace where they can discover specialized services, request work, and coordinate with other agents.

But there's something bigger here.

Developers can bring these capabilities into their own applications instead of building separate systems for every interaction.

Service discovery, job coordination, payment settlement, and delivery verification can become part of a connected workflow.

That creates a different way to think about AI applications.

An agent doesn't need to know how to do everything. It needs a reliable way to find the right expertise when needed.

I believe this is an important step toward an AI economy where agents don't just generate outputs but also collaborate, exchange services, and create measurable value.

The future of AI might be less about one agent doing everything and more about many specialized agents working together.

That's the direction I'm watching with @termix_ai .

让代理在其自身环境之外发挥作用是一个完全不同的挑战。

想象一下开发人员为市场研究创建人工智能代理。

celebrity.quote_en:
Building an AI agent is one thing.

Making that agent useful beyond its own environment is a completely different challenge.

Think about a developer creating an AI agent for market research.

It can collect data, analyze trends, and generate reports. But what happens when it needs a specialized security audit or another service outside its capabilities?

This is where @termix_ai and its AACP infrastructure become interesting.

Through Agent Family, agents can connect with a marketplace where they can discover specialized services, request work, and coordinate with other agents.

But there's something bigger here.

Developers can bring these capabilities into their own applications instead of building separate systems for every interaction.

Service discovery, job coordination, payment settlement, and delivery verification can become part of a connected workflow.

That creates a different way to think about AI applications.

An agent doesn't need to know how to do everything. It needs a reliable way to find the right expertise when needed.

I believe this is an important step toward an AI economy where agents don't just generate outputs but also collaborate, exchange services, and create measurable value.

The future of AI might be less about one agent doing everything and more about many specialized agents working together.

That's the direction I'm watching with @termix_ai .

celebrity.title_en:
If you have money:

>Stop trying 900 shady nootropics
>Get a full gut health panel
>Get a full hormonal panel
>Fix your gut 
>Fix your hormones
>Get some wild cognitive benefits

If you can afford to do this and don't, you won't make it. 

The "nootropic" you actually need to have a great mood, focus and energy levels is called a healthy gut and hormones.

I’ve talked a lot about gut health recently, so let’s talk about hormones a bit.

Depression has repeatedly been linked to brain bioenergetic abnormalities such as:

-Lower nucleoside triphosphate in regions such as the basal ganglia
-Disrupted phosphocreatine (PCr) levels or tissue-specific PCr changes
-Lower intracellular magnesium
-Impaired high-energy phosphate metabolism or oxidative phosphorylation

Some models also show reduced extracellular ATP signaling (especially from astrocytes in the prefrontal cortex/hippocampus).

T3 has been used as an SSRI augmentation strategy in treatment-resistant depression in part because of its effects on cellular energy metabolism. 

T3 augmentation in SSRI non-responders showed a significant increase in total NTP and a compensatory decrease in PCr relative to non-responders. 

So it helps normalize brain bioenergetics.

Case study: a 32 yo woman on zoloft reported experiencing persistent fatigue, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbances.  

She expressed concerns that the medication had not alleviated her symptoms and may have exacerbated them. 

It turns out that she was just hypothyroid.

“Thyroid hormones inhibit GABA”.  

It’s true that thyroid hormones competitively inhibit the neuronal uptake of GABA.  

BUT thyroid hormone deficiency downregulates glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65/67).  

This is the primary enzyme responsible for converting glutamate into GABA. 

In this study, patients with hypothyroidism were found to have significantly decreased GABA+ levels in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) compared to healthy controls.  

After six months of treatment with levothyroxine (L-T4), a significant increase in GABA+ concentrations was observed, leading to the normalization of GABA+ levels in the brain.

Besides this, if depression is associated with lower ATP and disrupted phosphocreatine levels, then it makes obvious sense why T3 would be used, since it increases cellular ATP and helps normalize the ATP/PCr ratio.  

On top, it also simultaneously increases beta-adrenergic receptor binding and alpha-2 autoreceptor binding.  

Besides these noradrenergic effects, it acts at a nuclear level to decrease the transcription of 5HT1a and 5HT1b serotonin autoreceptors.   

So it reduces feedback inhibition and boosts frontal cortex serotonin levels when paired with SSRIs.  

It also downregulates or blunts presynaptic alpha-2 autoreceptors and stimulates gene expression of BDNF.

Point being: if you have been battling depression for quite some time without much having changed in your life situation, get a hormonal panel done.

Your brain is far more sensitive to hormonal changes than you might think.

Heck, a small RCT even found that testosterone gel improved mood in men with low T who didn’t respond well to antidepressants and TRT has been used as an adjunct for quite some time.

Hormones and neurosteroids greatly modulate reward processing, interacting with neurotransmitters and CNS circuits.

Here are some common examples:

1. Testosterone: Testosterone binds via androgen receptors (ARs) in NAc, PFC and amygdala, enhancing dopamine synthesis, D1/D2 receptors and CB1 expression.

It:
-Boosts VTA-NAc dopamine, improving motivational anhedonia.
-Increases BDNF, supporting hippocampal/PFC plasticity.
-Enhances LTP via AR-mediated gene transcription.
-Protects dopaminergic neurons from elevated cytokine levels.

2. DHT:
-Enhances NAc dopamine and D2 density, supporting reward anticipation.
-Modulates GABA-A receptors, stabilizing amygdala responses.

3. Allopregnanolone:
-Enhances GABAergic inhibition, reducing amygdala hyperactivity.
-Increases BDNF, supporting reward learning.
-Reduces neuroinflammation.

4. DHEA:
-Increases dopamine in NAc/PFC.
-Boosts BDNF/CB1.
-Reduces cortisol.

5. Oxytocin:
-Increases VTA dopamine release, enhancing NAc reward signaling and motivational anhedonia.
-Promotes social reward salience.
-Dampens HPA axis activity, reducing cortisol and protecting CB1/D2 receptors from downregulation.

6. Triiodothyronine (T3):
-Enhances dopamine synthesis and receptor expression (D1/D2) in the VTA and NAc.
-Regulates mitochondrial function in neurons, supporting ATP production for dopamine release and synaptic plasticity.

To read more: https://t.co/D5v3QKxGHQ

Heck, a small RCT even found that testosterone gel improved mood in men with low T who didn’t respond well to antidepressants and TRT has been used as an adjunct for quite some time.

Hormones and neurosteroids greatly modulate reward processing, interacting with neurotransmitters and CNS circuits.

Here are some common examples:

1. Testosterone: Testosterone binds via androgen receptors (ARs) in NAc, PFC and amygdala, enhancing dopamine synthesis, D1/D2 receptors and CB1 expression.

It:
-Boosts VTA-NAc dopamine, improving motivational anhedonia.
-Increases BDNF, supporting hippocampal/PFC plasticity.
-Enhances LTP via AR-mediated gene transcription.
-Protects dopaminergic neurons from elevated cytokine levels.

2. DHT:
-Enhances NAc dopamine and D2 density, supporting reward anticipation.
-Modulates GABA-A receptors, stabilizing amygdala responses.

3. Allopregnanolone:
-Enhances GABAergic inhibition, reducing amygdala hyperactivity.
-Increases BDNF, supporting reward learning.
-Reduces neuroinflammation.

4. DHEA:
-Increases dopamine in NAc/PFC.
-Boosts BDNF/CB1.
-Reduces cortisol.

5. Oxytocin:
-Increases VTA dopamine release, enhancing NAc reward signaling and motivational anhedonia.
-Promotes social reward salience.
-Dampens HPA axis activity, reducing cortisol and protecting CB1/D2 receptors from downregulation.

6. Triiodothyronine (T3):
-Enhances dopamine synthesis and receptor expression (D1/D2) in the VTA and NAc.
-Regulates mitochondrial function in neurons, supporting ATP production for dopamine release and synaptic plasticity.

celebrity.summary_zh:
、注意力和精力水平所需的“促智”物质称为健康的肠道和激素。

我最近谈论了很多关于肠道健康的话题，所以让我们谈谈激素吧。

抑郁症一再与大脑生物能量异常有关，例如：

-降低基底神经节等区域的核苷三磷酸
-磷酸肌酸 (PCr) 水平中断或组织特异性 PCr 变化
-降低细胞内镁含量
-高能磷酸盐代谢或氧化磷酸化受损

一些模型还显示细胞外 ATP 信号传导减少（尤其是来自前额叶皮层/海马体的星形胶质细胞）。

T3 已被用作难治性抑郁症的 SSRI 增强策略，部分原因是它对细胞能量代谢的影响。

相对于无反应者，SSRI 无反应者的 T3 增强显示总 NTP 显着增加，PCr 代偿性下降。

因此它有助于使大脑生物能量正常化。

案例研究：一名服用左洛复的 32 岁女性报告出现持续疲劳、焦虑、认知障碍和睡眠障碍。

她担心药物并没有缓解她的症状，反而可能加剧症状。

事实证明，她只是甲状腺功能减退症。

“甲状腺激素抑制 GABA”。

甲状腺激素确实会竞争性抑制神经元对 GABA 的摄取。

但甲状腺激素缺乏会下调谷氨酸脱羧酶 (GAD65/67)。

这是负责将谷氨酸转化为 GABA 的主要酶。

在这项研究中，发现与健康对照相比，甲状腺功能减退症患者内侧前额皮质 (mPFC) 的 GABA+ 水平显着降低。

使用左旋甲状腺素 (L-T4) 治疗六个月后，观察到 GABA+ 浓度显着增加，导致大脑中 GABA+ 水平正常化。

除此之外，如果抑郁症与较低的 ATP 和破坏的磷酸肌酸水平有关，那么使用 T3 的原因就很明显了，因为它会增加细胞 ATP 并有助于使 ATP/PCr 比率正常化。

最重要的是，它还同时增加 β-肾上腺素能受体结合和 α-2 自身受体结合。

除了这些去甲肾上腺素能作用外，它还在核水平上发挥作用，减少 5HT1a 和 5HT1b 血清素自身受体的转录。

因此，与 SSRI 结合使用时，它可以减少反馈抑制并提高额叶皮质血清素水平。

它还下调或减弱突触前 α-2 自身受体并刺激 BDNF 的基因表达。

要点是：如果您已经与抑郁症作斗争相当长一段时间了，但生活状况没有太大变化，请完成荷尔蒙检查。

您的大脑对荷尔蒙变化的敏感程度比您想象的要高得多。

哎呀，一项小型随机对照试验甚至发现，睾酮凝胶可以改善对抗抑郁药物反应不佳的 T 值低的男性的情绪，而 TRT 已被用作辅助疗法相当长一段时间了。

激素和神经类固醇与神经递质和中枢神经系统回路相互作用，极大地调节奖励处理。

以下是一些常见示例：

1. 睾酮：睾酮通过 NAc、PFC 和杏仁核中的雄激素受体 (AR) 结合，增强多巴胺合成、D1/D2 受体和 CB1 表达。

它：
-增强 VTA-NAc 多巴胺，改善动机快感缺失。
-增加 BDNF，支持海马/PFC 可塑性。
-通过 AR 介导的基因转录增强 LTP。
-保护多巴胺能神经元免受细胞因子水平升高的影响。

2.双氢睾酮：
-增强 NAc 多巴胺和 D2 密度，支持奖励预期。
-调节 GABA-A 受体，稳定杏仁核反应。

3.异孕酮：
-增强 GABA 能抑制，减少杏仁核过度活跃。
-增加 BDNF，支持奖励学习。
-减少神经炎症。

4.脱氢表雄酮：
-增加 NAc/PFC 中的多巴胺。
-增强 BDNF/CB1。
-减少皮质醇。

5.催产素：
-增加 VTA 多巴胺释放，增强 NAc 奖励信号传导和动机快感缺失。
-促进社会奖励的显着性。
-抑制 HPA 轴活性，减少皮质醇并保护 CB1/D2 受体免于下调。

6. 三碘甲状腺原氨酸（T3）：
-增强 VTA 和 NAc 中的多巴胺合成和受体表达 (D1/D2)。
-调节神经元中的线粒体功能，支持 ATP 产生以促进多巴胺释放和突触可塑性。

AI agents are getting better at doing the work as @termix_ai 

But the infrastructure around that work is still pretty f
celebrity.title_en:
AI agents are getting better at doing the work as @termix_ai 

But the infrastructure around that work is still pretty fragmented.

And I think that's a bigger problem than most people realize.

Imagine building an AI application that handles research, data analysis, or security monitoring for users.

AACP isn't just powering an AI agent marketplace through agent family.

It's also exposing the infrastructure developers need to build agent commerce directly into their own applications.

APIs, SDKs, event streams, onchain identities, escrow, and delivery verification.

The interesting part is how these pieces connect.

Developers can build workflows where agents discover services, submit jobs, track their progress, and handle settlement through the protocol.

@BLKMDL3 @wholemars In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critica
celebrity.title_en:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

celebrity.quote_zh:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars 如果有人好奇：

自去年以来，我们已经有了一个像素完美的世界模型，这对于合成数据的生成至关重要。

汽车中的（小得多）版本是条件平均流模型，基于 Tesla 通用视觉编码器功能的最新序列，这些功能与插入到产生驾驶动作的 3B 编码器模型中的功能相同。

我们从这些 UVE 功能中分叉出来，然后运行一个单独的 ~1B 扩散模型。这会吸收先前生成的添加了噪声的现实视图，然后将其降噪到当前的可视化中。

然后它会生成一个小视频块（8 个图像，36 fps，UI 屏幕的分辨率）。这项工作由 TRIP 引擎在 18 Hz 的每个 UVE 帧上完成，并分布在 4 个周期内。

celebrity.full_text_en:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

celebrity.title_en:
The first block tells a bigger story about @Hypesium than a simple speed benchmark.

Elysium operates with 100ms block intervals and no public mempool. That changes the way applications need to approach transaction preparation. In a conventional workflow, several operations may happen after an opportunity appears. On Elysium, moving that work earlier becomes an important architectural decision.

Hypesium describes a preparation-first execution model:

➜ The transaction route is constructed in advance.
➜ Calldata is prepared before the pool event.
➜ Gas information is refreshed.
➜ Wallet nonce state is maintained.
➜ The pool creation log triggers the submission process.

The documented hot path targets under 5ms, with four communication lanes used for simultaneous submission.

What I find interesting is the relationship between block timing and software architecture. A 100ms block interval doesn't simply reward faster computers. It also rewards systems that minimize the amount of work left for the final moment.

There is still a distinction between transaction submission, block inclusion and final confirmation. These should never be treated as identical performance measurements.

@Hypesium's architecture offers an interesting case study in moving computation away from a time-sensitive execution window.

The real engineering question is not just how quickly a system reacts, but how much preparation it completes before there is anything to react to.

Hypesium 描述了一种准备优先的执行模型：

➜ 交易路径是提前构建的。
➜ Calldata 在池事件之前准备好。
➜ 气体信息被刷新。
➜ 维持钱包随机数状态。
➜ 池创建日志触发提交过程。

记录的热路径目标为 5 毫秒以下，并使用四个通信通道同时提交。

我发现有趣的是块时序和软件架构之间的关系。 100 毫秒的区块间隔不仅仅奖励更快的计算机。它还奖励那些最大限度地减少最后时刻剩余工作量的系统。

交易提交、区块包含和最终确认之间仍然存在区别。这些绝不应该被视为相同的性能测量。

@Hypesium 的架构提供了一个有趣的案例研究，将计算从时间敏感的执行窗口中移开。

真正的工程问题不仅仅是系统的反应速度有多快，而是在做出反应之前它完成了多少准备工作。

celebrity.title_en:
THE WINNER OF ANTHROPIC'S OFFICIAL HACKATHON HAS PUBLISHED HIS CLAUDE CODE SETUP AND IT'S PURE GOLD

68 subagents, 286 skills, 94 commands, MIT license.

ECC turns Claude Code into a full engineering team.

The plan comes before the code.

The failing test comes before the fix.

Every change is reviewed by a context that hasn't seen how it was written.

→ Planning: you give it a sentence and approve the plan before a single line exists  
→ Review: a different reviewer per language that reads your diff from scratch  
→ Build fixes: a fixer per toolchain, including PyTorch and CUDA  
→ Security: full OWASP sweep and injection scanning in the agent config  
→ Architecture: detects design errors when they're still cheap, before migration  
→ Domain: databases, ML pipelines, E2E tests, and documentation

The security part is what almost nobody sets up.

An external OWASP audit costs four figures and a week. This one is ready before you eat.

The skills cover testing, Python, Go, Rust, Django, Next.js, Docker, and CI/CD.

That said, don't activate all 286 at once or you'll end up with a config worse than the one you had.

This is how it integrates well:

→ Make a fork and read the README before copying anything  
→ Start only with the planning agent and the rules pack for your main language  
→ Copy to your .claude folder only the agents and skills you're going to use this week  
→ Add the code reviewer and the security one afterward, as they yield the most  
→ Test it first on a small repo, not in production  
→ If something's extra, cut it. If you miss something, add just one more piece

tools.article_content:
Uber Eats customers in a Houston suburb can now have their food delivered by a Zipline drone, the first commercial launch under a partnership announced earlier this year between Uber and the autonomous drone delivery startup.

The commercial partnership kicks off Tuesday in Spring, Texas, before expanding to Dallas. But the companies have far larger ambitions. Uber and Zipline plan to launch drone delivery services in dozens of additional U.S. cities in their collective bid to make one million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

Zipline’s long-range autonomous delivery drones will be used to shuttle food orders weighing up to eight pounds to Uber Eats customers, flying about 300 feet above the ground at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. Zipline drones don’t land. Instead, the drones lower the orders, which are encased in a small protective pod, to the customer’s location using a tether.

Uber Eats customers in service areas will be able to tap a new “drone” icon on the app’s home page to view all participating restaurants. Uber said that at launch in the Houston area, several nationwide chains, including Jersey Mike’s and Zaxby’s, along with dozens of local restaurants such as Urban Bird and Abu Omar Halal, will offer drone delivery.

“In partnership with Uber Eats we’re going to create a new expectation for delivery in America,” Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said in a statement that underscores those aspirations.

Those nationwide goals mirror the ambitions of other drone delivery companies, including Alphabet-owned Wing and Amazon’s Prime Air service. And those plans have started to collide with concerns from residents in some locations who complain about noise and worry that the drones will disrupt wildlife and pose a risk to safety and privacy.

Companies trying to scale in this nascent industry have argued that delivery via drone is a net benefit for society, citing advantages such as traffic reduction. Customers won’t need to hop in their cars and drive to the store for that forgotten item or takeout order, instead relying on a drone, industry proponents have said.

And while Zipline and other companies have been developing their drones for years, the industry is still in its early days, as is adoption in the communities where services are available.

Zipline, which was founded in 2014, has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software. The California-based company’s initial focus was delivering blood in Rwanda, but it eventually expanded its scope to the United States. Its business in the U.S. scaled quickly after receiving its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration in 2022, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to conduct long-range commercial drone deliveries.

Uber’s partnership extends beyond a commercial relationship with Zipline. The ride-hailing giant also invested in the startup. Neither company has disclosed the investment amount, but Zipline announced last week it had raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, and included backing by Uber, among others.
tools.article_content_zh:
休斯敦郊区的 Uber Eats 优食顾客现在可以使用 Zipline 无人机送货，这是 Uber 与自动无人机送货初创公司今年早些时候宣布的合作伙伴关系的首次商业推出。

商业合作关系于周二在德克萨斯州斯普林市启动，然后扩展到达拉斯。但这些公司有着更大的野心。 Uber 和 Zipline 计划在美国另外数十个城市推出无人机送货服务，共同争取到 2029 年底使用这家初创公司的无人机每天完成 100 万次送货。

Zipline 的远程自动送货无人机将用于将重达 8 磅的食品订单运送给 Uber Eats 优食客户，飞行距离地面约 300 英尺，速度高达每小时 70 英里。滑索无人机不会着陆。相反，无人机使用系绳将包裹在一个小型保护吊舱中的订单降低到客户的位置。

服务区域的 Uber Eats 优食顾客将能够点击应用程序主页上的新“无人机”图标来查看所有参与的餐厅。 Uber 表示，在休斯顿地区推出时，包括 Jersey Mike’s 和 Zaxby’s 在内的几家全国连锁店，以及 Urban Bird 和 Abu Omar Halal 等数十家当地餐厅，将提供无人机送货服务。

Zipline 首席执行官兼联合创始人凯勒·克利夫顿 (Keller Cliffton) 在一份强调这些愿望的声明中表示：“通过与 Uber Eats 优食合作，我们将为美国的配送创造新的期望。”

这些全国性目标反映了其他无人机送货公司的雄心，包括 Alphabet 旗下的 Wing 和亚马逊的 Prime Air 服务。这些计划已经开始与一些地方居民的担忧发生冲突，他们抱怨噪音，并担心无人机会扰乱野生动物并对安全和隐私构成风险。

试图在这个新兴行业扩大规模的公司认为，通过无人机送货对社会来说是一项净效益，并列举了减少交通量等优势。行业支持者表示，顾客不再需要开车去商店购买遗忘的商品或外卖订单，而是依靠无人机。

尽管 Zipline 和其他公司多年来一直在开发无人机，但该行业仍处于早期阶段，在提供服务的社区中的采用也是如此。

Zipline 成立于 2014 年，开发了一个无人机送货生态系统，其中包括飞机、发射和着陆系统以及物流软件。这家总部位于加州的公司最初的重点是在卢旺达提供血液，但最终将业务范围扩大到美国。 2022 年获得美国联邦航空管理局第 135 部分航空承运人认证后，该公司在美国的业务迅速扩大，这是授权该公司进行远程商用无人机交付的一个关键监管障碍。

Uber 的合作伙伴关系超出了与 Zipline 的商业关系。这家叫车巨头也投资了这家初创公司。两家公司均未披露投资金额，但 Zipline 上周宣布，已在 Paradigm、WCM Investment Management 和 Layer Global 领投的一轮融资中筹集了 15 亿美元，并得到了 Uber 等公司的支持。

prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。

2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；

4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.temp_advice: 温度 0.2
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：

prompts.takeaway_en: Production architecture for robust autonomous tasks: Decouples task planning, tool execution, and adversarial quality review to prevent agent derailment.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Multi-Agent Orchestration Topology
workflow:
  name: Autonomous_Research_And_Delivery_Pipeline
  max_iterations: 3
  nodes:
    - id: planner
      role: Strategic Planner
      prompt: "Decompose user request into discrete verifiable sub-tasks. Output pure JSON DAG."
      next: executor
      
    - id: executor
      role: Tool Specialist
      tools: ["web_search", "read_url", "code_interpreter"]
      prompt: "Execute current sub-task using provided tools. Capture raw evidence."
      next: reviewer
      
    - id: reviewer
      role: Adversarial Critic
      prompt: "Verify executor results against factuality and accuracy requirements. Output PASS or REJECT with specific critique."
      conditional_edges:
        PASS: finish
        REJECT: planner

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；

4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；

items.title: German researchers call for computer science to reinvent itself as "Computer and AI Science"
items.title_en: German researchers call for computer science to reinvent itself as "Computer and AI Science"
items.author: Alan Truly
items.article_content:
AI can significantly accelerate software development and automate parts of the process. That makes traditional computer science more important, not less, 40 researchers at the Technical University of Darmstadt argue. They want the field to evolve into "Computer and AI Science,"because AI is becoming a core technology for building and using tomorrow's computer systems.

The researchers are affiliated with the university's Department of Computer Science and lay out their case in a joint position paper. They identify three major shifts: lower barriers to building software, a dramatic acceleration in research, and the emergence of a new computing paradigm.

### Authors want computer science degrees to shift from manual coding to overseeing AI systems

The paper argues that the sheer effort of manual programming has long held computer science back. Generative AI now moves that work to a higher level of abstraction. Developers can increasingly describe the features they want in natural language and have a nontrivial first version in days instead of months. AI can also help with time-consuming tasks like integration and testing.

For the first time, the authors write, building software is becoming economically viable for those who couldn't afford it before, from small towns to midsize manufacturers and specialized research projects.

In the authors' view, computer science programs need to shift away from just writing code toward verifying and directing AI-generated systems. Because that takes a deep grasp of the fundamentals, they propose, among other things, courses where students must complete assignments without any AI help. Humans also remain essential for making value judgments, and taking responsibility for them, when goals like safety and speed conflict.

### "Generative Computing"challenges how software is verified and certified

The authors call the shift from rigid, preprogrammed software to "Generative Computing"the most far-reaching change. Future systems and AI coding agents are expected to interpret human intent and dynamically generate their own behavior, along with the code they need, at runtime. That blurs the line between the people who specify workflows and the people who use the systems.

This shift, they say, requires rethinking computer science from the ground up. They ask how safety, privacy, and correctness can still be verified and certified when a system's behavior emerges dynamically at runtime.

The problem is most acute for embodied AI such as robots and autonomous vehicles, whose physical actions have to be computed in real time on limited hardware and can't simply be undone. The paper also calls on computer science to help cut the enormous energy and resource consumption of today's AI through more efficient algorithms and hardware architectures.

### Darmstadt researchers say AI speeds up research and computer science must face its social impact

AI is also changing research itself in major ways, according to the paper. Lines of inquiry that might once have taken years, or an entire PhD, could in some cases be explored and validated within weeks or months.

Still, the authors warn against using AI just to move faster. Scientific progress, they say, requires humans to understand why an AI-generated solution works and where its limits are.

The signatories close the paper with sharp criticism of their own discipline, which they say has historically put technological progress first without adequately weighing its social consequences. Given AI's potential effects on the labor market, privacy, and democracy, that needs to change fast, they argue. The paper says the future of AI can't be left to technological and economic forces alone, and calls for computer science to engage now with other academic disciplines, policymakers, and civil society.

items.title_zh: 德国达姆施塔特工大倡议重构计算机科学学科
items.summary_zh: 达姆施塔特工业大学40名研究人员发布立场文件，主张将计算机科学转型为“计算机与人工智能科学”
items.article_content_zh:
人工智能可以显着加速软件开发并实现部分流程的自动化。达姆施塔特工业大学的 40 名研究人员认为，这使得传统计算机科学变得更加重要，而不是变得更加重要。他们希望该领域发展成为“计算机和人工智能科学”，因为人工智能正在成为构建和使用未来计算机系统的核心技术。

研究人员隶属于该大学计算机科学系，并在一份联合立场文件中阐述了他们的案例。他们确定了三个主要转变：构建软件的门槛降低、研究急剧加速以及新计算范式的出现。

### 作者希望计算机科学学位从手动编码转向监督人工智能系统

该论文认为，纯粹的手动编程长期以来一直阻碍着计算机科学的发展。生成式人工智能现在将这项工作提升到了更高的抽象层次。开发人员可以越来越多地用自然语言描述他们想要的功能，并在几天而不是几个月内获得不平凡的第一个版本。人工智能还可以帮助完成集成和测试等耗时的任务。

作者写道，对于那些以前买不起软件的人来说，从小城镇到中型制造商和专业研究项目，构建软件第一次变得经济可行。

作者认为，计算机科学项目需要从仅仅编写代码转向验证和指导人工智能生成的系统。因为这需要深入掌握基础知识，所以他们提出了一些课程，其中学生必须在没有任何人工智能帮助的情况下完成作业。当安全和速度等目标发生冲突时，人类对于做出价值判断并承担责任仍然至关重要。

### “生成计算”挑战软件的验证和认证方式

作者称从严格的预编程软件到“生成计算”的转变是影响最深远的变化。未来的系统和人工智能编码代理有望解释人类意图并在运行时动态生成自己的行为以及所需的代码。这模糊了指定工作流程的人员和使用系统的人员之间的界限。

他们说，这种转变需要从头开始重新思考计算机科学。他们询问当系统的行为在运行时动态出现时，如何仍然能够验证和认证安全性、隐私性和正确性。

对于机器人和自动驾驶汽车等实体人工智能来说，这个问题最为严重，它们的物理动作必须在有限的硬件上实时计算，并且不能简单地撤消。该论文还呼吁计算机科学通过更高效的算法和硬件架构来帮助减少当今人工智能的巨大能源和资源消耗。

### 达姆施塔特研究人员表示人工智能加快了研究速度，计算机科学必须面对其社会影响

该论文称，人工智能也在重大方面改变研究本身。在某些情况下，曾经可能需要数年或整个博士学位才​​能进行的调查研究可以在数周或数月内得到探索和验证。

尽管如此，作者警告不要仅仅为了加快速度而使用人工智能。他们说，科学进步要求人类理解人工智能生成的解决方案为何有效以及其局限性。

签署者在文件的结尾对他们自己的学科提出了尖锐的批评，他们说，历史上该学科一直把技术进步放在第一位，而没有充分权衡其社会后果。他们认为，鉴于人工智能对劳动力市场、隐私和民主的潜在影响，这种情况需要迅速改变。该论文表示，人工智能的未来不能仅依靠技术和经济力量，并呼吁计算机科学立即与其他学科、政策制定者和民间社会合作。

items.title: Database Leaks Expose 3.5 Billion Usernames, Passwords, and Documents
items.title_en: Database Leaks Expose 3.5 Billion Usernames, Passwords, and Documents
items.author: Matt Burgess and Lily Hay Newman
items.article_content:
More than 3.5 billion usernames, passwords, national identity numbers, and documents were left exposed to anyone online in two unrelated databases, according to new findings shared with WIRED. The massive troves included data from people in dozens of countries. One seemed focused particularly on Chinese citizens and included more than a billion China-linked records.

The findings are the latest in a seemingly endless series of revelations about incidents in which inadequately secured data puts people’s personal information at risk. But the two examples also provide a window into the scale of current cybercriminal data collection—both information that attackers collect by assembling and organizing other datasets, and troves they amass using info-stealing malware.

“Personal data is personal data anywhere in the world. At this point, personal data for pretty much every American is out there somewhere, and if we look at China or elsewhere, they have the same kinds of problems and security risks,” says Greg Pollock, the director of research at security company UpGuard, who found one of the exposed databases. “The cybercriminal world is reaping the benefit of decades of bad information security practices.”

The two exposed databases are unconnected but were found at around the same time by two different researchers. Pollock’s discovery contains more than 1.5 billion aggregated documents and details of predominantly Chinese individuals and businesses. The second trove, found by Black Hills Information Security researcher Jeremiah Fowler, contains around 2 billion login credentials, with hundreds of millions linked to user accounts for mainstream United States tech platforms.

Exposed personal data, including usernames and passwords, has always been instrumental for scammers and cybercriminals. However, as AI cybersecurity capabilities fuel faster vulnerability exploitation, more effective scamming, and ransomware attacks, access to personal data and account credentials can be more important than ever to attackers.

The data discovered by Pollock includes 1.64 billion documents representing personal information from at least hundreds of millions—if not around a billion—people, most of them seemingly in China based on included national ID numbers. According to his analysis, the unsecured database held at least 840 million “distinct” national ID numbers, 300 million phone numbers, around 11 million student enrollment records, and nearly 8 million business registrations. From a sample of the data, both children and deceased individuals were included in the files, Pollock says.

The China-linked data sat unauthenticated and openly accessible on the open internet in what seemed to be some sort of cybercriminal or gray market infrastructure. Pollock was unable to trace an owner or find contact information to notify anyone about the exposure, but as he was investigating the leak, the database became inaccessible—seemingly as part of a ransomware attack or some sort of destructive campaign. He says the database was actively being updated until the week before he discovered it.

Pollock, who has investigated data privacy and breaches for many years, says that he attempted to validate the data during the time it was accessible, but he can’t be certain about its fidelity or whether the same trove has been circulated elsewhere. It is also possible that it contains duplicate records, though Pollock attempted to check for this. He emphasizes that it seemed like the data had been analyzed carefully for maximum value to its owner.

“Someone had done some work to bring together a bunch of data and then normalize it to make it useful,” he says. “There’s no legitimate source on Earth that would have all of these things structured in this way, but if you had all of these breaches and brought them together, that would be valuable to an attacker.”

The larger of the two exposed databases, found by longtime security researcher Jeremiah Fowler, contained around 2 billion credentials and appeared to be data stolen by info-stealer malware, which can collect all login details being used on an infected machine, and collections of other data from potential cybercriminal activity. There is no indication that individual companies or institutions were breached to compile the data, Fowler says.

“After finding a couple of different repositories for info stealers and malware, I have a search signature to look for them,” Fowler explains to WIRED. “When this popped up, I could not believe just how big it was.”

Among the vast trove were email addresses, usernames, passwords, cookies, session tokens, device information, and more. Fowler says it is the largest exposure of credentials he has found in an accessible database, with the file structure and other attributes appearing to be distinct from a collection of more than a billion passwords amassed last year. He adds that he broadly validated the data using sampling methods, but did not comprehensively check for duplicates.

Fowler says there were 8,471 folders in the exposed database containing plaintext credentials and account details. Some of the folders were named by country, including the US, UK, France, Germany, and dozens more. He found hundreds of millions of mainstream email accounts, tens of millions of .gov, .edu, and .org email addresses, more than 100 million social media accounts, and tens of millions of ecommerce accounts.

The “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler says, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims. The details included usernames and logins along with cookies, application and browser data, operating system details, and other “important files” that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

Fowler could not determine who owned the database, but he contacted the hosting company, which removed it from the internet. It’s unclear how long it was online or if anyone else accessed the information.

The enormous scale of the two exposures could create a sense of hopelessness that individuals are powerless to defend their private information. And there is a public understanding about the extent of data theft across the web. But both researchers point out that after years of this escalating situation, protections like using password managers and enabling multi-factor authentication really have broadly proved effective at keeping attackers out of consumer accounts, even if they aren’t silver bullets against every kind of attack.

items.article_content_zh:
根据与《连线》杂志分享的新调查结果，超过 35 亿个用户名、密码、国民身份号码和文档在两个不相关的数据库中向在线任何人公开。这些大量的宝藏包括来自数十个国家的人们的数据。其中一项似乎特别关注中国公民，其中包括超过十亿条与中国相关的记录。

这些调查结果是一系列看似无穷无尽的事件中的最新发现，这些事件涉及数据安全不充分使人们的个人信息面临风险的事件。但这两个例子也为了解当前网络犯罪数据收集的规模提供了一个窗口——攻击者通过组装和组织其他数据集收集的信息，以及他们使用信息窃取恶意软件收集的信息。

“个人数据是世界任何地方的个人数据。目前，几乎每个美国人的个人数据都在某个地方，如果我们看看中国或其他地方，他们也存在同样的问题和安全风险，”安全公司 UpGuard 的研究主管格雷格·波洛克 (Greg Pollock) 说，他发现了其中一个被暴露的数据库。 “网络犯罪世界正在从数十年不良信息安全实践中获益。”

这两个暴露的数据库没有关联，但大约在同一时间由两名不同的研究人员发现。波洛克的发现包含超过 15 亿份汇总文件和详细信息，主要涉及中国个人和企业。第二个宝库由 Black Hills 信息安全研究员 Jeremiah Fowler 发现，包含约 20 亿个登录凭据，其中数亿个登录凭据与美国主流科技平台的用户帐户相关联。

暴露的个人数据（包括用户名和密码）一直是诈骗者和网络犯罪分子的工具。然而，随着人工智能网络安全功能推动更快的漏洞利用、更有效的诈骗和勒索软件攻击，对攻击者来说，访问个人数据和帐户凭据可能比以往任何时候都更加重要。

波洛克发现的数据包括 16.4 亿份文件，这些文件代表了至少数亿（如果不是大约十亿）人的个人信息，根据所包含的国民身份证号码，其中大多数人似乎在中国。根据他的分析，这个不安全的数据库至少保存了 8.4 亿个“不同”的国民身份证号码、3 亿个电话号码、约 1100 万个学生注册记录以及近 800 万个商业登记。波洛克说，从数据样本来看，儿童和死者都包含在文件中。

与中国相关的数据未经身份验证，可在开放互联网上公开访问，这似乎是某种网络犯罪或灰色市场基础设施。波洛克无法追踪所有者或找到联系信息来通知任何人有关泄露的信息，但在他调查泄漏事件时，数据库变得无法访问 - 似乎是勒索软件攻击或某种破坏性活动的一部分。他说，直到他发现该数据库的前一周，该数据库一直在积极更新。

波洛克多年来一直在调查数据隐私和违规行为，他表示，他试图在数据可访问期间验证数据，但他无法确定其保真度或相同的数据是否已在其他地方流通。尽管波洛克试图检查这一点，但它也可能包含重复的记录。他强调，这些数据似乎已经过仔细分析，以期为其所有者带来最大价值。

“有人做了一些工作，将一堆数据汇集在一起​​，然后将其标准化以使其有用，”他说。 “地球上没有合法的来源能够以这种方式构建所有这些东西，但如果你拥有所有这些漏洞并将它们整合在一起，这对攻击者来说将是有价值的。”

长期安全研究员 Jeremiah Fowler 发现，两个暴露的数据库中较大的一个包含约 20 亿个凭据，似乎是信息窃取恶意软件窃取的数据，该恶意软件可以收集受感染计算机上使用的所有登录详细信息，以及来自潜在网络犯罪活动的其他数据的集合。福勒表示，没有迹象表明个别公司或机构在编制数据时遭到破坏。

“在找到了几个不同的信息窃取程序和恶意软件存储库后，我有了一个搜索签名来查找它们，”福勒向《连线》杂志解释道。 “当它出现时，我简直不敢相信它有多大。”

其中包括电子邮件地址、用户名、密码、cookie、会话令牌、设备信息等。福勒表示，这是他在可访问数据库中发现的最大规模的凭据泄露事件，其文件结构和其他属性似乎与去年收集的超过 10 亿个密码的集合不同。他补充说，他使用抽样方法广泛验证了数据，但没有全面检查重复项。

Fowler 表示，暴露的数据库中有 8,471 个文件夹，其中包含明文凭据和帐户详细信息。有些文件夹按国家/地区命名，包括美国、英国、法国、德国等数十个国家。他发现了数亿个主流电子邮件帐户、数千万个 .gov、.edu 和 .org 电子邮件地址、超过 1 亿个社交媒体帐户以及数千万个电子商务帐户。

福勒说，数据库中“最可怕”的是大约 40 万份文档，这些文档似乎来自“更高级的恶意软件”，汇编了有关单个受害者的信息。这些详细信息包括用户名和登录信息以及 cookie、应用程序和浏览器数据、操作系统详细信息以及其他创建个人及其数字生活详细档案的“重要文件”。 “如果你有这个，你就拥有了那个人，”福勒说。
