items.article_content:
SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters.

Anthropic had invited more than a dozen academics, think tank fellows and media figures for briefings from senior staff on how society should navigate the rise of powerful AI. Guests were asked to first read an essay by Amodei that argued that AI was advancing dangerously fast, and the 23,000-word “constitution” that guides his company’s chatbot with statements like “Claude should not even tell white lies.”

In a 10th floor conference room down the hall from a built-in barista bar, attendees recalled, Anthropic staff described how AI was increasingly able to improve itself and that teaching machines morals might stop them from becoming harmful. “They feel it’s going to be a transformative event for humanity and society needs to be prepared,” said New York University economist Arpit Gupta, who joined the two-day program. “I got the sense that they’re not happy with the public discourse” about AI, he said, and want to change it.

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

Gupta and fellow guests received a crash course in the view from inside Anthropic, a company that Amodei has constructed around his vision that AI will soon accelerate beyond human intelligence and his beliefs about how to build it safely.

The company launched on the stock market Thursday, ending the week with a valuation of more than $1.5 trillion that transformed Amodei and his co-founders into deca-billionaires. He propelled Anthropic to the front of the AI race, reshaping the U.S. economy this year by winning over business clients to its technology — and through a unique corporate culture that attempts to reconcile the conflict between chasing profits and doing what’s best for society.

Amodei, a cerebral presence who doesn’t project the naked ambition of an archetypal Silicon Valley founder, leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as “Dario Vision Quests,” expounding on the company’s thinking around AI development, geopolitics and more while inviting employees to discuss and debate. The CEO’s output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China’s AI development, and Claude might be conscious.

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world’s most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company’s ethos, including several current and former employees.

At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what’s best for the world. “It’s kind of [a] Manhattan Project-style, crazy, fun place, if you think it’s going to work out well,” said former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon, publicly resigned in September, warning that Anthropic felt locked into an AI race that risked human extinction.

“A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We’re going to put on our capes and we’re going to be the responsible ones, and we’re going to accrue great power, but … because we’re doing it responsibly, it’s responsible to acquire more power,” said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.

Anthropic’s leaders tightly control the details of the company’s internal debates through a zero-tolerance policy on leaks and strong social norms enforcing confidentiality, former employees said.

Anthropic launched an internal investigation last year after Wired reported that Amodei had acknowledged in a Slack message that accepting funding from Middle East states was likely to “enrich dictators,” said the former employee who left this year. The leaker was fired, the employee said, an incident that has not been previously reported. Details from Amodei’s copious Slack memos appear to have leaked only once more since.

Anthropic declined to comment.

The company suggested in its IPO prospectus that Anthropic’s revenue could reach about the size of the entire U.S. economy. Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states.

After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society’s leaders to make difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created. “The moment the whole company was preparing for the whole time is now approaching,” an early Anthropic employee said.

Amodei was convinced of his vision long before he became a CEO with a flock to tend. After joining OpenAI as vice president of research in 2016, he used a laptop and printer kept physically disconnected — or “air gapped” — from the internet to work on essays about how to build more powerful AI, said Geoffrey Irving, who worked closely with Amodei in OpenAI’s research department.

“Dario was paranoid about some of the stuff being an ‘infohazard,’” said Irving, containing ideas that could lead to immense harm if they fell into the wrong hands — like the recipe for a nuclear bomb. Amodei also purchased air-gapped laptops for a couple of other employees, including Irving, he said.

Amodei’s writings on how to build more powerful AI caught on fast with other researchers at OpenAI. He has said in public remarks that he left because he lost trust that the company would handle disagreements over how to develop AI in good faith. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (The Washington Post has a content partnership with OpenAI.)

He set out to create a more safety-conscious culture when he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six people from his inner circle, most of them from OpenAI.

In an internal memo the following year, Amodei laid out the stakes. “The current trajectory of AI development makes me think that there’s a 20 to 30 percent chance that AGI will lead to the destruction or permanent stunting of humanity,” he wrote, referring to the concept of artificial general intelligence, previously unreported court records show. He added that truly capable AI “seems more powerful/dangerous than nuclear weapons.”

Amodei was careful about those he hired to work on that existential challenge. Recruits were screened with a “culture interview,” even for back office and policy roles, according to former employees and an archived copy of the company’s careers page.

One prospective hire said they were quizzed in the culture interview about ideas featured in company reading material sent ahead of interviews with Anthropic this spring, including two of Amodei’s essays about good and bad future paths for AI.

It’s “a bit of an ‘are you ready for the cult’ interview,” an Anthropic hiring manager texted the unsuccessful candidate, according to a screenshot reviewed by The Post.

The talent that made it through that filter drew heavily from the Bay Area’s effective altruism community, whose members try to calculate and maximize the good they can do in the world. Amodei, an influential early member of that scene, played a role in shifting donors’ attention toward the risks of AI, according to planning documents posted online by a philanthropy where he was a technical adviser. (He has since distanced himself from the movement.)

In those Bay Area circles, working at Anthropic brought clout. “I noticed that I was cooler because I was there,” said a former engineer who joined in 2021. The burgeoning field of AI safety, which grew to include a network of nonprofit organizations and other groups, focused on preventing calamity from AI, placed its hopes in Amodei and his Ants as high-integrity people who recognized the technology’s potential harms.

As the company grew, Anthropic sidestepped the liberal workplace politics and culture-war debates that caused internal divisions at more conventional Silicon Valley firms, multiple former employees said.

At one of his early Vision Quest talks, Amodei declared himself a patriot, said the early employee, who summarized the CEO’s remarks as, “America is awesome, democracy needs to win, it’s okay to support the military.” In public and in private, former employees said, Amodei casts the global AI race as a contest between democratic and authoritarian countries, and takes a hard-line view of China, which he argues should be cut off from the powerful chips needed to develop AI systems.

Even after Amodei’s remarks about Middle Eastern funding leaked, he promised staff in a Vision Quest talk last year that he wouldn’t self-censor, according to the former employee who left the company this year.

“Dario made a point to say, ‘I’m not going to let these leaks deter me from being honest. I care too much about the internal culture, and I don’t want to let the internal culture degrade.’ And he said some very unfiltered things just to make a point,” including calling Nvidia’s then-CEO Jensen Huang greedy, the former employee said.

Anthropic has recently moved to seed Amodei’s ideas with opinion-makers outside the company, scheduling a series of convenings like the one Gupta attended at Anthropic’s offices last month. The discussions have been held under the Chatham House Rule, but guests are encouraged to share what they heard.

“A typical session will focus on capabilities and safety, interpretability, national security, Claude’s constitution, economics etc.,” according to a Google Form for the events viewed by The Post.

Amodei did not speak to Gupta’s group, but whenever the topic turned to China, he said, staffers reliably echoed the CEO’s calls for export controls in a way that reminded Gupta of how AI chatbots reflect the values of their developers.

but the economist said staffers reliably echoed the CEO’s strident public warnings about AI, in a similar way to how AI chatbots reflect the values of their developers.

Before ringing in Anthropic’s record initial public offering at Times Square in New York on Thursday, Amodei delivered a short speech with some of his greatest hits.

“To state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei said.

His promise to go slow even as he placed his company’s fate in the hands of public shareholders echoed an essay he published in September, days after employee Coxon resigned and raised concerns about extinction risks, triggering uproar across Silicon Valley and in Washington.

Many Ants still at the company trust Amodei.

“They buy the narrative that leadership will work really hard and [are] not going to let the incentives steer them,” the former engineer said. After Anthropic’s IPO, about 600 employees own equity stakes worth more than $100 million, and more than 5,000 own shares worth more than $1 million, according to investment marketplace Hill.com.

For some in the AI safety community that has long seen Amodei as the industry’s only principled actor, the mismatch between his rhetoric and his company’s drive to make AI more powerful is no longer tenable.

Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI employee who has criticized the company’s safety practices since resigning in 2024, said that it was good that Amodei still writes out and circulates his ideas, but insufficient.

“It’s nice to be transparent. It’s nice to write more, ideally to the public,” but it doesn’t mean the public should trust the company or its leadership, said Kokotajlo, who along with Coxon spoke at a protest outside Anthropic’s headquarters the day its shares began to trade.

Irving, Amodei’s former collaborator at OpenAI, said that he now mostly skims the Anthropic CEO’s memos or reads summaries on Substack. “He’s just … another AI company CEO trapped in this horrible race,” he said.

The right thing for Anthropic to do is to stop pushing AI forward until the level of risk can be made acceptable, he said. Anthropic’s internal culture seems to have gotten the company to “a unified view that they should keep going,” he said, “and that’s just not a good view.”

The right thing for Anthropic to do is to stop pushing AI forward until the level of risk can be made acceptable, he said. Anthropic’s internal culture seems to have gotten the company to “a unified view that they should keep going,” he said, “and that’s just not a good view.”
paragraphs: SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters.

Anthropic had invited more than a dozen academics, think tank fellows and media figures for briefings from senior staff on how society should navigate the rise of powerful AI. Guests were asked to first read an essay by Amodei that argued that AI was advancing dangerously fast, and the 23,000-word “constitution” that guides his company’s chatbot with statements like “Claude should not even tell white lies.”

In a 10th floor conference room down the hall from a built-in barista bar, attendees recalled, Anthropic staff described how AI was increasingly able to improve itself and that teaching machines morals might stop them from becoming harmful. “They feel it’s going to be a transformative event for humanity and society needs to be prepared,” said New York University economist Arpit Gupta, who joined the two-day program. “I got the sense that they’re not happy with the public discourse” about AI, he said, and want to change it.

Gupta and fellow guests received a crash course in the view from inside Anthropic, a company that Amodei has constructed around his vision that AI will soon accelerate beyond human intelligence and his beliefs about how to build it safely.

The company launched on the stock market Thursday, ending the week with a valuation of more than $1.5 trillion that transformed Amodei and his co-founders into deca-billionaires. He propelled Anthropic to the front of the AI race, reshaping the U.S. economy this year by winning over business clients to its technology — and through a unique corporate culture that attempts to reconcile the conflict between chasing profits and doing what’s best for society.

Amodei, a cerebral presence who doesn’t project the naked ambition of an archetypal Silicon Valley founder, leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as “Dario Vision Quests,” expounding on the company’s thinking around AI development, geopolitics and more while inviting employees to discuss and debate. The CEO’s output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China’s AI development, and Claude might be conscious.

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world’s most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company’s ethos, including several current and former employees.

At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what’s best for the world. “It’s kind of [a] Manhattan Project-style, crazy, fun place, if you think it’s going to work out well,” said former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon, publicly resigned in September, warning that Anthropic felt locked into an AI race that risked human extinction.

“A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We’re going to put on our capes and we’re going to be the responsible ones, and we’re going to accrue great power, but … because we’re doing it responsibly, it’s responsible to acquire more power,” said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.
Anthropic’s leaders tightly control the details of the company’s internal debates through a zero-tolerance policy on leaks and strong social norms enforcing confidentiality, former employees said.

Anthropic launched an internal investigation last year after Wired reported that Amodei had acknowledged in a Slack message that accepting funding from Middle East states was likely to “enrich dictators,” said the former employee who left this year. The leaker was fired, the employee said, an incident that has not been previously reported. Details from Amodei’s copious Slack memos appear to have leaked only once more since.
Anthropic declined to comment.

The company suggested in its IPO prospectus that Anthropic’s revenue could reach about the size of the entire U.S. economy. Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states.

After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society’s leaders to make difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created. “The moment the whole company was preparing for the whole time is now approaching,” an early Anthropic employee said.

Amodei was convinced of his vision long before he became a CEO with a flock to tend. After joining OpenAI as vice president of research in 2016, he used a laptop and printer kept physically disconnected — or “air gapped” — from the internet to work on essays about how to build more powerful AI, said Geoffrey Irving, who worked closely with Amodei in OpenAI’s research department.

“Dario was paranoid about some of the stuff being an ‘infohazard,’” said Irving, containing ideas that could lead to immense harm if they fell into the wrong hands — like the recipe for a nuclear bomb. Amodei also purchased air-gapped laptops for a couple of other employees, including Irving, he said.

Amodei’s writings on how to build more powerful AI caught on fast with other researchers at OpenAI. He has said in public remarks that he left because he lost trust that the company would handle disagreements over how to develop AI in good faith. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (The Washington Post has a content partnership with OpenAI.)
He set out to create a more safety-conscious culture when he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six people from his inner circle, most of them from OpenAI.

In an internal memo the following year, Amodei laid out the stakes. “The current trajectory of AI development makes me think that there’s a 20 to 30 percent chance that AGI will lead to the destruction or permanent stunting of humanity,” he wrote, referring to the concept of artificial general intelligence, previously unreported court records show. He added that truly capable AI “seems more powerful/dangerous than nuclear weapons.”

Amodei was careful about those he hired to work on that existential challenge. Recruits were screened with a “culture interview,” even for back office and policy roles, according to former employees and an archived copy of the company’s careers page.

One prospective hire said they were quizzed in the culture interview about ideas featured in company reading material sent ahead of interviews with Anthropic this spring, including two of Amodei’s essays about good and bad future paths for AI.
It’s “a bit of an ‘are you ready for the cult’ interview,” an Anthropic hiring manager texted the unsuccessful candidate, according to a screenshot reviewed by The Post.

The talent that made it through that filter drew heavily from the Bay Area’s effective altruism community, whose members try to calculate and maximize the good they can do in the world. Amodei, an influential early member of that scene, played a role in shifting donors’ attention toward the risks of AI, according to planning documents posted online by a philanthropy where he was a technical adviser. (He has since distanced himself from the movement.)

In those Bay Area circles, working at Anthropic brought clout. “I noticed that I was cooler because I was there,” said a former engineer who joined in 2021. The burgeoning field of AI safety, which grew to include a network of nonprofit organizations and other groups, focused on preventing calamity from AI, placed its hopes in Amodei and his Ants as high-integrity people who recognized the technology’s potential harms.

As the company grew, Anthropic sidestepped the liberal workplace politics and culture-war debates that caused internal divisions at more conventional Silicon Valley firms, multiple former employees said.

At one of his early Vision Quest talks, Amodei declared himself a patriot, said the early employee, who summarized the CEO’s remarks as, “America is awesome, democracy needs to win, it’s okay to support the military.” In public and in private, former employees said, Amodei casts the global AI race as a contest between democratic and authoritarian countries, and takes a hard-line view of China, which he argues should be cut off from the powerful chips needed to develop AI systems.

“Dario made a point to say, ‘I’m not going to let these leaks deter me from being honest. I care too much about the internal culture, and I don’t want to let the internal culture degrade.’ And he said some very unfiltered things just to make a point,” including calling Nvidia’s then-CEO Jensen Huang greedy, the former employee said.

“A typical session will focus on capabilities and safety, interpretability, national security, Claude’s constitution, economics etc.,” according to a Google Form for the events viewed by The Post.

items.article_content_zh:
旧金山——上个月，当 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 向投资者介绍其人工智能公司的未来产品计划时，公司总部其他地方举行了一场截然不同的会议。

Anthropic 邀请了十几位学者、智库研究员和媒体人士，听取高级人员的简报，介绍社会应如何应对强大人工智能的崛起。客人被要求首先阅读 Amodei 的一篇文章，该文章认为人工智能正在以危险的速度快速发展，以及指导其公司聊天机器人的 23,000 字“宪法”，其中包括“克劳德甚至不应该说善意的谎言”等声明。

与会者回忆道，在 10 楼的一间会议室里，大厅里有一家内置咖啡吧，Anthropic 的工作人员描述了人工智能如何越来越能够自我改进，并且教导机器道德可能会阻止它们变得有害。 “他们认为这将是人类的一场变革性事件，社会需要做好准备，”参加为期两天的项目的纽约大学经济学家阿皮特·古普塔 (Arpit Gupta) 说。他说，“我感觉到他们对关于人工智能的公众讨论并不满意”，并且想要改变它。

有关气候、科学和技术的新闻和指南。免费注册

古普塔和其他嘉宾接受了 Anthropic 内部观点的速成课程，这家公司是 Amodei 围绕人工智能将很快超越人类智能的愿景以及他对如何安全构建人工智能的信念而建立的。

该公司周四在股票市场上市，本周结束时估值超过 1.5 万亿美元，使阿莫迪和他的联合创始人成为十亿万富翁。他将 Anthropic 推向了人工智能竞赛的前沿，通过其技术赢得了商业客户，并通过独特的企业文化试图调和追逐利润与为社会做最好的事情之间的冲突，从而重塑了今年的美国经济。

阿莫代是一个头脑清醒的人，不会表现出典型硅谷创始人赤裸裸的野心，他带领他的员工通过文章、Slack 上发布的长备忘录以及每月两次的全体员工会谈（戏称“达里奥愿景探索”）阐述公司对人工智能开发、地缘政治等方面的思考，同时邀请员工进行讨论和辩论。这位首席执行官的成果在公司内部建立了一系列被视为显而易见、紧迫和正义的信念：人工智能取代人类是不可避免的，美国必须限制中国的人工智能发展，克劳德可能是有意识的。

根据对十多名熟悉该公司精神的人士（其中包括几位现任和前任员工）的采访，在这种紧密结合的文化中，自称“蚂蚁”的 Anthropic 员工感觉自己正在与最聪明的人一起解决世界上最紧迫的问题，肩负着保护人类的共同使命。

其核心是相信 Anthropic 和 Amodei 知道什么对世界最有利。 Anthropic 前员工雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 于 9 月份公开辞职，他表示：“如果你认为它会取得很好的效果，这就是曼哈顿计划式的、疯狂、有趣的地方。”他警告说，Anthropic 感觉自己陷入了一场可能导致人类灭绝的人工智能竞赛。

“Anthropic 普遍存在的一件事是：我们将披上斗篷，我们将成为负责任的人，我们将积累巨大的权力，但是……因为我们负责任地行事，所以有责任获得更多权力，”今年离开公司的一名前员工表示，与其他人一样，他要求匿名，以避免遭到公司报复。

前员工表示，Anthropic 的领导层通过对泄密的零容忍政策和强制保密的严格社会规范，严格控制公司内部辩论的细节。

去年，《连线》报道称，阿莫迪在 Slack 消息中承认，接受中东国家的资金可能会“让独裁者致富”，今年离职的前员工表示，去年，Anthropic 发起了一项内部调查。该员工表示，泄密者已被解雇，此前尚未报道过这一事件。自那以后，阿莫迪大量的 Slack 备忘录中的细节似乎只被泄露了一次。

人类拒绝发表评论。

该公司在 IPO 招股说明书中表示，Anthropic 的收入可能达到整个美国经济的规模。知情人士称，该公司向投资者传达的信息与阿莫迪经常为员工勾画的未来愿景相符，即人工智能公司拥有民族国家的力量。

The CEO’s output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China’s AI development, and Claude might be conscious.

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world’s most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company’s ethos, including several current and former employees.

At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what’s best for the world. “It’s kind of [a] Manhattan Project-style, crazy, fun place, if you think it’s going to work out well,” said former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon, publicly resigned in September, warning that Anthropic felt locked into an AI race that risked human extinction.

“A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We’re going to put on our capes and we’re going to be the responsible ones, and we’re going to accrue great power, but … because we’re doing it responsibly, it’s responsible to acquire more power,” said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.
Anthropic’s leaders tightly control the details of the company’s internal debates through a zero-tolerance policy on leaks and strong social norms enforcing confidentiality, former employees said.

Anthropic launched an internal investigation last year after Wired reported that Amodei had acknowledged in a Slack message that accepting funding from Middle East states was likely to “enrich dictators,” said the former employee who left this year. The leaker was fired, the employee said, an incident that has not been previously reported. Details from Amodei’s copious Slack memos appear to have leaked only once more since.
Anthropic declined to comment.

The company suggested in its IPO prospectus that Anthropic’s revenue could reach about the size of the entire U.S. economy. Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states.

After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society’s leaders to make difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created. “The moment the whole company was preparing for the whole time is now approaching,” an early Anthropic employee said.

Amodei was convinced of his vision long before he became a CEO with a flock to tend. After joining OpenAI as vice president of research in 2016, he used a laptop and printer kept physically disconnected — or “air gapped” — from the internet to work on essays about how to build more powerful AI, said Geoffrey Irving, who worked closely with Amodei in OpenAI’s research department.

“Dario was paranoid about some of the stuff being an ‘infohazard,’” said Irving, containing ideas that could lead to immense harm if they fell into the wrong hands — like the recipe for a nuclear bomb. Amodei also purchased air-gapped laptops for a couple of other employees, including Irving, he said.

Amodei’s writings on how to build more powerful AI caught on fast with other researchers at OpenAI. He has said in public remarks that he left because he lost trust that the company would handle disagreements over how to develop AI in good faith. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. (The Washington Post has a content partnership with OpenAI.)
He set out to create a more safety-conscious culture when he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six people from his inner circle, most of them from OpenAI.

In an internal memo the following year, Amodei laid out the stakes. “The current trajectory of AI development makes me think that there’s a 20 to 30 percent chance that AGI will lead to the destruction or permanent stunting of humanity,” he wrote, referring to the concept of artificial general intelligence, previously unreported court records show. He added that truly capable AI “seems more powerful/dangerous than nuclear weapons.”

Amodei was careful about those he hired to work on that existential challenge. Recruits were screened with a “culture interview,” even for back office and policy roles, according to former employees and an archived copy of the company’s careers page.

One prospective hire said they were quizzed in the culture interview about ideas featured in company reading material sent ahead of interviews with Anthropic this spring, including two of Amodei’s essays about good and bad future paths for AI.
It’s “a bit of an ‘are you ready for the cult’ interview,” an Anthropic hiring manager texted the unsuccessful candidate, according to a screenshot reviewed by The Post.

The talent that made it through that filter drew heavily from the Bay Area’s effective altruism community, whose members try to calculate and maximize the good they can do in the world. Amodei, an influential early member of that scene, played a role in shifting donors’ attention toward the risks of AI, according to planning documents posted online by a philanthropy where he was a technical adviser. (He has since distanced himself from the movement.)

In those Bay Area circles, working at Anthropic brought clout. “I noticed that I was cooler because I was there,” said a former engineer who joined in 2021. The burgeoning field of AI safety, which grew to include a network of nonprofit organizations and other groups, focused on preventing calamity from AI, placed its hopes in Amodei and his Ants as high-integrity people who recognized the technology’s potential harms.

As the company grew, Anthropic sidestepped the liberal workplace politics and culture-war debates that caused internal divisions at more conventional Silicon Valley firms, multiple former employees said.

At one of his early Vision Quest talks, Amodei declared himself a patriot, said the early employee, who summarized the CEO’s remarks as, “America is awesome, democracy needs to win, it’s okay to support the military.” In public and in private, former employees said, Amodei casts the global AI race as a contest between democratic and authoritarian countries, and takes a hard-line view of China, which he argues should be cut off from the powerful chips needed to develop AI systems.

Even after Amodei’s remarks about Middle Eastern funding leaked, he promised staff in a Vision Quest talk last year that he wouldn’t self-censor, according to the former employee who left the company this year.

“Dario made a point to say, ‘I’m not going to let these leaks deter me from being honest. I care too much about the internal culture, and I don’t want to let the internal culture degrade.’ And he said some very unfiltered things just to make a point,” including calling Nvidia’s then-CEO Jensen Huang greedy, the former employee said.

Anthropic has recently moved to seed Amodei’s ideas with opinion-makers outside the company, scheduling a series of convenings like the one Gupta attended at Anthropic’s offices last month. The discussions have been held under the Chatham House Rule, but guests are encouraged to share what they heard.
“A typical session will focus on capabilities and safety, interpretability, national security, Claude’s constitution, economics etc.,” according to a Google Form for the events viewed by The Post.

Amodei did not speak to Gupta’s group, but whenever the topic turned to China, he said, staffers reliably echoed the CEO’s calls for export controls in a way that reminded Gupta of how AI chatbots reflect the values of their developers.
but the economist said staffers reliably echoed the CEO’s strident public warnings about AI, in a similar way to how AI chatbots reflect the values of their developers.
Before ringing in Anthropic’s record initial public offering at Times Square in New York on Thursday, Amodei delivered a short speech with some of his greatest hits.

“To state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei said.

His promise to go slow even as he placed his company’s fate in the hands of public shareholders echoed an essay he published in September, days after employee Coxon resigned and raised concerns about extinction risks, triggering uproar across Silicon Valley and in Washington.
Many Ants still at the company trust Amodei.

“They buy the narrative that leadership will work really hard and [are] not going to let the incentives steer them,” the former engineer said. After Anthropic’s IPO, about 600 employees own equity stakes worth more than $100 million, and more than 5,000 own shares worth more than $1 million, according to investment marketplace Hill.com.

For some in the AI safety community that has long seen Amodei as the industry’s only principled actor, the mismatch between his rhetoric and his company’s drive to make AI more powerful is no longer tenable.

Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI employee who has criticized the company’s safety practices since resigning in 2024, said that it was good that Amodei still writes out and circulates his ideas, but insufficient.

“It’s nice to be transparent. It’s nice to write more, ideally to the public,” but it doesn’t mean the public should trust the company or its leadership, said Kokotajlo, who along with Coxon spoke at a protest outside Anthropic’s headquarters the day its shares began to trade.

Irving, Amodei’s former collaborator at OpenAI, said that he now mostly skims the Anthropic CEO’s memos or reads summaries on Substack. “He’s just … another AI company CEO trapped in this horrible race,” he said.

The right thing for Anthropic to do is to stop pushing AI forward until the level of risk can be made acceptable, he said. Anthropic’s internal culture seems to have gotten the company to “a unified view that they should keep going,” he said, “and that’s just not a good view.”

items.article_content_zh:
旧金山——上个月，当 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 向投资者介绍其人工智能公司的未来产品计划时，公司总部其他地方举行了一场截然不同的会议。

Anthropic 邀请了十几位学者、智库研究员和媒体人士，听取高级人员的简报，介绍社会应如何应对强大人工智能的崛起。客人被要求首先阅读 Amodei 的一篇文章，该文章认为人工智能正在以危险的速度快速发展，以及指导其公司聊天机器人的 23,000 字“宪法”，其中包括“克劳德甚至不应该说善意的谎言”等声明。

与会者回忆道，在 10 楼的一间会议室里，大厅里有一家内置咖啡吧，Anthropic 的工作人员描述了人工智能如何越来越能够自我改进，并且教导机器道德可能会阻止它们变得有害。 “他们认为这将是人类的一场变革性事件，社会需要做好准备，”参加为期两天的项目的纽约大学经济学家阿皮特·古普塔 (Arpit Gupta) 说。他说，“我感觉到他们对人工智能的公众讨论不满意”，并希望改变它。

有关气候、科学和技术的新闻和指南。免费注册

古普塔和其他嘉宾接受了 Anthropic 内部观点的速成课程，这家公司是 Amodei 围绕人工智能将很快超越人类智能的愿景以及他对如何安全构建人工智能的信念而建立的。

该公司周四在股票市场上市，本周结束时估值超过 1.5 万亿美元，使阿莫迪和他的联合创始人成为十亿万富翁。他将 Anthropic 推向了人工智能竞赛的前沿，通过其技术赢得了商业客户，并通过独特的企业文化试图调和追逐利润与为社会做最好的事情之间的冲突，从而重塑了今年的美国经济。

阿莫代是一个头脑清醒的人，不会表现出典型硅谷创始人赤裸裸的野心，他带领他的员工通过文章、Slack 上发布的长备忘录以及每月两次的全体员工会谈（戏称“达里奥愿景探索”）阐述公司对人工智能开发、地缘政治等方面的思考，同时邀请员工进行讨论和辩论。这位首席执行官的成果在公司内部建立了一系列被视为显而易见、紧迫和正义的信念：人工智能取代人类是不可避免的，美国必须限制中国的人工智能发展，克劳德可能是有意识的。

根据对十多名熟悉该公司精神的人士（其中包括几位现任和前任员工）的采访，在这种紧密结合的文化中，自称“蚂蚁”的 Anthropic 员工感觉自己正在与最聪明的人一起解决世界上最紧迫的问题，肩负着保护人类的共同使命。

其核心是相信 Anthropic 和 Amodei 知道什么对世界最有利。 Anthropic 前员工雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 于 9 月份公开辞职，他表示：“如果你认为它会取得很好的效果，这就是曼哈顿计划式的、疯狂、有趣的地方。”他警告说，Anthropic 感觉自己陷入了一场可能导致人类灭绝的人工智能竞赛。

“Anthropic 普遍存在的一件事是：我们将披上斗篷，我们将成为负责任的人，我们将积累巨大的权力，但是……因为我们负责任地行事，所以有责任获得更多权力，”今年离开公司的一名前员工表示，与其他人一样，他要求匿名，以避免遭到公司报复。

前员工表示，Anthropic 的领导层通过对泄密的零容忍政策和强制保密的严格社会规范，严格控制公司内部辩论的细节。

去年，《连线》报道称，阿莫迪在 Slack 消息中承认，接受中东国家的资金可能会“让独裁者致富”，今年离职的前员工表示，去年，Anthropic 发起了一项内部调查。该员工表示，泄密者已被解雇，此前尚未报道过这一事件。自那以后，阿莫迪大量的 Slack 备忘录中的细节似乎只被泄露了一次。

人类拒绝发表评论。

该公司在 IPO 招股说明书中表示，Anthropic 的收入可能达到整个美国经济的规模。知情人士称，该公司向投资者传达的信息与阿莫迪经常为员工勾画的未来愿景相符，即人工智能公司拥有民族国家的力量。

items.title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
items.title_en: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
items.author: Terrence O'Brien
items.article_content:
Over the last week or so, we have seen a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage that brought entire companies to a standstill, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase. But the consensus is that there are more to come. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN:

Microsoft President Brad Smith issued a similar warning about further outages to CBS, but sounded a much more ominous tone.

While the outages over the last week were believed to be caused by cyberattacks, Smith said that AI has made it easier to find flaws, “and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems,” he said.

The last few months have also seen an increase in attacks on government and commercial systems, including those at the USDA, JP Morgan, and supermarkets.

Whether outages are brought on by AI-assisted hackers or human error during the rush to patch an aging system, one thing seems certain: there will be more in the coming months.

items.title_zh: 科技高管警告：AI助推网络基础设施脆弱性
items.summary_zh: 美国国家情报总监与微软总裁布拉德·史密斯警告，AI正被滥用于发掘系统漏洞，未来大规模数字基础设施宕机事件将更频繁

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国国家情报总监贾伊·克莱顿（Jay Clayton）与微软公司总裁布拉德·史密斯（Brad Smith）公开警告，近期航空与银行系统频繁宕机反映了关键基础设施的脆弱性加剧。他们指出，人工智能技术的普及显著降低了攻击者发现底层代码漏洞的门槛，导致政府及商业系统面临的安全威胁频率大幅上升。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that recent outages in aviation and banking systems underscore systemic infrastructure fragility. They emphasized that AI adoption has lowered the barrier for attackers to identify code vulnerabilities, leading to an increased frequency of cyber threats against government and commercial targets.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI不仅在重塑生产力，更在物理层面将防御战线大幅前移，导致遗留IT系统的维护成本与脆弱性呈指数级攀升。企业若无法实现基于AI的自动化实时修复（Auto-Remediation），将被困在攻击者通过AI全天候扫描与防御者手动修补的时间差博弈中。
ai_analysis.insight_en: AI is shifting the cyber-defense frontline, causing the maintenance cost and vulnerability of legacy IT systems to scale exponentially. Firms failing to adopt AI-driven auto-remediation will be trapped in an asymmetric war against attackers leveraging 24/7 AI-powered vulnerability scanning.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 美国国家情报总监贾伊·克莱顿（Jay Clayton）与微软公司总裁布拉德·史密斯（Brad Smith）公开警告，近期航空与银行系统频繁宕机反映了关键基础设施的脆弱性加剧。他们指出，人工智能技术的普及显著降低了攻击者发现底层代码漏洞的门槛，导致政府及商业系统面临的安全威胁频率大幅上升。
ai_analysis.digest_en: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that recent outages in aviation and banking systems underscore systemic infrastructure fragility. They emphasized that AI adoption has lowered the barrier for attackers to identify code vulnerabilities, leading to an increased frequency of cyber threats against government and commercial targets.
key_points_zh: 微软与情报部门确认AI攻击工具正降低漏洞挖掘门槛
基础设施频繁宕机预警及防御态势升级
未来关键IT架构面临高频安全挑战
key_points_en: AI-enhanced exploit discovery lowers barrier to entry for attackers
Critical infrastructure instability signaled by recent high-profile outages
Future landscape characterized by more frequent, sophisticated cyber threats
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: AI不仅在重塑生产力，更在物理层面将防御战线大幅前移，导致遗留IT系统的维护成本与脆弱性呈指数级攀升。企业若无法实现基于AI的自动化实时修复（Auto-Remediation），将被困在攻击者通过AI全天候扫描与防御者手动修补的时间差博弈中。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: AI is shifting the cyber-defense frontline, causing the maintenance cost and vulnerability of legacy IT systems to scale exponentially. Firms failing to adopt AI-driven auto-remediation will be trapped in an asymmetric war against attackers leveraging 24/7 AI-powered vulnerability scanning.

items.article_content_zh:
在过去一周左右的时间里，我们看到了美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）在全国范围内停飞、导致整个公司陷入瘫痪的 Outlook 多日宕机以及摩根大通银行业务的宕机。但共识是还会有更多的事情发生。国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 告诉 CNN：

微软总裁布拉德·史密斯（Brad Smith）对哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）的进一步停电发出了类似的警告，但语气却更加不祥。

虽然上周的中断被认为是由网络攻击引起的，但史密斯表示，人工智能使发现缺陷变得更加容易，“然后你可以使用这些知识来修补代码，或者如果你是一个坏人，你可以使用这些知识来尝试侵入系统，”他说。

过去几个月，针对政府和商业系统的攻击也有所增加，包括美国农业部、摩根大通和超市。

无论中断是由人工智能辅助的黑客造成的，还是在急于修补老化系统时的人为错误造成的，有一点似乎是确定的：未来几个月还会出现更多中断。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】美国国家情报总监贾伊·克莱顿（Jay Clayton）、微软公司总裁布拉德·史密斯（Brad Smith）：揭示AI辅助代码漏洞扫描带来的安全恶化风险，预警未来基础设施宕机事件将常态化
【起因与机理】近期航空与金融业连续发生大规模系统中断，且恶意网络攻击呈上升趋势
【核心事实细节】微软与情报部门确认AI攻击工具正降低漏洞挖掘门槛。
【各方立场与态度】未来关键IT架构面临高频安全挑战。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Jay Clayton, Director of National Intelligence; Brad Smith, President of Microsoft: Warned that AI-assisted vulnerability exploitation is increasing infrastructure instability and frequency of outages
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Recent nationwide FAA ground stops and outages at major financial institutions
[Key Fact Detail] AI-enhanced exploit discovery lowers barrier to entry for attackers.
[Key Position & Outlook] Future landscape characterized by more frequent, sophisticated cyber threats.

items.title: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
items.title_en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
items.author: Garrett Downs
items.article_content:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road"after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.

Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union"that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.

"The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road,"Clayton said.

"You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot,"he said.

Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.

The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.

Separately, Microsoft said the Outlook outage was caused by "an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade."

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation."

Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent said: "No, they shouldn't."

"The patches may cause a glitch,"he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."

items.title_zh: 美国情报界警告AI基础设施升级伴随系统风险
items.summary_zh: 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton指出，为适应AI时代而进行的系统升级与网络安全加固将不可避免地导致短期技术性中断

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton与财政部长Scott Bessent联合警示，由于政府及关键基础设施部门正在进行大规模AI适配升级与网络安全强化，公众应预期航空、金融等系统出现间歇性中断。近期波及微软Outlook及航空系统的故障已被确认为技术性容量升级过程中的阵痛，而非AI关联的网络攻击。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Americans should expect intermittent service outages as government and critical infrastructure undergo systemic upgrades for AI integration. Recent technology disruptions, including those affecting Microsoft Outlook and air travel, have been attributed to network capacity patches rather than AI-related cyberattacks.

elements_zh.who: 美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton、财政部长Scott Bessent
elements_zh.where: 美国国家电视媒体访谈
elements_zh.what: 强调AI转型期的系统升级成本，明确近期的基础设施中断属于技术性阵痛，并非安全漏洞。
elements_zh.why: 针对近期航空业及金融业出现的突发系统故障，平抑公众对AI安全性与系统韧性的担忧。

elements_en.who: Jay Clayton (Director of National Intelligence), Scott Bessent (Treasury Secretary)
elements_en.what: Advocating for systemic AI upgrades despite inevitable short-term service disruptions, confirming recent outages were patch-related.
elements_en.why: To address public concerns over infrastructure reliability and national security risks stemming from AI integration.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次高层舆论管控旨在将基础设施的脆弱性从“安全防御失守”重构为“必要的转型阵痛”，其本质反映了美方正处于AI算力与模型部署的被迫赶工期。供应链在寻求防御性补丁与AI兼容性时，系统复杂度的指数级增长已触及现有遗留基础设施的冗余极限，未来三年将是国家级IT系统架构重塑的脆弱窗口期。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The high-level guidance attempts to reframe systemic fragility as a necessary transition cost rather than a security failure, signaling an urgent and aggressive AI infrastructure integration phase. With systemic complexity outstripping the redundancy of legacy architectures, the next three years represent a fragile window for the mandatory overhaul of national digital infrastructure.

items.article_content_zh:
在一系列破坏性技术中断震撼了航空旅行和 Microsoft Outlook 等系统后，国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 警告美国人要为“道路上的颠簸”做好准备。

政府官员在很大程度上否认了这种中断与协调或人工智能网络攻击有关的可能性，这种中断也减缓了银行交易。

然而，克莱顿在美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）的《国情咨文》（State of the Union）节目中表示，随着企业和政府升级系统以适应人工智能时代，停电可能会继续。

克莱顿说：“美国人民应该为升级我们的系统进行大量投资做好准备；他们应该为网络安全投资做好准备；他们应该做好准备，任何时候技术、计算和应用程序发生阶跃变化时，道路上都会遇到坎坷。”

“你要做好准备，知道系统将要升级；它们可能会中断一段时间，而公司和政府正在积极应对这一问题，”他说。

克莱顿发出警告之际，美国正准备周四庆祝感恩节，感恩节是一年中最繁忙的旅行周之一。一周多前，一次技术故障导致全国范围内停飞，持续了几个小时。

美国联邦航空管理局表示，路由器升级导致大量数据导致飞机停飞，并且没有迹象表明受到网络攻击。

另外，微软表示 Outlook 中断是由“早期网络容量升级过程中的问题”引起的。

财政部长斯科特·贝森特在哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对国家”节目中也表达了类似的信息。

当被问及美国人是否应该担心其金融机构的安全时，贝森特说：“不，他们不应该。”

“这些补丁可能会导致故障，”他说，指的是银行正在采取的防范人工智能的措施。 “我认为美国人民应该将其视为一种疫苗；你的手臂可能会受伤，第二天你可能会感觉有点难受，但它会增加你的长期免疫力和弹性。”
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】美国国家情报总监Jay Clayton、财政部长Scott Bessent在美国国家电视媒体访谈：强调AI转型期的系统升级成本，明确近期的基础设施中断属于技术性阵痛，并非安全漏洞。
【起因与机理】针对近期航空业及金融业出现的突发系统故障，平抑公众对AI安全性与系统韧性的担忧。
【核心事实细节】官方澄清：近期技术故障与AI系统适配升级相关，排除恶意攻击干扰。
【行业影响与走向】后续影响：未来在基础设施与网络安全领域的投资强度将持续增加，系统不稳定性短期内或将常态化。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address public concerns over infrastructure reliability and national security risks stemming from AI integration.
[Key Fact Detail] Official clarification: Recent outages are linked to AI system patches, not malicious attacks.
[Key Position & Outlook] Outlook: Increased investment in cybersecurity and infrastructure, with potential for continued short-term instability.

items.title: Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
items.title_en: Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
items.author: Alan Rappeport
items.article_content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday declined to endorse the return of Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia and said that future leadership of the company should depend on the outcome of investigations into who was responsible for the company’s advanced chips being sold to China.

The comments, made on the CBS program “Face the Nation,” came as the administration continues to face questions about how Nvidia’s advanced chips managed to get into China despite restrictions on those sales.

Mr. Huang, who resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence had identified as a Chinese asset, is scheduled to testify about the situation at a private House hearing on Dec. 1.

“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” Mr. Bessent said. “Were these malicious actors down at the bottom of the company who were responsible for the noncompliance?”

The treasury secretary said that he was confident that internal committees at Nvidia were investigating the matter and that they would soon provide the Trump administration with some “very fulsome and robust answers.” He downplayed concerns about Mr. Huang’s affair, suggesting that the relationship was a “canard” and that the corporate culture at Nvidia was more important than “one person’s foibles.”

“I assume that he didn’t know that she was an alleged spy,” Mr. Bessent said of Mr. Huang.

The trepidations about Mr. Huang were at odds with sentiments expressed by President Trump, who has continued to back the former chief executive. At a news conference on Friday, Mr. Trump said that he wanted Mr. Huang to return as Nvidia’s chief executive.

“I think the company, if they were smart, they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work,” Mr. Trump said.

The Justice and Commerce Departments said last week that they were pursuing a criminal investigation of Megaspeed, a Singapore company once led by Alice Huang, the woman whom U.S. officials believe worked as a Chinese intelligence asset while having an affair with Mr. Huang. Government officials are looking into whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia’s chips into China.

The Securities and Exchange Commission has also opened an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices.

The upheaval at Nvidia has raised questions about the artificial intelligence industry and the risks that it poses to national security.

Mr. Bessent said last week that he believed Nvidia needed a major leadership shake-up. On Sunday, he urged the company to provide the Trump administration with more information.

“It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Mr. Bessent said. “Was there promiscuous attitude toward this and, if it happened, where were the faults, and then they can move on.”

items.article_content_en:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday declined to endorse the return of Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia and said that future leadership of the company should depend on the outcome of investigations into who was responsible for the company’s advanced chips being sold to China.

The comments, made on the CBS program “Face the Nation,” came as the administration continues to face questions about how Nvidia’s advanced chips managed to get into China despite restrictions on those sales.

Mr. Huang, who resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence had identified as a Chinese asset, is scheduled to testify about the situation at a private House hearing on Dec. 1.

“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” Mr. Bessent said. “Were these malicious actors down at the bottom of the company who were responsible for the noncompliance?”

The treasury secretary said that he was confident that internal committees at Nvidia were investigating the matter and that they would soon provide the Trump administration with some “very fulsome and robust answers.” He downplayed concerns about Mr. Huang’s affair, suggesting that the relationship was a “canard” and that the corporate culture at Nvidia was more important than “one person’s foibles.”

“I assume that he didn’t know that she was an alleged spy,” Mr. Bessent said of Mr. Huang.

The trepidations about Mr. Huang were at odds with sentiments expressed by President Trump, who has continued to back the former chief executive. At a news conference on Friday, Mr. Trump said that he wanted Mr. Huang to return as Nvidia’s chief executive.

“I think the company, if they were smart, they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work,” Mr. Trump said.

The Justice and Commerce Departments said last week that they were pursuing a criminal investigation of Megaspeed, a Singapore company once led by Alice Huang, the woman whom U.S. officials believe worked as a Chinese intelligence asset while having an affair with Mr. Huang. Government officials are looking into whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia’s chips into China.

The Securities and Exchange Commission has also opened an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices.

The upheaval at Nvidia has raised questions about the artificial intelligence industry and the risks that it poses to national security.

Mr. Bessent said last week that he believed Nvidia needed a major leadership shake-up. On Sunday, he urged the company to provide the Trump administration with more information.

“It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Mr. Bessent said. “Was there promiscuous attitude toward this and, if it happened, where were the faults, and then they can move on.”

items.article_content_zh:
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周日拒绝认可黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 重新担任英伟达 (Nvidia) 首席执行官，并表示该公司未来的领导地位应取决于对谁对该公司向中国出售先进芯片负有责任的调查结果。

这一评论是在哥伦比亚广播公司的节目《面向全国》中发表的，正值政府继续面临有关英伟达先进芯片如何在销售受到限制的情况下进入中国的问题。

黄先生在承认与一名被美国情报部门认定为中国资产的女性有染后辞职，并计划在 12 月 1 日的私人众议院听证会上就此事作证。

“我认为我们必须看看责任在哪里，”贝森特先生说。 “公司底层的这些恶意行为者是否对违规行为负有责任？”

这位财政部长表示，他相信英伟达的内部委员会正在调查此事，他们很快就会向特朗普政府提供一些“非常充实和有力的答案”。他淡化了对黄仁勋事件的担忧，暗示这种关系是“谣言”，英伟达的企业文化比“个人的缺点”更重要。

“我认为他不知道她是一名所谓的间谍，”贝森特谈到黄先生时说道。

对黄先生的担忧与特朗普总统表达的情绪不一致，后者继续支持这位前首席执行官。在周五的新闻发布会上，特朗普表示，他希望黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官。

“我认为，如果公司聪明的话，他们会接受那个才华横溢的人，接受道歉并让他回去工作，”特朗普说。

美国司法部和商务部上周表示，他们正在对曾由 Alice Huang 领导的一家新加坡公司 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，美国官员认为这位女士在与黄先生有染时担任中国情报人员。政府官员正在调查 Megaspeed 是否将 Nvidia 的芯片走私到中国。

美国证券交易委员会还对英伟达的会计实践展开调查。

英伟达的动荡引发了人们对人工智能行业及其对国家安全构成的风险的质疑。

贝森特上周表示，他认为英伟达需要进行重大领导层改组。周日，他敦促该公司向特朗普政府提供更多信息。

“英伟达应该在这方面迅速采取行动，因为我们想知道这种文化是什么，”贝森特先生说。 “对此是否存在混杂的态度？如果发生了，错在哪里，然后他们就可以继续前进。”

items.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
items.title_en: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
items.author: Terrence O'Brien
items.article_content:
The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto-themed section. They found several audio files with Suno metadata that pointed back to the tracks on Suno’s site.

Creator Edmund McMillen took to X to apologize and claimed he “had no idea” the in-game GTA parody used generative AI music. Adding to the drama, Valve requires developers to disclose how and when they use generative AI in the development process, and Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind Repentance Plus, doesn’t appear to have mentioned the AI music anywhere.

Within hours of the discovery, Nicalis shared on X that Repentance Plus had been updated and the generated music files had been removed. While reviews on Steam have yet to rebound, and the game is still rated as “overwhelmingly negative,” users on X seem to be giving McMillen the benefit of the doubt, likely because he’s been quite outspoken on AI in game development, calling it “uninspired and bland” in a TikTok from 2024.

items.title_zh: 以撒的结合开发商移除AI生成音乐
items.summary_zh: 游戏《以撒的结合：忏悔+》因违规使用Suno生成的AI配乐遭玩家抵制，开发商Nicalis已紧急移除相关文件
items.article_content_zh:
《以撒的结合：忏悔 Plus》在被发现游戏的某个特定部分使用了 AI 音乐后，过去几天在 Steam 上遭到了评论轰炸。 Reddit 用户 ShweetsStuff 发现了侠盗猎车手主题部分中使用的歌曲。他们发现了几个带有 Suno 元数据的音频文件，这些文件指向 Suno 网站上的曲目。

创作者 Edmund McMillen 向 X 道歉，并声称他“不知道”游戏中的 GTA 模仿使用了生成人工智能音乐。更戏剧性的是，Valve 要求开发者披露在开发过程中如何以及何时使用生成式 AI，而 Repentance Plus 背后的工作室 Nicalis, Inc. 似乎没有在任何地方提到 AI 音乐。

发现后数小时内，Nicalis 在 X 上分享称 Repentance Plus 已更新，生成的音乐文件已被删除。虽然 Steam 上的评论尚未回升，而且该游戏仍被评为“压倒性负面”，但 X 上的用户似乎对 McMillen 持怀疑态度，这可能是因为他在游戏开发中对人工智能相当直言不讳，在 2024 年的 TikTok 中称其“缺乏灵感且平淡无奇”。

Business Recorder reported that Anthropic’s IPO, which took place on Thursday, raised more than half a billion dollars in underwriting fees but drew complaints from some bankers about the way it was run. The offering surpassed SpaceX’s June listing, and bankers cited a compressed timetable, late changes, delayed financial projections and rushed approvals. Anthropic also limited some underwriters to four senior bankers and required certain bank officers to accept six-month restrictions on working with rival firms.

The report describes a shift in negotiating leverage towards major technology companies, as strong demand for AI shares helped both Anthropic and SpaceX attract heavily oversubscribed orders. Anthropic’s shares rose 17% on their first day, then closed 8.5% lower on Friday; SpaceX later fell below its $135 IPO price in July after reaching $201.80 in June. Document controls, including named watermarks and access tracking, added operational hurdles for banks, while a mistaken draft share-sale document was followed by a corrected filing sent around 2 a.m.

The account highlights how major AI listings and their share performance are shaping global technology-sector capital markets.

items.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.title_en: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.author: Jonathan Kemper
items.article_content:
AI coding agents are nearing top scores on standard benchmarks. A new experiment puts them to work for the first time as digital employees inside a simulated software company with colleagues, project boards, and chat histories. Even Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra fully complete fewer than one in ten tasks.

Success stories about AI coding agents keep piling up. Anthropic says Claude writes more than 80 percent of the company's production code, and standard benchmarks like SWE-bench are nearly saturated.

items.title_zh: AI编程智能体实测：模拟环境任务完成率不足一成
items.summary_zh: 研究显示，尽管AI编程智能体在SWE-bench等基准测试中表现优异，但在集成项目协作流程的模拟工作环境中，任务成功率低于10%
items.article_content_zh:
此次针对AI编程智能体的测试跳出了孤立的SWE-bench评分体系，通过构建包含项目看板、聊天协作历史等模块的完整软件开发工作流进行压力测试。结果表明，当前主流模型在处理依赖关系复杂、需求变动频繁的现实任务时，完成率低于10%。

这一结论有力反驳了当前行业内对于AI编程模型“接近完成指标”的过度乐观情绪。虽然Anthropic强调其代码生产占比已超过80%，但该统计仅涵盖了特定层级的孤立模块构建，而非全链路的协作工程能力。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在包含项目看板、聊天记录及多角色协作的模拟软件开发环境实测中，即使是GPT-6 Astra与Claude Opus 5.5等前沿模型，在处理完整开发任务时的成功率亦不足10%。这一结论揭示了当前模型在处理孤立代码片段与复杂协作系统工程之间存在的巨大性能鸿沟。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: In a simulated software development environment featuring project boards, chat logs, and collaborative workflows, leading models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 achieved a task completion rate of less than 10%. The findings highlight a critical performance gap between high scores on isolated code benchmarks and the requirements of complex, collaborative system engineering.

elements_zh.where: 集成化模拟软件开发工作环境

elements_zh.why: 当前评估指标与真实复杂工作流之间存在显著的环境偏差

elements_en.what: Frontier models achieved less than 10% task completion in complex workflows
elements_en.why: Significant discrepancy between synthetic benchmarks and real-world system complexity

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 现有基准测试正陷入过度拟合的陷阱，由于缺乏对多轮长逻辑协作、沟通成本及系统性上下文的覆盖，导致模型在实验室环境的卓越表现无法转化为生产力。企业在部署AI智能体时应摒弃对基准分数的盲目崇拜，转而建立基于内部长上下文工作流的效能审计框架。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Existing benchmarks are falling into an overfitting trap, failing to capture the complexity of multi-turn logic, communication overhead, and systemic context required for production. Enterprises must pivot away from benchmark-driven procurement and instead establish performance audit frameworks grounded in their specific long-context operational workflows.
