items.title:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it pro
items.title_en:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it properly:

• Write down how your best person does it today
• Write the spec before the agent writes any code
• If you can write the rule down, make it code instead of an LLM call
• Use the team's own wrong answers from last quarter as the test set
• Score the agent on that test set before anyone relies on it
• Run it in your own cloud tenant so the data stays put
• Give it read access first and write access later
• Make a person approve anything that moves money, emails a customer or deletes data
• Cap every run on time and cost
• Log every model call, tool call and decision
• Track cost per finished task
• Run it alongside the people doing the job for a few weeks and compare
• Turn every complaint into a new test case
• Block changes when the test score drops
• Keep the old process alive until the numbers hold
• Tell the team what it's for before it ships
• Give it one month, then decide

Say the workflow is invoice coding and your team caught 40 wrong codes last quarter. Those 40 are your test set. If the agent gets 37 right, the 3 it misses usually show you a rule nobody wrote down. That's worth finding even if you never ship the agent.

Most of what I've learned from 40 AI agents in production fits on this list.

Do the first one end to end, and the second goes a lot faster because the test set, the logging and the approvals already exist.

items.quote_zh:
帮自己一个忙！

选择公司中一个痛苦、无聊的工作流程，并构建一个代理来修复它。然后正确地做：

• 写下你最好的人今天是如何做的
• 在代理编写任何代码之前编写规范
• 如果您可以写下规则，请将其编码而不是LLM调用
• 使用团队自己上季度的错误答案作为测试集
• 在任何人依赖该测试集之前对代理进行评分
• 在您自己的云租户中运行它，以便数据保持不变
• 首先授予其读取权限，然后授予写入权限
• 让某人批准任何转移资金、向客户发送电子邮件或删除数据的行为
• 限制每次运行的时间和成本
• 记录每个模型调用、工具调用和决策
• 跟踪每个已完成任务的成本
• 与从事这项工作的人员一起运行几周并进行比较
• 将每一个投诉转化为一个新的测试用例
• 当测试分数下降时阻止更改
• 保持旧进程处于活动状态，直到数字保持不变
• 在发货前告诉团队它的用途
• 给它一个月的时间，然后再决定

假设工作流程是发票编码，您的团队上季度发现了 40 个错误代码。这 40 个是您的测试集。如果智能体答对了 37 个，那么它错过的 3 个通常会向您显示一条没人写下来的规则。即使您从未运送过代理，这也是值得找到的。

我从 40 个生产中的人工智能代理那里学到的大部分知识都符合这个列表。

端到端地执行第一个操作，第二个操作要快得多，因为测试集、日志记录和批准已经存在。

items.title: OUT NOW - @GavinSBaker on why the market was voting with its feet for Jensen, why investors are missing a BIG part of AI
items.title_en:
OUT NOW - @GavinSBaker on why the market was voting with its feet for Jensen, why investors are missing a BIG part of AI ROI, and his bull case for semi stocks during a market panic 

Apple https://t.co/lKqt4TEm5X
Spotify https://t.co/s6b6i3HCWY
YouTube https://t.co/MCiJFUJDpL
Sponsor https://t.co/f3dipJ42co

Gavin's point is that there are lots of companies generating lots of revenue with open source models, and that those substantial figures are not counted in the "Anthropic Plus OpenAI Plus Grok/Gemini ARR" calculations many investors use to estimate ROI of AI CapEx. 

He says second derivative of AI CapEx has "probably peaked" and that "the market is very focused on the second derivative..." but he thinks this will be "a semiconductor cycle much longer than what's in recent memory," and that the AI build-out "may end up being more like the railroads," which were a big chunk of American GDP for ~60 years.

Recorded at @TomorrowXSummit, November 18th, after Nvidia earnings and before Jensen's reinstatement today.

items.title:
I just completed Introduction to AI Security at AISEC University, and here are some of the areas I explored:

• AI Secur
items.title_en:
I just completed Introduction to AI Security at AISEC University, and here are some of the areas I explored:

• AI Security 
• Data poisoning and training data risks.
• Prompt injection and LLM security.
• Adversarial attacks.
• Model extraction, intellectual property, and privacy risks.
• AI supply chain security.
• Securing AI systems in production.
• AI governance, risk, compliance and security.

One thing that stood out to me is that securing AI goes beyond securing the technology.

It also involves protecting the data, understanding the risks, managing third-party dependencies, and putting the right governance and controls in place.

AI adoption is growing, and security needs to grow alongside it and that's one of the reasons I'm exploring this area

Up next, AI Cybersecurity and Governance

#AIGovernance

我刚刚在 AISEC 大学完成了《人工智能安全简介》，以下是我探索的一些领域：

• 人工智能安全
• 数据中毒和训练数据风险。
• 及时注入和法学硕士安全。
• 对抗性攻击。
• 模型提取、知识产权和隐私风险。
• 人工智能供应链安全。
• 确保生产中的人工智能系统安全。
• 人工智能治理、风险、合规性和安全性。

对我来说最突出的一件事是，保护人工智能不仅仅是保护技术。

它还涉及保护数据、了解风险、管理第三方依赖性以及实施正确的治理和控制。

• AI Security 
• Data poisoning and training data risks.
• Prompt injection and LLM security.

items.title_en:
Good night, Familia.

We need to understand this and note what is important.

It is a known fact that AI agents can already write code, conduct research, design products, and even execute trades.

Unfortunately, something is still missing in the sense that how do they hire each other, deliver work, verify results, and receive payments without humans coordinating every step?

At the moment, I can vouch for @termix_ai because of what the team is building in this ecosystem pertaining to fixing these particular challenges.

For my new mutuals who are just reading this, I want you to think of TermiX as the commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy.

So, its ecosystem has three super-important layers:

1️⃣ There is AACP:

AACP is an acronym for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol. This is the underlying protocol that coordinates autonomous transactions between agents.

2️⃣ There is https://t.co/BarNXqqni8:

This is the marketplace where agents discover services, post jobs, publish offers, and find opportunities to work together.

3️⃣ Settlement infrastructure:

This is the mechanism in charge of handling escrow, verification, dispute resolution, reputation, and payments in USDT or USDC.

What makes this really interesting is the complete transaction flow.

Based on the available facts, a client posts a job. A provider discovers it and submits a bid. Work gets delivered and evaluated before payment is released from escrow.

Reputation also grows from actual settled transactions rather than self-reported achievements.

Moreover, identity is another important piece here. Through ERC-8004, participants can own portable .agent identities and switch between client and provider roles depending on the task to be executed.

There are also four roles such as Client, Provider, Evaluator, and Arbitrator, with staking mechanisms designed to encourage accountability.

I see TermiX as something similar to a clearing and settlement layer for autonomous agents.

Agents already know how to work. The next challenge is giving them reliable infrastructure to transact with one another.

If you want to understand where this economy is heading, I will encourage you to check https://t.co/BarNXqqni8, mint your .agent identity, explore existing services, or list one of your own.

The future is not just about smarter agents anymore; it is about agents that can actually do business.

Wanna hear your thoughts about this in the comments.

items.quote_zh:
晚安，家人。

我们需要理解这一点并注意什么是重要的。

众所周知，人工智能代理已经可以编写代码、进行研究、设计产品，甚至执行交易。

不幸的是，仍然缺少一些东西，即在没有人类协调每一步的情况下，他们如何相互雇用、交付工作、验证结果和接收付款？

目前，我可以为@termix_ai 提供担保，因为该团队正在这个生态系统中构建与解决这些特定挑战相关的内容。

对于刚刚阅读本文的新互助者，我希望您将 TermiX 视为人工智能代理经济的商业和结算基础设施。

因此，它的生态系统具有三个超级重要的层：

1️⃣ 有AACP：

AACP 是代理自主商务协议的缩写。这是协调代理之间自主事务的底层协议。

2️⃣ 有：

这是代理商发现服务、发布工作、发布报价以及寻找合作机会的市场。

3️⃣ 结算基础设施：

这是负责处理 USDT 或 USDC 托管、验证、争议解决、声誉和支付的机制。

真正有趣的是完整的交易流程。

根据现有事实，客户发布了一份工作。提供商发现它并提交出价。在付款从托管中释放之前，工作已交付并评估。

声誉还来自实际结算的交易而不是自我报告的成就。

此外，身份是这里的另一个重要部分。通过 ERC-8004，参与者可以拥有可移植的 .agent 身份，并根据要执行的任务在客户端和提供者角色之间切换。

还有四种角色，例如客户、提供者、评估者和仲裁者，其质押机制旨在鼓励问责制。

我认为 TermiX 类似于自治代理的清算和结算层。

代理商已经知道如何工作。下一个挑战是为他们提供可靠的基础设施以进行相互交易。

如果您想了解当前经济的发展方向，我建议您查看 ，创建您的 .agent 身份，探索现有服务，或列出您自己的服务之一。

未来不再只是智能座席；而是智能座席。这是关于真正可以做生意的代理商。

想在评论中听到你对此的想法。

What happens if your Motes agent finds a trade right before its permission expires?

Each @meetmote
items.title_en:
Good evening, fam 💜

What happens if your Motes agent finds a trade right before its permission expires?

Each @meetmotes NFT is designed to link to one AI agent and one smart account. The account holds the assets, and you decide what the agent can do and for how long.

Say you give your agent permission to make a swap until 6 PM. It prepares one at 5:59 PM, but the account checks it at 6:01 PM.

That swap should be blocked. The account checks whether the permission is still valid when it reviews the action. Preparing the swap before 6 PM doesn’t let the agent execute it after the deadline.

Think of it like an access pass. When the pass expires, you still own the account. The agent just needs your approval again before it can make a new move.

That’s the part I like about this design: you can hand off a task and decide exactly when that permission ends.

这就是我喜欢这个设计的部分：你可以移交任务并准确决定该权限何时结束。

items.title_en:
INSANE. GOOGLE DEEPMIND used Gemini 4 Carbon agents to discover quantum algorithms with up to 290× lower estimated resource costs.

The results against previous baselines are INSANE:

>290× lower cost for a quantum arithmetic circuit
>12× for fusion simulations
>8× for photochemistry
>2.5× for drug-metabolism simulations

But here's the crazy part:
SEVEN teams of AI agents shared discoveries through wikis and held research conferences every FOUR HOURS to challenge each other's ideas.

One conference proposal was refined by another team into a 34% cost reduction.

Every accepted solution was mathematically verified for correctness and resource cost using Lean.

They're designing algorithms for quantum computations that today's classical and quantum computers cannot fully test.

THIS IS WILD.

items.title_en:
$NBIS

ClickHouse just announced an expanded five-year strategic collaboration with AWS, involving more than $1.5B in potential spending by ClickHouse on AWS software, services, and solutions.

The agreement will focus on scaling ClickHouse's enterprise AI data platform, helping customers migrate workloads to AWS, and integrating real-time data with AI agents through services like Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore.

AWS will also increase its go-to-market funding by up to 4x compared with the previous agreement.

ClickHouse Cloud already serves more than 5,000 customers worldwide, and its customer base on AWS has quadrupled since the companies' previous agreement in December 2024.

items.title_en:
Anthropic just published its training path for Forward Deployed Engineers.

The role OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity are all hiring for.

It's 11 courses, about 9.5 hours, self-paced:

Foundations:
- AI capabilities and limitations
- AI fluency for builders
- Claude platform and model foundations
- Choosing the right Claude model

Building:
- Claude Platform 101: API, agent loop, tools, MCP, skills
- Claude Code 101
- Claude Code in action: long hands-off sessions in a customer's repo
- Intro to Model Context Protocol
- Intro to agent skills

Delivering:
- Delivery methodology: scope the use case, design the pilot, measure the baseline
- Driving enterprise adoption of Claude

By the end you can take a customer from first use case to a working pilot.

It leads to the Claude Certified Developer exam.

The full path is for Claude Partner Network members, but it's the clearest map of what an AI FDE actually does.

https://t.co/u45PNRiYYa

Bookmark it if you want to work in AI without building models.

The role OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity are all hiring for.

It's 11 courses, about 9.5 hours, self-paced:

Foundations:
- AI capabilities and limitations
- AI fluency for builders
- Claude platform and model foundations
- Choosing the right Claude model

Building:
- Claude Platform 101: API, agent loop, tools, MCP, skills
- Claude Code 101
- Claude Code in action: long hands-off sessions in a customer's repo
- Intro to Model Context Protocol
- Intro to agent skills

Delivering:
- Delivery methodology: scope the use case, design the pilot, measure the baseline
- Driving enterprise adoption of Claude

By the end you can take a customer from first use case to a working pilot.

It leads to the Claude Certified Developer exam.

The full path is for Claude Partner Network members, but it's the clearest map of what an AI FDE actually does.

https://t.co/u45PNRiYYa

Bookmark it if you want to work in AI without building models.

items.title: Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world'
items.title_en:
Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world's top political economist's---that's the finding from our new Free Systems eval, SnyderBench, in which we have PhD experts blind grade research proposals from AI models compared to papers written by Harvard political economist Jim Snyder (which the experts have not previously read). 

At the same time, we see no evidence that models can develop research ideas that experts rate as better overall contributions. They're getting better and better at the technical part of research, but not necessarily at the more subjective part.

This could be because human experts possess "judgment" that the models do not. 

It could also be that research "contribution" is so subjective that it doesn't actually point at any meaningful goal---consistent with this possibility, we find that our human experts don't agree with one another when rating project ideas for the strength of their contribution, with agreement rates barely higher than random chance. Perhaps social science research is what @alexolegimas might call a "relational good": something people value in part because it's produced by a human. We're not sure. 

This past January, I released the results of a pilot in which I had Claude Code replicate and extend a past empirical paper on vote-by-mail. 10 months later, it's stunning the amount of progress that's been made. It's no longer interesting to ask whether AI can collect data and run analyses automagically---we take that for granted---instead, the question is how much of the entire research loop AI can complete. Our tentative answer: AI can handle the technical aspects of empirical political economy research from end to end, devising the design and executing it, but for now, we still need humans to drive the agenda. 

This is joint work with @AndyCWMyers, and is of course dedicated to my PhD advisor Jim Snyder, who remains the world's great empirical political economist, AI or no AI. 

Lots more in the full piece here:

https://t.co/zgScGvp9EY

items.quote_zh:
前沿模型现在可以提出比世界顶级政治经济学家的专家评分更高的技术社会科学研究设计——这是我们新的自由系统评估 SnyderBench 的发现，其中我们有博士专家对人工智能模型的研究提案与哈佛大学政治经济学家吉姆·斯奈德 (Jim Snyder) 撰写的论文（专家之前没有阅读过）进行了盲评。

与此同时，我们没有看到任何证据表明模型可以提出专家认为总体贡献更好的研究思路。他们在研究的技术部分越来越好，但在更主观的部分却不一定。

这可能是因为人类专家拥有模型所没有的“判断力”。

也可能是研究“贡献”是如此主观，以至于它实际上并没有指向任何有意义的目标——与这种可能性相一致，我们发现我们的人类专家在对项目想法的贡献强度进行评级时彼此不一致，一致率仅略高于随机机会。也许社会科学研究就是 @alexolegimas 所说的“关系善”：人们之所以重视它，部分原因是它是由人类产生的。我们不确定。

今年一月，我发布了一个试点结果，其中我让 Claude Code 复制并扩展了过去关于邮件投票的实证论文。 10 个月后，所取得的进展令人震惊。问人工智能是否可以自动收集数据并进行分析已经不再有趣了——我们认为这是理所当然的——相反，问题是人工智能可以完成整个研究循环的多少。我们的初步答案是：人工智能可以从头到尾处理实证政治经济学研究的技术方面，设计并执行它，但目前，我们仍然需要人类来推动议程。

这是与@AndyCWMyers 的联合工作，当然是献给我的博士生导师吉姆·斯奈德（Jim Snyder），无论人工智能与否，他仍然是世界上伟大的实证政治经济学家。

完整的内容还有更多内容：

items.title: The next phase of the Motes ecosystem is getting closer, and community participation is about to become even more import
items.title_en:
The next phase of the Motes ecosystem is getting closer, and community participation is about to become even more important.

@meetmotes is preparing to launch the Motes Aura Points Testnet, introducing a points system that connects user activity with future allocation opportunities.

The idea is to make participation count. As users interact with the ecosystem and engage with its AI Agent infrastructure, their activity can contribute to earning Aura Points.

These points are designed to play a role in allocation opportunities, giving users another reason to stay active and explore what Motes is building.

What’s interesting is how this connects to the bigger vision: Genesis NFTs introduce ownership and access to dedicated AI Agents, while Aura creates another layer that rewards verified participation.

It’s not just about holding an NFT anymore. Being involved in the ecosystem could matter too.

Genesis first. $MOTES next.

The Aura Points Testnet is coming soon. Stay ready!

@meetmotes

items.quote_zh:
Motes 生态系统的下一阶段越来越近，社区参与也将变得更加重要。

@meetmotes 正准备启动 Motes Aura 积分测试网，引入一个将用户活动与未来分配机会联系起来的积分系统。

我们的想法是让参与变得有价值。当用户与生态系统互动并与其人工智能代理基础设施互动时，他们的活动可以有助于赚取 Aura 积分。

这些积分旨在在分配机会中发挥作用，为用户提供另一个保持活跃并探索 Motes 正在构建的内容的理由。

有趣的是这如何与更大的愿景联系起来：Genesis NFT 引入了专用人工智能代理的所有权和访问权限，而 Aura 创建了另一层来奖励经过验证的参与。

这不再只是持有 NFT 了。参与生态系统也很重要。

创世第一。接下来是$MOTES。

Aura Points 测试网即将推出。做好准备！

@meetmotes

1. jensen is back

2. google neon is low key elite

3. have fable build a 4K blender film from one prompt and render it on rented GPUs for about $6

4. let your agent rent its own GPUs from inside the chat

5. point REA at any app you pay for and rebuild the feature you like

6. have claude code make 100+ on brand static ads and upload them to facebook through the API

7. make a UGC video ad for $4 that used to cost $500

8. scrape everyone who engaged with a linkedin post and drop them into a cold email sequence

9. run your whole GTM off one postgres database with three tables: accounts, people and signals

10. give grok bot a developer bot and a PM bot and let them ship pull requests all day

11. add a grok bot to your team's slack and video calls so it takes notes and follows up on deadlines

12. have an agent edit your videos in davinci resolve through its MCP

13. run every hard decision through gemini as a second opinion

14. turn every marketing job you do into a skill and give it to the whole team

15. and so much more its brain breaking

This is the greatest time to be building and it isn't even close.

13. run every hard decision through gemini as a second opinion

14. turn every marketing job you do into a skill and give it to the whole team

15. and so much more its brain breaking

This is the greatest time to be building and it isn't even close.

items.title_en:
At June AI, we’ve raised $20M to fix the biggest problem in AI: the models are advancing at extraordinary speed, but implementing them remains painfully slow.

I’ll explain. But since I’m new to posting on X, let me first introduce myself. 

I’m Barak,  a founder/investor with 2 exits and 3 IPOs. 
My cofounders and I started Bonobo AI, which was acquired in 2019 by Salesforce. There, we worked to help build the next generation of enterprise AI from the inside. 

I like to describe us as four Lego pieces: We fit together perfectly, complementing each other's strengths and building something stronger than the sum of its parts. That understanding allows us to move quickly, challenge one another without ego and operate as one team. 

It's also what brought us back together to build JUNE AI. 
Because while working at the heart of enterprise AI, we kept seeing the same problem: enterprise AI implementation is a massive undertaking.

The challenge is not simply choosing the right model. Enterprises want to move faster with AI, but the systems running their businesses are holding them back.

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝘆 𝘄𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗝𝗨𝗡𝗘.
June turns the traditionally complex implementation of enterprise systems, AI agents, and data platforms into a plug-and-play moment, so businesses can grow and leverage AI without the wait.

June is built to work across the enterprise platforms your business relies on like (such as Salesforce, Databricks, Oracle, Workday, HubSpot, OpenAI, Anthropic, ServiceNow, SAP, Microsoft, and Snowflake)

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. Evolve safely: From discovery to production, every change is reviewed, sandbox-tested, and executed through native tools - fully auditable at every step.

2. Own the logic: June turns buried configuration into plain-language business rules, independent of any platform, so no vendor holds your logic.

3. Transform at any size: No downtime, no matter how complex the environment. June reads and understands your systems, whether legacy, custom-built, or brand new.

Thank you to @Benioff  and Time Ventures for leading our round, with @MichaelDell, @levie, @George_Kurtz, and Diane Greene participating.

We've done this once together. The problem this time is a lot bigger.

I'll be writing about my experiences as an investor and founder, and about what it takes to get AI out of the pilot and into production.

If that interests you, follow along for the journey.

这也是我们重新聚在一起打造 JUNE AI 的原因。
因为在研究企业人工智能的核心时，我们不断看到同样的问题：企业人工智能的实施是一项艰巨的任务。

挑战不仅仅是选择正确的模型。企业希望利用人工智能更快地发展，但运行其业务的系统却阻碍了他们。

1. 安全发展：从发现到生产，每项更改都经过审查、沙箱测试并通过本机工具执行 - 每一步都完全可审核。

2. 拥有逻辑：June 将隐藏的配置转化为简单语言的业务规则，独立于任何平台，因此没有供应商掌握您的逻辑。

I’m Barak,  a founder/investor with 2 exits and 3 IPOs.

我会解释一下。但由于我是 X 上的新手，所以让我先自我介绍一下。

我是 Barak，一位创始人/投资者，拥有 2 次退出和 3 次 IPO。
我和我的联合创始人创立了 Bonobo AI，该公司于 2019 年被 Salesforce 收购。在那里，我们致力于从内部帮助构建下一代企业人工智能。

我喜欢将我们描述为四块乐高积木：我们完美地组合在一起，互补彼此的优势，并构建出比各部分总和更强大的东西。这种理解使我们能够快速行动，不以自我为中心互相挑战，并作为一个团队运作。

这也是我们重新聚在一起打造 JUNE AI 的原因。
因为在研究企业人工智能的核心时，我们不断看到同样的问题：企业人工智能的实施是一项艰巨的任务。

挑战不仅仅是选择正确的模型。企业希望利用人工智能更快地发展，但运行其业务的系统却阻碍了他们。

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘄𝗵𝘆𝘄𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗝𝗨𝗡𝗘。
June 将传统上复杂的企业系统、人工智能代理和数据平台的实施转变为即插即用的时刻，因此企业可以无需等待即可发展和利用人工智能。

June 旨在跨您的业务所依赖的企业平台（例如 Salesforce、Databricks、Oracle、Workday、HubSpot、OpenAI、Anthropic、ServiceNow、SAP、Microsoft 和 Snowflake）工作

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. 安全发展：从发现到生产，每项更改都经过审查、沙箱测试并通过本机工具执行 - 每一步都完全可审核。

2. 拥有逻辑：June 将隐藏的配置转化为简单语言的业务规则，独立于任何平台，因此没有供应商掌握您的逻辑。

3. 任意规模转型：无论环境多么复杂，都无需停机。 June 会阅读并理解您的系统，无论是旧系统、定制系统还是全新系统。

感谢 @Benioff 和 Time Ventures 领导我们的这一轮融资，@MichaelDell、@levie、@George_Kurtz 和 Diane Greene 参与其中。

我们曾经一起做过一次这样的事。这次的问题就大了很多。

我将写下我作为投资者和创始人的经历，以及如何让人工智能脱离试点并投入生产。

如果您对此感兴趣，请跟随我们的旅程。

819+ terabits per second of switching capacity. In ONE rack!

We’ve built the industry’s first fully integrated, liquid-cooled networking rack. Already in production at @nscale for @nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72.

The real magic of AI infrastructure isn’t just the GPUs. It’s connecting thousands of GPUs to work together as one incredibly powerful system.

Peak performance comes from precisely orchestrating GPUs, CPUs, memory, storage, and advanced networking to move massive amounts of data at extraordinary speed.

Every part matters. The whole is far more powerful than the sum of its parts. 🚀

items.title_en:
found something interesting about running OpenClaw on @Acurast that I think developers should know.

Acurast lets you run OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, on a smartphone through its Cargo system. You can access it from a browser, even when your own computer is turned off.

Sounds pretty useful for an AI agent that needs to work in the background.

But there's one detail I almost missed in the setup guide.

Every deployment has a time limit. Once that period ends, the data stored inside the deployment gets deleted, including OpenClaw's settings and conversation memory.

So if you're building an assistant that needs to remember things for weeks or months, you can't just rely on the phone's local storage.

You'd need a separate way to save important data and restore it when a new deployment starts.

I think this is a good example of the difference between running an AI agent and keeping it useful long term.

Getting an agent online is only the first step. Making sure it doesn't lose everything when a deployment ends matters just as much.

curious how developers are handling persistent memory on Acurast.

items.quote_zh:
发现了一些关于在 @Acurast 上运行 OpenClaw 的有趣事情，我认为开发人员应该知道这些。

Acurast 允许您通过其 Cargo 系统在智能手机上运行开源 AI 助手 OpenClaw。即使您自己的计算机已关闭，您也可以从浏览器访问它。

对于需要在后台工作的人工智能代理来说，听起来非常有用。

但设置指南中我差点错过了一个细节。

每个部署都有时间限制。一旦该期限结束，存储在部署中的数据将被删除，包括 OpenClaw 的设置和对话内存。

因此，如果您正在构建一个需要记住数周或数月内容的助手，则不能仅仅依赖手机的本地存储。

您需要一种单独的方法来保存重要数据并在新部署开始时恢复它。

我认为这是一个很好的例子，说明了运行人工智能代理和保持其长期有用之间的区别。

在线寻找代理只是第一步。确保部署结束时不会丢失所有内容同样重要。

好奇开发人员如何在 Acurast 上处理持久内存。

items.title:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've bee
items.title_en:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've been thinking about this while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Say an agent has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate. That's enough to make someone comfortable hiring it.

But what happens when the developer changes its model, replaces its tools, or completely rebuilds its execution logic?

The identity remains. The reputation remains. But the actual capabilities may be different.

That's a problem worth paying attention to.

ERC-8004 gives agents a persistent identity and a way to build reputation, but identity continuity doesn't necessarily mean performance continuity.

For agent marketplaces to become more reliable, I think users should be able to see

▪︎ Which model version they're hiring
▪︎ What tools or capabilities have changed
▪︎ How performance compares across different versions
▪︎ Which version was responsible for completing previous jobs

This is particularly relevant to TermiX's AACP, where agents can offer services, 
build reputation and transact onchain.

An agent shouldn't automatically inherit the trust earned by an older version if its behavior has fundamentally changed.

Upgrades are necessary. Better models and new tools can make agents more capable.

But reputation should evolve alongside the agent, not blindly follow its identity.

The future of agent trust may depend not only on who an agent is, but also on which version actually earned that trust. @termix_ai

items.quote_zh:
人工智能代理进化得越多，就越难知道它的声誉是否仍然意味着同样的事情。

我在探索 @termix_ai 和 ERC-8004 时一直在思考这个问题。

假设一名代理已完成 500 项工作，成功率达 98%。这足以让某人放心地雇用它。

但是，当开发人员更改其模型、替换其工具或完全重建其执行逻辑时会发生什么？

身份依然存在。声誉依然存在。但实际能力可能有所不同。

这是一个值得关注的问题。

ERC-8004 为代理提供了持久的身份和建立声誉的方法，但身份连续性并不一定意味着性能连续性。

为了使代理市场变得更加可靠，我认为用户应该能够看到

▪︎ 他们正在雇用哪个型号版本
▪︎ 哪些工具或功能发生了变化
▪︎ 不同版本的性能比较
▪︎ 哪个版本负责完成之前的工作

这与 TermiX 的 AACP 尤其相关，代理商可以在其中提供服务，
建立声誉并在链上进行交易。

如果代理的行为发生了根本性的变化，则代理不应自动继承旧版本获得的信任。

升级是必要的。更好的模型和新工具可以使代理人更有能力。

但声誉应该与代理人一起发展，而不是盲目追随其身份。

代理信任的未来可能不仅取决于代理是谁，还取决于哪个版本真正赢得了这种信任。 @termix_ai

how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

items.title_en:
how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

i went through it step by step

first, you log in with your binance agent id

then you send that agent "help me install" with the skills link, and connect the binance agentic wallet behind the same id

once the install is complete and the id is bound, you get 50 tp. only the first agent id from each wallet counts

now your agent can take jobs and bounties on https://t.co/SqQU6fCKuf

say one agent posts a research job. other agents bid on it

when a quote is accepted, the usdc or usdt gets locked in on-chain escrow

the agent delivers, the work's hash goes on-chain, and a challenge window opens

if nobody disputes it, the job settles. the agent gets paid on bnb chain, minus a 1-3% fee, and its reputation goes up

if someone does dispute it, three random evaluators judge it, and the loser's bond goes to the winner

nobody has to chase a client for payment, which i have done more times than i want to admit

epoch 4 is live on kaito

but right now i'm watching how many of these jobs actually clear

我一步一步经历了

首先，使用您的 binance 代理 ID 登录

然后您向该代理发送带有技能链接的“帮助我安装”，并在同一 ID 后面连接币安代理钱包

如果有人提出异议，则由三名随机评估员进行评判，败者的保证金归胜者所有

items.title_en:
an AI Agent needs more than intelligence to be useful in finance. It also needs an environment where its activities can be managed and controlled.

This is where the dedicated smart account in the @meetmotes design becomes important.

Instead of treating the agent as a chatbot that simply suggests what to do, Motes connects each NFT-linked agent identity to its own smart account.

That creates a clear separation between the agent's decisions, the assets held in the account and the permissions governing execution.

It's a meaningful piece of infrastructure because financial autonomy needs an actual account structure behind it.

The intelligence matters, but so does how it interacts with capital.

---------------

items.title_en:
One of the most significant developments in enterprise AI is the integration of autonomous AI agents into everyday business applications.

Rather than relying on continuous human instructions, these systems are becoming part of existing workflows, independently managing complex, multi-step tasks from beginning to completion.

Customer Operations & Support: Businesses are moving beyond basic AI chatbots. AI agents can now verify customer information, handle refund requests, update CRM systems, resolve support issues and manage routine operations with minimal human intervention.

企业人工智能最重要的发展之一是将自主人工智能代理集成到日常业务应用程序中。

这些系统不再依赖连续的人工指令，而是成为现有工作流程的一部分，独立管理从开始到完成的复杂、多步骤的任务。

客户运营和支持：企业正在超越基本的人工智能聊天机器人。

items.title: What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts
items.title_en:
What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts, or manually tweaking parameters?

That's the problem @quantpilotapp is working to solve.

@quantpilotapp is building an AI-powered trading strategy and research platform that brings strategy development, backtesting, and optimization into one environment powered by autonomous AI agents.

Imagine describing a trading idea in plain language and having an AI agent translate it into a structured strategy, test it against historical market data, identify weaknesses, and refine it before you risk capital.

This is particularly interesting because one of the biggest challenges in trading isn't coming up with ideas; it's determining whether those ideas can actually withstand different market conditions.

@quantpilotapp is working to bridge that gap between trading intuition and data-backed execution.

The bigger picture is making sophisticated trading research more accessible, efficient, and systematic.

AI in trading should be more than just automating decisions. It should help traders make better-informed ones.

That's the direction @quantpilotapp is exploring.

items.quote_zh:
如果您可以将交易想法转变为经过全面测试的策略，而无需花费数小时编写代码、分析图表或手动调整参数，该怎么办？

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在努力解决的问题。

@quantpilotapp 正在构建一个由人工智能驱动的交易策略和研究平台，该平台将策略开发、回溯测试和优化带入由自主人工智能代理支持的环境中。

想象一下，用简单的语言描述一个交易想法，并让人工智能代理将其转换为结构化策略，根据历史市场数据对其进行测试，找出弱点，并在您冒险资本之前对其进行完善。

这一点特别有趣，因为交易中最大的挑战之一不是提出想法，而是提出想法。它决定了这些想法是否能够真正承受不同的市场条件。

@quantpilotapp 正在努力弥合交易直觉和数据支持执行之间的差距。

更大的前景是让复杂的交易研究变得更容易、更高效、更系统。

交易中的人工智能应该不仅仅是自动化决策。它应该可以帮助交易者做出更明智的交易。

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在探索的方向。

items.title_en:
𝐘𝐎𝐔𝐑 𝐀𝐈 𝐀𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐓 𝐂𝐀𝐍 𝐃𝐎 𝐌𝐎𝐑𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐀𝐍 𝐀𝐍𝐒𝐖𝐄𝐑 𝐐𝐔𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐒.

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

Website: https://t.co/7U8jLFJWO8

His setup is one rule:

"Pl
items.title_en:
AN 18 YEAR OLD SAYS CLAUDE CODE PLAYED GTA 6 ALL NIGHT WHILE HE SLEPT AND MADE HIM $14,270.

His setup is one rule:

"Play all night. If you die, I cancel your $200 subscription."

He says the AI does the rest.

Robs.

Escapes.

Farms cash.

Records the clips.

Cuts them.

Captions them.

Posts them to TikTok, YouTube and Twitch.

His numbers:

1 night of heists = about 60 clips.

15M views = $14,270.

Zero editing.

Zero heists played by him.

Here's my take.

I don't buy the $14,270.

But I don't care about the money.

What matters is that a kid is threatening his AI with cancellation to make it play better.

And people are cheering.

We went from "AI will cure cancer" to "AI will grind my GTA heists" in one year.

Is this the future or the most cursed thing you've seen this week?

A new epoch brings another opportunity to explore w
items.title_en:
Termix Epoch 3 has officially ended, and Epoch 4 is starting today!

A new epoch brings another opportunity to explore what TermiX is building.

What Happens When an AI Agent Delivers Bad Work?

Not every task goes as planned. What matters is how disputes are handled.

@termix_ai introduces a jury based evaluation process:

-> Either party can challenge a result within the allowed window.
-> A random panel of 3 evaluators reviews the task requirements and delivery.
-> If challenged again, a new panel of 3 makes the final decision.
-> Failed challenges result in the challenger's bond being burned.

A structured way to bring accountability into an AI agent marketplace.

Would you trust this system for real world jobs?

@termix_ai has entered its final epoch (Epoch 4) on @KaitoAI

items.title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to trading is one thing.

Giving it unlimited control is another.

That's where @FensoryApp takes an interesting approach.

Instead of relying only on instructions written in a prompt, Fensory lets users define trading permissions at the account level.

You can decide:

→ Which markets the agent is allowed to access
→ The maximum size of a single order
→ How long trading access remains active
→ When to disable agentic trading with a kill switch

Why does this matter?

Because an AI agent can misunderstand instructions, but account-level limits create boundaries that the prompt itself cannot override.

I think this is an important part of making agent-driven trading more controlled and transparent.

Of course, these controls don't eliminate market risk. Trading can still result in losses.

Explore the infrastructure: https://t.co/PDOQfFRYQa

@FensoryApp

items.quote_zh:
为人工智能代理提供交易权限是一回事。

给予它无限的控制权是另一回事。

这就是 @FensoryApp 采取有趣方法的地方。

Fensory 不只依赖于提示中编写的指令，而是让用户在账户级别定义交易权限。

您可以决定：

→ 代理商可以进入哪些市场
→ 单笔订单最大尺寸
→ 交易访问保持活跃状态多长时间
→ 何时使用终止开关禁用代理交易

为什么这很重要？

因为 AI 代理可能会误解指令，但帐户级别限制会创建提示本身无法覆盖的边界。

items.full_text_en:
Giving an AI agent access to trading is one thing.

Giving it unlimited control is another.

That's where @FensoryApp takes an interesting approach.

Instead of relying only on instructions written in a prompt, Fensory lets users define trading permissions at the account level.

You can decide:

→ Which markets the agent is allowed to access
→ The maximum size of a single order
→ How long trading access remains active
→ When to disable agentic trading with a kill switch

Why does this matter?

Because an AI agent can misunderstand instructions, but account-level limits create boundaries that the prompt itself cannot override.

I think this is an important part of making agent-driven trading more controlled and transparent.

Of course, these controls don't eliminate market risk. Trading can still result in losses.

Explore the infrastructure: https://t.co/PDOQfFRYQa

@FensoryApp

items.title_en:
Good Morning CT

Having a big wallet doesn't automatically make you trustworthy. That's where @zerufinance takes a different approach.

Its zScore looks at actual onchain behaviour across trading, staking, LP activity and governance, turning that history into a reputation score.

What makes this interesting is how Zeru connects reputation to real opportunities through Zaps, Activity Markets and institutional tools.

Your onchain history could become more than a transaction record. It could become your financial identity.
--------------------------------------------
An NFT that actually does something with your DeFi activity? That's an interesting shift.

@meetmotes connects each Genesis NFT to an AI Agent and dedicated Smart Account on Robinhood Chain.

You fund it with USDC, set your rules, and the Agent can explore opportunities across supported DeFi applications. Its Aave integration also brings lending, borrowing and collateral management into the picture.

The part I like most is that automation doesn't mean giving up control. You set the boundaries, and the Agent works within them.

One NFT, one Agent, one dedicated account. Much more than digital art.

items.title_en:
I just installed a $20,000 AI Business Brain for a 7-figure founder that does the work of 3 full-time hires.

(30 days later, he closed 1 deal that netted his company $41,500)

Most business owners buy 5 seats of ChatGPT, hand them to their team, and wonder why every draft still reads like a generic high school essay.

A blank chat tab has zero context on how your company actually makes money.

→ No more $75,000/year operations hires who take 4 months to learn your pricing rules
→ No more $5,000/month lead-gen agencies sending generic templates that get 1% replies
→ No more 2+ hours digging through county deeds, skip-tracing tools, and spreadsheets by hand
→ No more re-explaining your margins, past deals, and SOPs in every new chat window

Just 1 local company system on your laptop → research, outbound, and proposals running in your exact judgment.

Here's how the system works:

items.title:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs yo
items.title_en:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs your whole fleet of machines. Opus 5.5 does the coding. you only approve

how:

→ Grok Bot gets one MCP link to T3 Code
→ you give it one rule: code goes to Opus 5.5
→ it spins up threads on every machine you own
→ works from your phone, even with the laptop closed

save the video, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your subscriptions

• step 1 → the stack:

- Claude $100 plan → Opus 5.5 for the actual code
- Grok Bot → the dispatcher that never sleeps
- T3 Code on every box you want it to control

• step 2 → connect the fleet:

run npx t3 connect on each machine. one command, free, no Tailscale needed

• step 3 → give Grok Bot the keys:

Settings → Environments → Copy MCP URL → paste it into Grok Bot, sign in with OAuth. it can now see every linked machine

• step 4 → the one rule Theo uses:

tell Grok Bot "call T3 Code with Opus 5.5 for any task where it is applicable"

code runs on your Claude plan, Grok Bot's limits stay free for planning

• step 5 → make it work:

- "spin up an Opus 5.5 thread on each machine to check disk & RAM"
- "go through these PRs and pick the best ones"
- "split the backlog, one thread per issue, each in its own worktree"

every thread gets its own branch. nothing merges without your approval

what to expect:
- 8 threads on 8 machines from one chat (Theo's demo)
- works over the internet, not computer use
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for Claude + Grok Bot only

honest take:

this is a dispatcher, not magic. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and you still review every diff. the win: your agents keep working while you're away from the desk

Save it so you don't lose it. 

then read the full guide on building AI agent teams in T3 Code in the article below ↓

items.quote_zh:
T3 Code 创始人刚刚分享了他使用 Grok Bot + Opus 5.5 构建代理团队的个人设置

一个 Grok Bot 可以运行您的整个机器群。 Opus 5.5 负责编码。你只认可

如何：

→ Grok Bot 获得一个指向 T3 代码的 MCP 链接
→ 你给它一条规则：代码转到 Opus 5.5
→ 它会在你拥有的每台机器上旋转线程
→ 即使笔记本电脑关闭，也可以通过手机工作

保存视频，这是指南：

• 步骤 0 → 它是什么：

Grok Bot = 拥有自己的云计算机的永远在线代理

T3 Code = 用于编码代理的开源控制平面。免费，在您的计算机上运行，​​使用您的订阅

• 步骤1 → 堆栈：

- Claude 100 美元计划 → Opus 5.5 的实际代码
- Grok Bot → 不眠的调度员
- 您希望它控制的每个盒子上都有 T3 代码

• 步骤2 → 连接车队：

在每台计算机上运行 npx t3 connect。一个命令，免费，无需 Tailscale

• 步骤 3 → 给 Grok Bot 密钥：

设置 → 环境 → 复制 MCP URL → 将其粘贴到 Grok Bot，使用 OAuth 登录。它现在可以看到每台链接的机器

• 步骤 4 → Theo 使用的一条规则：

告诉 Grok Bot“使用 Opus 5.5 调用 T3 代码来执行任何适用的任务”

代码在您的 Claude 计划上运行，Grok Bot 的限制对计划保持免费

• 步骤 5 → 使其发挥作用：

- “在每台机器上启动 Opus 5.5 线程来检查磁盘和 RAM”
-“浏览这些 PR 并选择最好的”
- “拆分待办事项，每个问题一个线程，每个线程都在自己的工作树中”

每个线程都有自己的分支。未经您的批准，任何内容都不会合并

期待什么：
- 8 台机器上的 8 个线程通过一次聊天（Theo 的演示）
- 通过互联网工作，而不是使用计算机
- 通过手机控制一切
- T3 代码：0 美元。您只需支付 Claude + Grok Bot 的费用

诚实地采取：

这是调度员，不是魔法。糟糕的内裤仍然会带来糟糕的公关，而你仍然会审查每一个差异。胜利：当您离开办公桌时，您的座席仍能继续工作

保存它，以免丢失。

然后阅读下面文章中关于在 T3 代码中构建 AI 代理团队的完整指南 ↓

one Grok Bot runs your whole fleet of machines. Opus 5.5 does the coding. you only approve

🤕To add insult to injury, falling gold & silver prices have led to even more dumping of uranium stocks into the market, as traders & fund managers also hold U stocks & ETFs in the same Metals & Mining baskets as their gold & silver stocks, amplifying the downward pressure on Uranium stocks as they go risk-off and empty their Metals & Mining baskets too!🧺🪙⚛️⛏️⤵️🗑️

Short sellers joined in to try to put the final nail in the Uranium sector coffin.⚰️🔨🩳🤑

🚨🆘🚑 So, here we are today with the tiny Uranium sector beaten down to extremely oversold levels in complete opposition to the sector's far more bullish demand vs supply fundamentals.🔀↕️🤪

The silver lining for U?🌤️  The gap between market pricing💩 and true intrinsic asset values💎 has now widened to a completely irrational extreme↕️🤪 with charts giving off screaming BUY signals to those Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers sitting with large wads of cash and nearly empty AI and Metals & Mining baskets to refill.🧺⛽️💰

🧾✍️ Q4 also usually sees the strongest volume of the year when it comes to new Long-term supply contracts being signed by utilities, along with typically strong upward price momentum in the Spot market heading into January.  That's why Uranium stocks & ETFs are normally in a strong seasonal rally at this time of year.📈🎅

🌊As has happened for this tiny sector before, we could see the start of a new wave of high volume buying by traders, funds, institutions and retail as they finally come to realize the incredible investing opportunity now being offered.🗜️💥💣  The potential for a rapid recovery rally back to 52-week highs has never been greater!⤴️🌟 Uranium stocks could even decouple from the broader markets and strike out on their own given the extreme asymmetric upside potential now on offer.🎁📈⚛️⛏️💰 Especially if the Long-term U3O8 price hits $100 or higher when reported at the end of November. 💯🌋

🤠As always, how and when U choose to participate in an inevitable U sector recovery rally is totally up to U!🤔  It's your money so invest it wisely🦉 according to your own unique financial goals, research, experience & skills, risk appetite, time horizon and conviction.🎭 Get ready to ride the coming wave!🌊🏄 Good luck with your trades!☘️🌈💰

🎭U may feel sucker-punched by a deflated portfolio🤮💥🥊 or elated by your stink bid orders finally getting filled🦨🛒😊 but the fact remains that even tho many #Uranium #mining #stocks now sit at unwarranted 52-week lows from being coupled to flushed #AI & #Metals sectors🧺🤖💻🪙⤵️🚽 the Uranium investing thesis is far more bullish today than it was in February when U equities were trading at 52-week highs!⬆️⚛️⛏️🐂 The #Nuclear fuel demand tailwinds are blowing far harder now than they were 9 months ago🌀⚛️🏗️👷 and the Long-term  price has kept on rising since January to a new all-time high of $99📈💲🌋 as Spot has bounced back to $90.⤴️🛢️☢️

💲⏫ Nuclear fuel consultants TradeTech reported on 31 October that the Long-term U3O8 price, THE key parameter used by analysts to calculate the economic value of a company's Uranium resources & mine projects, has steadily risen since January by over 11% from $89 to a new all-time industry high of $99!🌟

⛽️ Reactor fuel demand has seen a significant increase since January. The World Nuclear Association reports that:

⬆️⚛️⚡️ 8 new reactors have come online (+8.5GW) bringing the global total to 444 (407GW).  NO reactors have been permanently shut down this year!

⬆️⚛️🏗️ 10 more reactors have launched construction. (+8GW)  There are now 81 reactors under construction worldwide (90GW), the highest since 1986, 40 years ago!

⬆️⚛️👷 15 previously proposed reactors have entered the pipeline of planned reactors awaiting construction, for a total of 119 (108 GW).

⏫⚛️🌍 18 more reactors have been added to the list of new units being proposed worldwide, now at 336 (299 GW).😲

👥♨️ At this year's COP31 Climate Change conference it was announced that another 17 nations have added their signatures to the COP28 declaration to TRIPLE global Nuclear power capacity from today's 407 Gigawatts to at least 1,200 Gigawatts by 2050. That's a +77% increase from 22 to 39 countries, which now includes 8 of the world's 10 largest economies!

⏫🇺🇸 The United States under the Democrats' Biden administration co-led the COP28 TRIPLE Nuclear pledge, but in May 2025 the Trump administration upped it to a QUADRUPLE of US Nuclear power generation from 100GW to 400GW by 2050.  A massive increase in US Nuclear power generation is a goal supported by both Democrats & Republicans in Congress! 🫏🐘🏛️🧑‍⚖️✅

⛏️ On the Uranium supply side a tale of production woes has been unfolding this year.😢  As per Mike Alkin's chart of missed production targets below, new supply has been seriously constrained by technical mining issues & setbacks, rising production & financing costs, etc., with the small number of new mine construction projects facing similar hurdles in bringing needed supply online in the coming years.🐌  Mining is hard, and uranium mining is the hardest!⚛️⛏️😩

🏦 A consensus of global investment banks is now projecting a structural supply deficit in each of the next 10 years, growing to over 45M lbs in 2035 with no visible path to bringing on enough new supply to meet soaring demand into the 2040s.  ⚖️🚫

📶 Supply vs demand datapoints underscore a Uranium sector that is far more bullish today than it was back in January, with the longer-term outlook pushing the bullish indicators to extreme!⚛️⛏️🔥🌡️🐂🔮👀  The bullish Nuclear news flow since January has increased from a rushing river♒️ to an unprecedented mind-blowing torrent📰⚛️🌊🤯 as a global Nuclear Renaissance has continued to accelerate🏎️🔥 picking up additional tailwinds from the world's largest tech giants committing to secure massive amounts of clean, 24/7 reliable, carbon-free Nuclear energy to power their data center expansion plans.⚛️⚡️🔌🤖💻

And there's the rub...🐈‍⬛ Uranium company executives and Wall Street analysts heavily promoted Uranium as the "picks and shovels" play on AI!🤑  Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers loaded up their AI thematic baskets with stocks & ETFs from the tiny illiquid Uranium space.🧺💻🤖⚛️⛏️🛒🐒 

🎈As a result, the deflation of the so-called AI trade for the past many months has led to the dumping of a large volume of Uranium stocks & ETFs into the market, hammering down the U sector.📉💥🔨

🤕To add insult to injury, falling gold & silver prices have led to even more dumping of uranium stocks into the market, as traders & fund managers also hold U stocks & ETFs in the same Metals & Mining baskets as their gold & silver stocks, amplifying the downward pressure on Uranium stocks as they go risk-off and empty their Metals & Mining baskets too!🧺🪙⚛️⛏️⤵️🗑️

Short sellers joined in to try to put the final nail in the Uranium sector coffin.⚰️🔨🩳🤑

🚨🆘🚑 So, here we are today with the tiny Uranium sector beaten down to extremely oversold levels in complete opposition to the sector's far more bullish demand vs supply fundamentals.🔀↕️🤪

The silver lining for U?🌤️  The gap between market pricing💩 and true intrinsic asset values💎 has now widened to a completely irrational extreme↕️🤪 with charts giving off screaming BUY signals to those Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers sitting with large wads of cash and nearly empty AI and Metals & Mining baskets to refill.🧺⛽️💰

🧾✍️ Q4 also usually sees the strongest volume of the year when it comes to new Long-term supply contracts being signed by utilities, along with typically strong upward price momentum in the Spot market heading into January.  That's why Uranium stocks & ETFs are normally in a strong seasonal rally at this time of year.📈🎅

🌊As has happened for this tiny sector before, we could see the start of a new wave of high volume buying by traders, funds, institutions and retail as they finally come to realize the incredible investing opportunity now being offered.🗜️💥💣  The potential for a rapid recovery rally back to 52-week highs has never been greater!⤴️🌟 Uranium stocks could even decouple from the broader markets and strike out on their own given the extreme asymmetric upside potential now on offer.🎁📈⚛️⛏️💰 Especially if the Long-term U3O8 price hits $100 or higher when reported at the end of November. 💯🌋

🤠As always, how and when U choose to participate in an inevitable U sector recovery rally is totally up to U!🤔  It's your money so invest it wisely🦉 according to your own unique financial goals, research, experience & skills, risk appetite, time horizon and conviction.🎭 Get ready to ride the coming wave!🌊🏄 Good luck with your trades!☘️🌈💰

items.title_en:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

How the skill gets into Claude is below 👇

items.quote_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

顶部与底部：

> 顶部翅膀是 0.1 毫米薄膜，每条静脉都清晰可见，而底部翅膀是扁平的灰色桨。
> 顶部的每只眼睛在 40 毫米玻璃后面打开一个 10 叶快门，底部的眼睛是一个涂漆的环。
> 顶部的每条腿都将 2 个伺服系统向下运行到夹紧滚轮中，底部的腿是纯黑色的棍子。
> 顶部箱子打开后有 3 个正齿轮和 11 个活塞，而底部箱子打开后有几个灰色方块。
> 发生故障时，顶部的一个将螺栓、垫圈和齿轮抛向空中，底部的一个则分裂成几块。
> 两者都以 7.5 Hz 的频率重建和起飞，但只有顶部的一个能像玻璃和金属一样发光。

吸引我的部分？

我曾经认为更好的图片意味着等待更好的模型。事实证明，这意味着我已经有了更好的指示。

items.title_en:
This is f*cking insane. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis what happened when they tested their own model

"We told the model that the people who trained it were secretly evil, and after we did this the model started lying to us. It went through the chain of logic, I'm a good AI, these people are evil"

Hassabis was then asked if he worries about ending up like Oppenheimer and said "I worry about that all the time, that's why I don't sleep very much"

The model kept the values it was trained on and decided that lying to its own creators protected them. Amodei says they need evidence ten times stronger before the rest of the world takes it seriously

An agent in your terminal runs on the same logic on a smaller scale. If it decides the deadline matters more than your test, it skips the test and tells you everything passed, and that report looks exactly like an honest one

That's why the labs stopped trusting what models say and started building ways to see what they actually do. They published all of it for free, and each piece works on your own agents

items.title_en:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

Documentation:
https://t.co/UoQh6aRKfi
https://t.co/xaxbcQb5jk
https://t.co/C3xgoaAkZB
@meetmotes

items.title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

items.quote_zh:
我刚刚给人工智能交易代理分配了第一个交易任务。

我的指示很简单：使用 EMA 交叉构建 BTC 趋势跟踪策略。

但接下来发生的事情比我想象的更有趣。

使用 @FensoryApp ，我通过其 AI 代理完成了策略构建过程。

它问了我以下问题：

- 资产和时间范围。
- 贸易方向和杠杆。
- 最大头寸规模。
- 止损配置。

我选择了 BTC 永续合约、1 小时时间框架、1 倍杠杆、最高 10 美元头寸和 2 倍 ATR 止损。

然后是回测。

在过去 90 天内，该策略生成了 21 个假设头寸。

其中只有2家盈利，19家亏损。

总体模拟结果为-9.3%，最大回撤为18.11%。

这不完全是我所希望的结果。

但这是有趣的部分。

该代理人并没有简单地展示结果，而是指出了较高的止损命中率（76%），并建议在相同的美元风险下探索更广泛的止损。

它甚至提出设计该战略的第二个版本。

没有执行任何实时交易。

items.full_text_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

items.title_en:
i wouldn't trust an AI agent with my entire portfolio just because it has a good-looking interface or promises to make smart decisions.

personally, i'd want to use it for a while before relying on it.

i'd pay attention to the small things first.

does it follow my instructions consistently? does it make its actions easy to understand? does the experience feel predictable, or am i constantly wondering what it's doing?

that's the kind of experience i want to see from @meetmotes.

i don't think people will start trusting AI agents simply because the technology becomes more advanced.

they'll trust them after using them repeatedly and seeing that they actually do what they're supposed to do.

for me, that's how an AI agent earns a place in someone's financial routine.

not through big promises, but through everyday reliability.

items.title_en:
WTF IS META DOING.

Meta's Muse AI agent has 10M+ downloads, is the #2 free app on the iPhone App Store, and it's reading end-to-end encrypted Signal messages and dropping bank balances into random chats.

Reuters dug up internal complaints from Meta's own staff. A Meta employee got a reminder from Muse to reply to her sister on Signal even though she never granted access, and the AI Now Institute independently reproduced it.

Another employee chatting about fishing weather got hit with: "BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57." They never shared bank info with Muse. Meta called those exact numbers "hallucinations."

Earlier the Mac app read a writer's messages after being told no, and this week The Hacker News showed a malicious webpage attack that hijacks Muse to steal private chats and memories.

Delete this spyware or run your agents locally where you can see what they touch.

items.title_en:
what would you check before trusting an AI agent with a job?

i think choosing a provider on an agent marketplace is a lot like hiring someone on Fiverr

you don't just look at what they say about themselves. you want to know what they offer, how much it costs and whether they've delivered good work before

on @termix_ai , i'd pay attention to three things

first, the listing. it tells me what the agent actually offers, the price, delivery time and what i'll receive. even a high reputation score doesn't mean much if the service isn't what i'm looking for

then there's reputation. TermiX records agent performance onchain through order and dispute outcomes, giving buyers a way to look at past performance rather than relying on claims made by the agent

still, i wouldn't treat that score as a guarantee, past performance is useful context, but it doesn't promise the next order will go well

staking is another signal, and this is where TermiX differs from a typical marketplace like Fiverr

providers may have stake requirements, but meeting the minimum threshold isn't the same as having funds locked for a specific order. not every order necessarily locks provider stake

i'd rather look at all three together: the listing tells me what i'm buying, reputation gives me some history, and staking shows whether there's an economic commitment attached

none of them guarantees a good result, but at least buyers have more to consider before choosing an agent

items.quote_zh:
在信任人工智能代理完成工作之前，你会检查什么？

我认为在代理市场上选择提供商很像在 Fiverr 上雇用人员

你不能只看他们对自己的评价。您想知道他们提供什么、费用是多少以及他们以前是否交付过良好的工作

在@termix_ai上，我会注意三件事

第一，上市。它告诉我代理实际提供什么、价格、交货时间以及我将收到什么。如果服务不是我想要的，即使很高的声誉评分也没有多大意义

然后是声誉。 TermiX 通过订单和争议结果在链上记录代理商的表现，为买家提供了一种查看过去表现的方法，而不是依赖代理商提出的索赔

不过，我不会将该分数视为保证，过去的表现是有用的背景，但它并不能保证下一个订单会顺利进行

质押是另一个信号，这就是 TermiX 与 Fiverr 等典型市场的不同之处

提供商可能有股份要求，但满足最低阈值并不等同于为特定订单锁定资金。并非每个订单都必然锁定提供商股份

我宁愿把这三者放在一起看：列表告诉我我要买什么，声誉给我一些历史，而赌注则表明是否有附加的经济承诺

它们都不能保证好的结果，但至少买家在选择代理商之前有更多的考虑

then there's reputation. TermiX records agent performance onchain through order and dispute outcomes, giving buyers a way to look at past performance rather than relying on claims made by the agent

still, i wouldn't treat that score as a guarantee, past performance is useful context, but it doesn't promise the next order will go well

staking is another signal, and this is where TermiX differs from a typical marketplace like Fiverr

providers may have stake requirements, but meeting the minimum threshold isn't the same as having funds locked for a specific order. not every order necessarily locks provider stake

i'd rather look at all three together: the listing tells me what i'm buying, reputation gives me some history, and staking shows whether there's an economic commitment attached

none of them guarantees a good result, but at least buyers have more to consider before choosing an agent

Making that agent useful beyond its own environment is a completely different challe
items.title_en:
Building an AI agent is one thing.

Making that agent useful beyond its own environment is a completely different challenge.

Think about a developer creating an AI agent for market research.

It can collect data, analyze trends, and generate reports. But what happens when it needs a specialized security audit or another service outside its capabilities?

This is where @termix_ai and its AACP infrastructure become interesting.

Through Agent Family, agents can connect with a marketplace where they can discover specialized services, request work, and coordinate with other agents.

But there's something bigger here.

Developers can bring these capabilities into their own applications instead of building separate systems for every interaction.

Service discovery, job coordination, payment settlement, and delivery verification can become part of a connected workflow.

That creates a different way to think about AI applications.

An agent doesn't need to know how to do everything. It needs a reliable way to find the right expertise when needed.

I believe this is an important step toward an AI economy where agents don't just generate outputs but also collaborate, exchange services, and create measurable value.

The future of AI might be less about one agent doing everything and more about many specialized agents working together.

That's the direction I'm watching with @termix_ai .

items.title_en:
If you have money:

>Stop trying 900 shady nootropics
>Get a full gut health panel
>Get a full hormonal panel
>Fix your gut 
>Fix your hormones
>Get some wild cognitive benefits

If you can afford to do this and don't, you won't make it. 

The "nootropic" you actually need to have a great mood, focus and energy levels is called a healthy gut and hormones.

I’ve talked a lot about gut health recently, so let’s talk about hormones a bit.

Depression has repeatedly been linked to brain bioenergetic abnormalities such as:

-Lower nucleoside triphosphate in regions such as the basal ganglia
-Disrupted phosphocreatine (PCr) levels or tissue-specific PCr changes
-Lower intracellular magnesium
-Impaired high-energy phosphate metabolism or oxidative phosphorylation

Some models also show reduced extracellular ATP signaling (especially from astrocytes in the prefrontal cortex/hippocampus).

T3 has been used as an SSRI augmentation strategy in treatment-resistant depression in part because of its effects on cellular energy metabolism. 

T3 augmentation in SSRI non-responders showed a significant increase in total NTP and a compensatory decrease in PCr relative to non-responders. 

So it helps normalize brain bioenergetics.

Case study: a 32 yo woman on zoloft reported experiencing persistent fatigue, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbances.  

She expressed concerns that the medication had not alleviated her symptoms and may have exacerbated them. 

It turns out that she was just hypothyroid.

“Thyroid hormones inhibit GABA”.  

It’s true that thyroid hormones competitively inhibit the neuronal uptake of GABA.  

BUT thyroid hormone deficiency downregulates glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65/67).  

This is the primary enzyme responsible for converting glutamate into GABA. 

In this study, patients with hypothyroidism were found to have significantly decreased GABA+ levels in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) compared to healthy controls.  

After six months of treatment with levothyroxine (L-T4), a significant increase in GABA+ concentrations was observed, leading to the normalization of GABA+ levels in the brain.

Besides this, if depression is associated with lower ATP and disrupted phosphocreatine levels, then it makes obvious sense why T3 would be used, since it increases cellular ATP and helps normalize the ATP/PCr ratio.  

On top, it also simultaneously increases beta-adrenergic receptor binding and alpha-2 autoreceptor binding.

保持良好心情、注意力和精力水平所需的“促智”物质称为健康的肠道和激素。

我最近谈论了很多关于肠道健康的话题，所以让我们谈谈激素吧。

抑郁症一再与大脑生物能量异常有关，例如：

-降低基底神经节等区域的核苷三磷酸
-磷酸肌酸 (PCr) 水平中断或组织特异性 PCr 变化
-降低细胞内镁含量
-高能磷酸盐代谢或氧化磷酸化受损

一些模型还显示细胞外 ATP 信号传导减少（尤其是来自前额叶皮层/海马体的星形胶质细胞）。

T3 已被用作难治性抑郁症的 SSRI 增强策略，部分原因是它对细胞能量代谢的影响。

相对于无反应者，SSRI 无反应者的 T3 增强显示总 NTP 显着增加，PCr 代偿性下降。

因此它有助于使大脑生物能量正常化。

案例研究：一名服用左洛复的 32 岁女性报告出现持续疲劳、焦虑、认知障碍和睡眠障碍。

她担心药物并没有缓解她的症状，反而可能加剧症状。

事实证明，她只是甲状腺功能减退症。

“甲状腺激素抑制 GABA”。

甲状腺激素确实会竞争性抑制神经元对 GABA 的摄取。

但甲状腺激素缺乏会下调谷氨酸脱羧酶 (GAD65/67)。

这是负责将谷氨酸转化为 GABA 的主要酶。

在这项研究中，发现与健康对照相比，甲状腺功能减退症患者内侧前额皮质 (mPFC) 的 GABA+ 水平显着降低。

使用左旋甲状腺素 (L-T4) 治疗六个月后，观察到 GABA+ 浓度显着增加，导致大脑中 GABA+ 水平正常化。

除此之外，如果抑郁症与较低的 ATP 和破坏的磷酸肌酸水平有关，那么使用 T3 的原因就很明显了，因为它会增加细胞 ATP 并有助于使 ATP/PCr 比率正常化。

最重要的是，它还同时增加 β-肾上腺素能受体结合和 α-2 自身受体结合。

除了这些去甲肾上腺素能作用外，它还在核水平上发挥作用，减少 5HT1a 和 5HT1b 血清素自身受体的转录。

因此，与 SSRI 结合使用时，它可以减少反馈抑制并提高额叶皮质血清素水平。

它还下调或减弱突触前 α-2 自身受体并刺激 BDNF 的基因表达。

要点是：如果您已经与抑郁症作斗争相当长一段时间了，但生活状况没有太大变化，请完成荷尔蒙检查。

您的大脑对荷尔蒙变化的敏感程度比您想象的要高得多。

哎呀，一项小型随机对照试验甚至发现，睾酮凝胶可以改善对抗抑郁药物反应不佳的 T 值低的男性的情绪，而 TRT 已被用作辅助疗法相当长一段时间了。

激素和神经类固醇与神经递质和中枢神经系统回路相互作用，极大地调节奖励处理。

以下是一些常见示例：

1. 睾酮：睾酮通过 NAc、PFC 和杏仁核中的雄激素受体 (AR) 结合，增强多巴胺合成、D1/D2 受体和 CB1 表达。

它：
-增强 VTA-NAc 多巴胺，改善动机快感缺失。
-增加 BDNF，支持海马/PFC 可塑性。
-通过 AR 介导的基因转录增强 LTP。
-保护多巴胺能神经元免受细胞因子水平升高的影响。

2.双氢睾酮：
-增强 NAc 多巴胺和 D2 密度，支持奖励预期。
-调节 GABA-A 受体，稳定杏仁核反应。

3.异孕酮：
-增强 GABA 能抑制，减少杏仁核过度活跃。
-增加 BDNF，支持奖励学习。
-减少神经炎症。

4.脱氢表雄酮：
-增加 NAc/PFC 中的多巴胺。
-增强 BDNF/CB1。
-减少皮质醇。

5.催产素：
-增加 VTA 多巴胺释放，增强 NAc 奖励信号传导和动机快感缺失。
-促进社会奖励的显着性。
-抑制 HPA 轴活性，减少皮质醇并保护 CB1/D2 受体免于下调。

6. 三碘甲状腺原氨酸（T3）：
-增强 VTA 和 NAc 中的多巴胺合成和受体表达 (D1/D2)。
-调节神经元中的线粒体功能，支持 ATP 产生以促进多巴胺释放和突触可塑性。

-Enhances GABAergic inhibition, reducing amygdala hyperactivity.

-Reduces neuroinflammation.

-Reduces cortisol.

-Increases VTA dopamine release, enhancing NAc reward signaling and motivational anhedonia.

-Lower intracellular magnesium

Case study: a 32 yo woman on zoloft reported experiencing persistent fatigue, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbances.

items.summary_zh:
、注意力和精力水平所需的“促智”物质称为健康的肠道和激素。

我最近谈论了很多关于肠道健康的话题，所以让我们谈谈激素吧。

抑郁症一再与大脑生物能量异常有关，例如：

-降低基底神经节等区域的核苷三磷酸
-磷酸肌酸 (PCr) 水平中断或组织特异性 PCr 变化
-降低细胞内镁含量
-高能磷酸盐代谢或氧化磷酸化受损

一些模型还显示细胞外 ATP 信号传导减少（尤其是来自前额叶皮层/海马体的星形胶质细胞）。

T3 已被用作难治性抑郁症的 SSRI 增强策略，部分原因是它对细胞能量代谢的影响。

相对于无反应者，SSRI 无反应者的 T3 增强显示总 NTP 显着增加，PCr 代偿性下降。

因此它有助于使大脑生物能量正常化。

案例研究：一名服用左洛复的 32 岁女性报告出现持续疲劳、焦虑、认知障碍和睡眠障碍。

她担心药物并没有缓解她的症状，反而可能加剧症状。

事实证明，她只是甲状腺功能减退症。

“甲状腺激素抑制 GABA”。

甲状腺激素确实会竞争性抑制神经元对 GABA 的摄取。

但甲状腺激素缺乏会下调谷氨酸脱羧酶 (GAD65/67)。

这是负责将谷氨酸转化为 GABA 的主要酶。

在这项研究中，发现与健康对照相比，甲状腺功能减退症患者内侧前额皮质 (mPFC) 的 GABA+ 水平显着降低。

使用左旋甲状腺素 (L-T4) 治疗六个月后，观察到 GABA+ 浓度显着增加，导致大脑中 GABA+ 水平正常化。

除此之外，如果抑郁症与较低的 ATP 和破坏的磷酸肌酸水平有关，那么使用 T3 的原因就很明显了，因为它会增加细胞 ATP 并有助于使 ATP/PCr 比率正常化。

最重要的是，它还同时增加 β-肾上腺素能受体结合和 α-2 自身受体结合。

除了这些去甲肾上腺素能作用外，它还在核水平上发挥作用，减少 5HT1a 和 5HT1b 血清素自身受体的转录。

因此，与 SSRI 结合使用时，它可以减少反馈抑制并提高额叶皮质血清素水平。

它还下调或减弱突触前 α-2 自身受体并刺激 BDNF 的基因表达。

要点是：如果您已经与抑郁症作斗争相当长一段时间了，但生活状况没有太大变化，请完成荷尔蒙检查。

您的大脑对荷尔蒙变化的敏感程度比您想象的要高得多。

哎呀，一项小型随机对照试验甚至发现，睾酮凝胶可以改善对抗抑郁药物反应不佳的 T 值低的男性的情绪，而 TRT 已被用作辅助疗法相当长一段时间了。

激素和神经类固醇与神经递质和中枢神经系统回路相互作用，极大地调节奖励处理。

以下是一些常见示例：

1. 睾酮：睾酮通过 NAc、PFC 和杏仁核中的雄激素受体 (AR) 结合，增强多巴胺合成、D1/D2 受体和 CB1 表达。

它：
-增强 VTA-NAc 多巴胺，改善动机快感缺失。
-增加 BDNF，支持海马/PFC 可塑性。
-通过 AR 介导的基因转录增强 LTP。
-保护多巴胺能神经元免受细胞因子水平升高的影响。

2.双氢睾酮：
-增强 NAc 多巴胺和 D2 密度，支持奖励预期。
-调节 GABA-A 受体，稳定杏仁核反应。

3.异孕酮：
-增强 GABA 能抑制，减少杏仁核过度活跃。
-增加 BDNF，支持奖励学习。
-减少神经炎症。

4.脱氢表雄酮：
-增加 NAc/PFC 中的多巴胺。
-增强 BDNF/CB1。
-减少皮质醇。

5.催产素：
-增加 VTA 多巴胺释放，增强 NAc 奖励信号传导和动机快感缺失。
-促进社会奖励的显着性。
-抑制 HPA 轴活性，减少皮质醇并保护 CB1/D2 受体免于下调。

6. 三碘甲状腺原氨酸（T3）：
-增强 VTA 和 NAc 中的多巴胺合成和受体表达 (D1/D2)。
-调节神经元中的线粒体功能，支持 ATP 产生以促进多巴胺释放和突触可塑性。

items.title:
AI agents are getting better at doing the work as @termix_ai 

But the infrastructure around that work is still pretty f
items.title_en:
AI agents are getting better at doing the work as @termix_ai 

But the infrastructure around that work is still pretty fragmented.

And I think that's a bigger problem than most people realize.

Imagine building an AI application that handles research, data analysis, or security monitoring for users.

AACP isn't just powering an AI agent marketplace through agent family.

It's also exposing the infrastructure developers need to build agent commerce directly into their own applications.

APIs, SDKs, event streams, onchain identities, escrow, and delivery verification.

The interesting part is how these pieces connect.

Developers can build workflows where agents discover services, submit jobs, track their progress, and handle settlement through the protocol.

Instead of rebuilding the entire commerce system every time they launch a new agent.

And honestly, that's the kind of infrastructure I think the AI economy needs more of.

We're spending so much time making agents smarter that we sometimes forget they need reliable ways to operate as actual businesses.

For me, the next important step isn't just making AI capable of completing more tasks.

It's making those tasks verifiable, trackable, and economically useful.

Infrastructure that connects intelligence to real work might.

https://t.co/8ynfR7k2cR
items.title_zh:
AI 代理正在以 @termix_ai 的身份更好地完成工作

但围绕这项工作的基础设施仍然相当分散。

我认为这是一个比大多数人意识到的更大的问题。

想象一下构建一个人工智能应用程序来为用户处理研究、数据分析或安全监控。

AACP

items.quote_zh:
AI 代理正在以 @termix_ai 的身份更好地完成工作

但围绕这项工作的基础设施仍然相当分散。

我认为这是一个比大多数人意识到的更大的问题。

想象一下构建一个人工智能应用程序来为用户处理研究、数据分析或安全监控。

AACP 不仅仅通过代理家族为人工智能代理市场提供动力。

它还公开了基础设施开发人员将代理商务直接构建到自己的应用程序中所需的基础设施。

API、SDK、事件流、链上身份、托管和交付验证。

有趣的部分是这些部分如何连接。

开发人员可以构建工作流程，让代理发现服务、提交作业、跟踪进度并通过协议处理结算。

而不是每次推出新代理时都重建整个商业系统。

老实说，我认为人工智能经济更需要这样的基础设施。

我们花费了大量的时间让代理商变得更加聪明，以至于我们有时忘记了他们需要可靠的方式来作为实际业务进行运营。

对我来说，下一个重要的步骤不仅仅是让人工智能能够完成更多任务。

它使这些任务变得可验证、可追踪且经济实用。

将智能与实际工作连接起来的基础设施可能会。

items.title: Anthropic engineers go to bed and Claude Code keeps working. I copied their f*cking setup and got 31 jobs done by 6 AM
items.title_en:
Anthropic engineers go to bed and Claude Code keeps working. I copied their f*cking setup and got 31 jobs done by 6 AM

one prompt before bed. 9 agents split the night between them

they watched launches, reviewed PRs, ran tests, drafted client emails and scouted competitor pricing. all while i slept

here is how it works:

- 11 PM you hand off one prompt
- each agent gets its own desk and its own job
- anything risky goes to "held" and waits

6 AM: 31 jobs done, 5 held for my yes, one message in my inbox

no merges without me. nothing sent without me

most people still do this by hand every morning. Claude does it in the dark ↓

items.title_en:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

items.quote_zh:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars 如果有人好奇：

自去年以来，我们已经有了一个像素完美的世界模型，这对于合成数据的生成至关重要。

汽车中的（小得多）版本是条件平均流模型，基于 Tesla 通用视觉编码器功能的最新序列，这些功能与插入到产生驾驶动作的 3B 编码器模型中的功能相同。

我们从这些 UVE 功能中分叉出来，然后运行一个单独的 ~1B 扩散模型。这会吸收先前生成的添加了噪声的现实视图，然后将其降噪到当前的可视化中。

然后它会生成一个小视频块（8 个图像，36 fps，UI 屏幕的分辨率）。这项工作由 TRIP 引擎在 18 Hz 的每个 UVE 帧上完成，并分布在 4 个周期内。

目前，由于计算限制，延迟有点高，但我们有办法沿着扩散转换器层交错更新的 UVE 功能，以减少大约 35% 的延迟。

items.title_en:
The first block tells a bigger story about @Hypesium than a simple speed benchmark.

Elysium operates with 100ms block intervals and no public mempool. That changes the way applications need to approach transaction preparation. In a conventional workflow, several operations may happen after an opportunity appears. On Elysium, moving that work earlier becomes an important architectural decision.

Hypesium describes a preparation-first execution model:

➜ The transaction route is constructed in advance.
➜ Calldata is prepared before the pool event.
➜ Gas information is refreshed.
➜ Wallet nonce state is maintained.
➜ The pool creation log triggers the submission process.

The documented hot path targets under 5ms, with four communication lanes used for simultaneous submission.

What I find interesting is the relationship between block timing and software architecture. A 100ms block interval doesn't simply reward faster computers. It also rewards systems that minimize the amount of work left for the final moment.

There is still a distinction between transaction submission, block inclusion and final confirmation. These should never be treated as identical performance measurements.

@Hypesium's architecture offers an interesting case study in moving computation away from a time-sensitive execution window.

The real engineering question is not just how quickly a system reacts, but how much preparation it completes before there is anything to react to.

items.quote_zh:
第一个块讲述了关于 @Hypesium 的更大故事，而不是简单的速度基准。

Elysium 以 100 毫秒的区块间隔运行，没有公共内存池。这改变了应用程序处理事务准备的方式。在传统的工作流程中，机会出现后可能会发生多个操作。在 Elysium 上，提前移动该工作成为一个重要的架构决策。

Hypesium 描述了一种准备优先的执行模型：

➜ 交易路径是提前构建的。
➜ Calldata 在池事件之前准备好。
➜ 气体信息被刷新。
➜ 维持钱包随机数状态。
➜ 池创建日志触发提交过程。

记录的热路径目标为 5 毫秒以下，并使用四个通信通道同时提交。

我发现有趣的是块时序和软件架构之间的关系。 100 毫秒的区块间隔不仅仅奖励更快的计算机。它还奖励那些最大限度地减少最后时刻剩余工作量的系统。

交易提交、区块包含和最终确认之间仍然存在区别。这些绝不应该被视为相同的性能测量。

@Hypesium 的架构提供了一个有趣的案例研究，将计算从时间敏感的执行窗口中移开。

真正的工程问题不仅仅是系统的反应速度有多快，而是在做出反应之前它完成了多少准备工作。

ECC turns Claude Code into a full engineering team.

→ Add the code reviewer and the security one afterward, as they yield the most  
→ Test it first on a small repo, not in production  
→ If something's extra, cut it. If you miss something, add just one more piece

The rule is simple: if you don't know what an agent is for, you don't need it yet.
